API Reference Guide

Packet service management

This section describes some of the packet service management tasks that you can perform using Navigator MC REST API.

  • The IFD API version numbers (for example, “v6” in “ifd.v6.resourceTypes”) that appear in this chapter do not necessarily reflect the IFD API version numbers associated with this current Navigator MC release. They are provided only as an example. For a list of supported releases and their related version numbers, see the "Versioning" section in the Navigator MC REST API overview chapter.

  • To allow service provisioning on multi-domain (mix of G.8032 & MPLS) transport, GCS property allowMultiDomainPaths needs to set as true. By default, the value is false. Refer API calls for updating GCS property

  • Currently, multi-domain paths are applicable only for 2-endpoint E-Line services.

GCS Properties for Concurrency in modification of L2 entities

GCS Property Name Description

enableConcurrentModification

  • This property is used to enable concurrency in the modification of L2 entities

Possible values are: true, false
The default value is: true

  • For Legacy implementation, GCS property enableConcurrentModification needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

concurrentModificationBatchSize

  • This property is used to set the size of the concurrent modification batch of L2 entities.

Possible values are: An integer greater than 1
The default value is: 10

  • This property would only be applicable if enableConcurrentModification is set as true.

  • For Legacy implementation, GCS property enableConcurrentModification needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

GCS Properties for Service Provisioning Over G.8032 ring transport

GCS Property Name Description

l2ServiceCreateSecureRplNode

  • By Default, GCS property l2ServiceCreateSecureRplNode is set as true. L2 service creation will secure the Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) node i.e. Navigator MC will get the latest Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) information and perform two step provisioning. In the first step, provisioning will happen on Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) nodes followed by provisioning on the remaining nodes.

  • For Legacy implementation, where service provisioning will happen in a single step without knowledge of Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) information, GCS property l2ServiceCreateSecureRplNode needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

l2ServiceDeleteSecureRplNode

  • By Default, GCS property l2ServiceDeleteSecureRplNode is set as true. L2 service deletion will secure the Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) node i.e. Navigator MC will get the latest Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) information and perform two step de-provisioning. In the first step, de-provisioning will happen on non Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) nodes followed by de-provisioning on Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) nodes.

  • For Legacy implementation, where service de-provisioning will happen in a single step without knowledge of Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) information, GCS property l2ServiceDeleteSecureRplNode needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

l2ServiceCreateBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB

  • By Default, the GCS property l2ServiceCreateBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB is set as true. L2 service creation will be blocked when all ring nodes have Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) i.e. OCB or CCB is configured on each node of the ring.

  • For Legacy implementation, where service is provisioned even if Operational Channel Block(OCB) or Configured Channel Block(CCB) is configured on each node of the ring, GCS property l2ServiceCreateBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

l2ServiceDeleteBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB

  • By Default, the GCS property l2ServiceDeleteBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB is set as true. L2 service deletion will be blocked when all ring nodes have Operational Channel Block(OCB)/Configured Channel Block(CCB) i.e. OCB or CCB is configured on each node of the ring.

  • For Legacy implementation, where service will de-provision even if Operational Channel Block(OCB) or Configured Channel Block(CCB) is configured on each node of the ring, GCS property l2ServiceDeleteBlockAllNodesOCBorCCB needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

GCS Properties for Service Provisioning with Highest Class Element to Smallest Vid

This section is applicable for 6500 and 8x devices only.

GCS Property Name Description

l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid

  • By Default, GCS property l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid is set as false i.e legacy implementation would be used for class element assignment.

  • To assign highest class-element to smallest VID or smallest inner VID (pure dual-tag), GCS property l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid needs to be set as true. For Ranged+Untagged Service, Untagged VID would have the highest class element if GCS property l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid is set as true. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

To configure PW-Handoff service with tagged cfm configuration on 6500 and 8x device, GCS property l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid must be set as true.

l2EditBlockTrafficImpactedScenario

  • By Default, GCS property l2EditBlockTrafficImpactedScenario is set as true. During modification, if l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid is set as true and smallest VID needs to be removed to correct class-element assignment i.e. traffic would be impacted, then modification operation would be blocked. If user still wants to proceed with modification knowingly that traffic would be impacted, GCS property l2EditBlockTrafficImpactedScenario needs to be set as false. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

GCS Properties to Enable Targeted Sync for Unprotected Eline Over Pure MPLS

This section is applicable for 6500, 6x and 10x devices only.

GCS Property Name Description

enableTargetSyncForUnprotectedElinePureMPLS

  • By Default, GCS property enableTargetSyncForUnprotectedElinePureMPLS is set as false i.e legacy implementation/Inventory Sync would be used for all service types on all underlying topologies.

  • To enable Target/Selective Sync for L2 Service Provisioning, Modification and Deletion for Unprotected Eline Over Pure MPLS, GCS property enableTargetSyncForUnprotectedElinePureMPLS needs to be set as true. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

The enableTargetSyncForUnprotectedElinePureMPLS is only applicable for L2 Service over Pure MPLS( no spur/G.8032). Currently only Seamless BGP and RSVP-TE is supported as underlying transport. Inventory sync would be stopped if enableTargetSyncForUnprotectedElinePureMPLS is set as True.

GCS Property to allow configuring CFM-based VLLI for multipoint EVPL services

GCS Property Name Description

allowMultipointEvplVlli

  • By Default, GCS property allowMultipointEvplVlli is set as false i.e. CFM-based VLLI configuration is allowed only for multipoint EPL services.

  • To allow CFM-based VLLI configuration for multipoint EVPL services during Provisioning, Modification and Add endpoint flows, GCS property allowMultipointEvplVlli needs to be set as true. Refer to API calls for updating GCS property

Basic packet-related API calls

This section describes the basic API calls used to view the existing packet service inventory managed by Navigator MC:

  • Retrieve all discovered / planned Ethernet services including the related TPEs

  • Retrieve a discovered / planned Ethernet service by FRE ID, including the related TPEs

  • Retrieve a discovered / planned Ethernet service by FRE ID

  • Retrieve all discovered / planned Ethernet services for a specific network construct

  • Retrieve a discovered / planned Ethernet service by a specific name

  • Retrieve L2 service intent façade product ID

  • Retrieve MC-LAG service endpoints

  • Retrieve details for a service using MC-LAG endpoints or an ICL

  • Retrieve configuration resources

  • Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management

Retrieve all discovered / planned Ethernet services including the related TPEs

To retrieve all Ethernet services (including the related TPEs), use the Services Inventory (FREs) API.

You can also use this API call for service discovery and inventory of an E-LAN service with one of the following endpoints: CES SAOS 6.x, 8700 SAOS 8.x, or 6500-S Packet Fabric.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "layerRate" as ETHERNET and include TPEs.

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/fres?layerRate=ETHERNET&type=service&include=tpes

Retrieve an E-Tree single-root service

This API call applies to service discovery and inventory of an E-Tree single-root service over Static MPLS transport only with:

  • Multi-segment pseudowire (MS-PW) (6.x (as leaf), 8700 (as leaf or root), 6500 Packet Fabric (as leaf or root)

  • Single-segment pseudowire (SS-PW) (6.x (as leaf), 8700 (as leaf or root), 6500 Packet Fabric (as leaf or root)

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/fres/<FRE_ID>

Specify the FRE_ID of the E-Tree service.

Retrieve an E-Tree dual-root service

This API call applies to service discovery and inventory of an E-Tree dual-root (same node) service over Static MPLS (SS-PW/MS-PW) (6.x (as leaf), 8700 (as leaf or root), 6500 Packet Fabric (as leaf or root).

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/fres/<FRE_ID>

Retrieve details for a service using MC-LAG endpoints or an ICL

You can use the REST API to retrieve details about an E-Line service that includes MC-LAG endpoints. The same call can be used to retrieve information about the Inter-chassis Link (ICL) that supports an MC-LAG.

Sample request:

The following request retrieves details for a specified service:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/fres/<FRE_ID>

For <FRE_ID>, specify the FRE_ID of the service (either an E-Line service or an ICL).

Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve a TPE / FRE including CFT, CFM attributes

  • Retrieve an FRE E-Access service

  • Retrieve an FRE 3-point service

To perform these actions, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

This section describes the API calls to retrieve, provision, and delete E-Line services:

Assign a node role (Prerequisite for E-Line provisioning in seamless MPLS network)

Before you create an E-Line services in a Dynamic MPLS network, perform the following four-step process to designate the L2 switch fabric equipment group(s) in each of the 6500 nodes or a 39xx NE with a 'network role' of either Network Interface Device (NID), Access Node (AN), or Aggregation Node (AGN).

After a device has been assigned a node role, the routing engine becomes aware of where the boundaries of MPLS, RSVP-TE, and QinQ are. This is particularly important for the tunnel auto-create function whereby the AGN nodes need to be identified.

For 6500 NEs, the role assignment is against the L2 switch fabric equipment group, not against a node. This is due to the case where a node such as a 6500 TIDc can have more than one L2 switch fabric (for example, one shelf is an AN and another is an AGN).

You can use the Market REST API to assign a node role on a device for the first three steps in the process and the Network element (constructs) REST API for the fourth and final step in the process.

Perform the following four steps in the process:

  • Retrieve an MPLSOperationContainer resource and select one of the resource IDs

  • Execute a custom operation: the node role assignment on a device

  • Retrieve the result to confirm the operation

  • Retrieve the network constructs

  1. Retrieve an MPLSOperationContainer resource and select one of the resource IDs.

    For example, in the following sample, the resource ID, RID is 5c6cfe16-36a7-43f6-9b9c-46446486f463.

    Sample request

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

    Retrieve an MPLS Operation Container static resource and specify it in the GET call.

  1. Execute a custom operation: the node role assignment on a device.

    Sample request

    POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

    Specify the required Node role.

    Also, for 6500 devices, specify the shelf, and eqptGrp. For SAOS 6x/8700 devices, the shelf and eqptGrp attributes are not applicable.

    {
	"interface": "assignEquipmentGroupRole",
	"inputs": {
		"ncID": "c982c0a8-777e-3104-876c-98716d851215",
		"l2NodeRole": "AN",
		"shelf": "1",
		"eqptGrp": "41"
	}
}

{

Provision unprotected E-Line EVPL over MPLS transport with/without QinQ spurs

To provision an E-Line EVPL service over MPLS transport between 5160 & 3931 nodes with a constraint to include a specific node in the route and fixed CoS mapping with pBit of 5, use the Market API.

CVID can be given as range or single value ("200-300,545,689,1100-2111") using outerVlanIDRange. Either outervlanIdRange or outerVlanId can be used in provisioning and modification of E-Line service.
The API call used to create a service can include the following constraints:

  • constraints.transport.directionality, to constrain the service to unidirectional or bidirectional MPLS tunnels

  • constraints.transport.signal to constrain the service to use dynamic or static MPLS tunnels

If you omit these constraints, Navigator MC’s Path Computation Engine (PCE) will choose a best-effort path that can either be based on unidirectional or bi-directional LSP.

Sample request

POST {{Navigator MC Server}}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

{

                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                                878
                                        ]
                                    },

                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                                        "ingressCosPbit": 5
                                    },
                                    "location": {
                                        "port": "9"
                                    }
                                        }
                                    ]
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {

                    "role": "Z_UNI",

                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                                878
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                                        "ingressCosPbit": 5
                                    },
                                       "location": {
                                            "port": "4"
                                         }
                                        }
                                    ]
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ],
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "linearOnly":false

      "includeRouteObjects": [
          {
              "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
              "value": ["5150_0025"],
              "constraintType": "HARD"
          }
      ]
    }

Provision unprotected E-Line EVPL over mix of G.8032 and MPLS transport with/without QinQ spurs

To provision an E-Line EVPL service over mix of G.8032 rings and MPLS transport with constraints to include a specific node, G.8032 ring and tunnel in the route, use the Market API.

CVID can be given as range or single value ("200-300,545,689,1100-2111") using outerVlanIDRange. Either outervlanIdRange or outerVlanId can be used in provisioning and modification of E-Line service.
The API call used to create a service can include the following constraints:

Sample request

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

{

      "originator": "BP2"

    "interactive_mode": "true",

    "coreTransport": "Any",
	"allowQinQSpur": true,
	"transportProtection": "PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT",
    "constraints": {
      "transport": {
        "directionality": "bidirectional"
      },
      "routes": [
          {
          "protection": "unprotected",

            "A",
            "Z"

          "includeRouteObjects": [

                "locations": [

                "constraintType": "HARD"
            },
            {
                "locations": [
                    {
                        "lspName": "LSP-2123-87s",
                        "nodeName": "65SD_2123"
                    }
                ],
                "objectType": "LSP_NAME",
                "constraintType": "HARD"
            },
            {
                "locations": [
                    {
                        "nodeName": "65SD_2123",
                        "g8032RingName": "left_major_vr"
                    }
                ],
                "objectType": "G8032_RING_NAME",
                "constraintType": "HARD"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "coreSvid": 555,
    "endpoints": [
      {
        "settings": {
          "role": "A_ENNI",
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {

Provision an unprotected E-Line EVPL service over Linear QinQ

To provision an E-Line EVPL service over Linear transport between 5160 & 3931 nodes with a constraint to include a specific route, scheduled deployment, and fixed CoS mapping with pBit of 5, use the Market API.

The API call used to create a service can include the following constraints:

  • constraints.transport.directionality, to constrain the service to unidirectional or bidirectional MPLS tunnels

  • constraints.transport.signal to constrain the service to use dynamic or static MPLS tunnels

If you omit these constraints, Navigator MC’s Path Computation Engine (PCE) will choose a best-effort path that can either be based on unidirectional or bi-directional LSP.

Core SVID can be explicitly provided instead of using auto calculated core SVID by system.

  • properties.coreSvid, to provide a valid core SVID value in range [1-4094]

If there is no path satisfying the provided core SVID then error message will contain the FIRST and NEXT available vid’s to be used as core SVID.

Provision unprotected E-Line services over MPLS transport with MS-PW excluding QinQ spurs

To provision E-Line services, use the Market API.

The API call used to create a service can include the following constraints:

  • constraints.transport.directionality, to constrain the service to unidirectional or bidirectional MPLS tunnels

  • constraints.transport.signal to constrain the service to use dynamic or static MPLS tunnels

If you omit these constraints, Navigator MC’s Path Computation Engine (PCE) will choose a best-effort path that can either be based on unidirectional or bi-directional LSP.

Sample request

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the attributes in the properties section as in the following suggestions:

  • "allowQinQSpur": false

  • "protectedPseudowire": false

  • "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT"

          "constraintType": "HARD",

    "oamEnabled": false,
    "endpoints": [

        "settings": {
          "node": "87_4333n6",
          "role": "A_UNI",
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {
                    "outerVlanId": [
                      3415
                    ]
                  },
                  "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                  "location": {
                      "slot": "1",
                      "port": "7"
                   },

                  "ingressCosSetting": {
                    "ingressCosPolicy": "L2PcpCos"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      },

          "details": [

                {
                  "filter": {

                  },

Provision an E-LINE service over a unidirectional MPLS tunnel

Navigator MC supports the provisioning of E-Line services over unidirectional tunnels in much the same way they are provisioned over bi-directional tunnels.

Navigator MC supports dynamic MPLS unidirectional tunnels using the following devices as LER or LSRs:

  • 6500-T release 13.0 both in TIDc and non-TIDc configurations

  • 6500 PTS release 13.0 in non-TIDc configuration

  • 5170, when MPLS capable

This topic provides examples of provisioning an E-Line service over a unidirectional tunnel. Key elements of the API call that constrain the service to transport over a unidirectional tunnel are these properties:

  • constraints.transport.directionality

    • bidirectional

    • unidirectional

  • constraints.transport.signal

    • Static

    • Dynamic

To provision E-Line services, use the Market API.

This topic includes two sections:

  • Constrain tunnel directionality when provisioning an E-Line service

  • Constrain directionality and include/exclude specific LSPs

Constrain tunnel directionality when provisioning an E-Line service

Below is an example of the API calls used to create an E-Line service that is explicitly constrained to use a unidirectional tunnel, but is not constrained to include or exclude any specific objects.

Create the facade:

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "allowQinQSpur": false,
        "name": "jmEVPL",
        "protectedPseudowire": false,
        "transportProtection": "UNPROTECTED_ONLY",
        "linearOnly": false,
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "oamEnabled": false,
        "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "SIM1",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "1",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41",
                                        "slot": "2",
                                        "port": "20"
                                    },
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            781
                                        ]
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "SIM2",
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "1",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41",
                                        "slot": "1",
                                        "port": "20"
                                    },
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            781
                                        ]
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ],
        "constraints": {
            "transport": {
                "directionality": "unidirectional",
                "signal": "Dynamic"
            }
        }
    }
}
Constrain directionality and include/exclude specific LSPs

You can also use the Constraints block of the API call to require specific LSPs to be included in the service path, and specify those that should be included in each direction. The following call constrains the service path:

  • to use unidirectional, unprotected dynamic tunnels

  • to strictly include the node SIM2 and the LSP sim1sim2 on the A to Z path

  • to strictly use the LSP sim2sim1 on the Z to A path.

Create the facade:

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "allowQinQSpur": false,
        "name": "jmEVPL",
        "protectedPseudowire": false,
        "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_ONLY",
        "linearOnly": false,
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "oamEnabled": false,
        "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "SIM1",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "1",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41",
                                        "slot": "2",
                                        "port": "20"
                                    },
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            781
                                        ]
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "SIM2",
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "1",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41",
                                        "slot": "1",
                                        "port": "20"
                                    },
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            781
                                        ]
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ],
        "constraints": {
            "transport": {
                "directionality": "unidirectional",
                "signal": "Dynamic"
            },
            "routes": [{
                    "protection": "UNPROTECTED",
                    "direction": ["A", "Z"],
                    "includeRouteObjects": [{
                            "constraintType": "HARD",
                            "locations": [{
                                    "nodeName": "SIM2",
                                    "lspName": "sim1sim2"
                                }
                            ],
                            "objectType": "LSP_NAME"
                        }
                    ]
                }, {
                    "protection": "UNPROTECTED",
                    "direction": ["Z", "A"],
                    "includeRouteObjects": [{
                            "constraintType": "HARD",
                            "locations": [{
                                    "nodeName": "SIM1",
                                    "lspName": "sim2sim1"

                                }
                            ],
                            "objectType": "NODE_NAME"
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}

Provision control frame tunneling on EPL and EVPL

To provision the control frame tunneling option on EPL or EVPL, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the following attribute:

  • "controlFrameTunneling": "enabled"

{
  "productId": "{{L2T_PRODUCT_ID}}",
  "label": "L2 EVPL Layer Termination A",
  "discovered": false,
  "properties":
    {
        "layerRate": "ETHERNET",
        "evcPortType": "MAPPED",
        "interfaceType": "UNI",
        "signalIndex": {
            "mappingTable": [
                { "label": "402" }
            ]
        },
        "ingressCosSetting": {
            "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
            "ingressCosPbit": 5
        },
        "ingressPolicer": {
            "cir": 1000,
            "eir": 500,
            "cbs": 200,
            "ebs": 100
        },
        "controlFrameTunneling": "enabled"
}

Sample response

No textual response except the HTTP status code

To retrieve information, use the NSI getTPE/getFRE REST API (see Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management. )

Provision an E-Line service with custom Class of Service (CoS) mapping

You can use the Navigator MC API to specify a customized CoS setting at each endpoint of a service during service provisioning.

You can include the same parameters when adding an endpoint to an E-LAN service to configure the new endpoint to use a customized CoS mapping.

You might want to use a customized CoS mapping to rearrange adjacent service provider CoS, or to merge together existing CoS mappings. (For example, on a SAOS 6x platform a PBit of 0 and DEI of 0 are transparently mapped to an internal CoS of 0 and color of 0 in the default map. You might want to use a customized mapping to group both PBit 0 and PBit 1, and map them to an internal CoS of 1)

The CoS maps you refer to using this API call must have already been created on the device.

Use the Market API to provision a service with a custom CoS mapping.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Note that in the following API calls:

  • L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID is a product ID to create Layer-2 Service in Facade.

  • SVC_RSC_ID is the Facade resource ID of the Layer-2 service.

Note in particular the following CoS parameters for the service endpoints the sample call provided below:

"ingressCosSetting": { "ingressCosPolicy": "L2PcpCos"

"ingressCosSetting": { "ingressCosPolicy": "custom", "ingressCosMapName": "CustomCosMap"

Sample request:

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serverTrailList": [],
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "name": "EVPLCustomCoS",
                "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "customerName": "DefaultCustomerName",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "3938_0032",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            781
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "L2PcpCos"
                                    },
                                    "location": {
                                    	"port": "1"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "5142_0049",

                    "details": [

                                    },
                                    "location": {

                        }
                    ]

}

Provision a three-point E-Line service with pseudowire protection

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to provision an E-Line service with Pseudowire protection (for both single-segment and multi-segment Pseudowires), and select one or more specific LSP tunnels to carry the A-Z, A-Z', and Z-Z' routes.

This capability is also supported in cases where the LSP path includes linear Q-in-Q spurs.

Note: The example below shows the configuration of a three-point protected E-Line service; but with minor variations the same API call can be used to provision a conventional two-point E-Line service instead.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

As part of the call, you must specify the LSP Tunnel Selection block, extracted below:

"primaryPathConstraints": {
  "includeRouteObjects": [
    {
      "constraintType": "HARD",
      "value": [
        "87_5775n4",
        "IFDAutomation2"
      ],
      "objectType": "LSP_NAME"
    }
  ]
},

Provision a V-shaped three-point E-Line (with PW-based VLLI) service with pseudowire protection

In a V-shaped Dual-homed E-Line (with PW-based VLLI) service:

  1. PW-based VLLI will be configured at Z-end only.

  2. No Pseudowire would be configured between Z and Z' ends.

  3. Re-route of primary pseudowire (PW) would intermittently disable VLLI for all the services on Z-end port.

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to provision a V-shaped three-point E-Line (with PW-based VLLI) service with pseudowire protection (for both single-segment and multi-segment Pseudowires), and select one or more specific LSP tunnels to carry the A-Z, and A-Z' routes.

Note: The example below shows the configuration of a V-shaped Dual-homed E-Line (with PW-based VLLI) service.

Provision per-EVC policing option

To provision the per-EVC policing option, use Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the following attributes:

  • "cir"

  • "eir"

  • "cbs"

  • "ebs"

{
  "productId": "{{L2T_PRODUCT_ID}}",
  "label": "L2 EVPL Layer Termination A",
  "discovered": false,
  "properties":
    {
        "layerRate": "ETHERNET",
        "evcPortType": "MAPPED",
        "interfaceType": "UNI",
        "signalIndex": {
            "mappingTable": [
                { "label": "402" }
            ]
        },
        "ingressCosSetting": {
            "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
            "ingressCosPbit": 5
        },
        "ingressPolicer": {
            "cir": 1000,
            "eir": 500,
            "cbs": 200,
            "ebs": 100
        },
        "controlFrameTunneling": "enabled"
}

Sample response:

There is no textual response except the HTTP status code

To retrieve information, use the NSI getTPE/getFRE REST API (see Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management.)

Provision constraints — transport protection

To provision the transport protection constraint, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

The "transportProtection" attribute specifies the underlying transport for the service. Values related to the transportProtection attribute follow.

transportProtection value Description

PROTECTED_ONLY

Find a path which uses only protected transport.

UNPROTECTED_ONLY

Find a path which uses only unprotected transport.

PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT

Find a path which gives priority to protected transport but, if that’s not possible, allows other transport types to be used.

UNPROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT

Find a path which gives priority to unprotected transport but, if that’s not possible, allows other transport types to be used.

<not specified>

Find a path based on the least number of hops without giving priority to any transport (protected/unprotected).
The attribute "linearOnly": true constrains the service to be linear only, regardless of the transportProtection. 
{

Create a packet service with Control Frame Tunneling (CFT)

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to provision a packet service that uses a custom Layer 2 Control Frame Tunneling (L2CFT) map, thereby allowing you to control which protocols are allowed to tunnel through each service. You can specify a custom L2CFT map on each endpoint of a packet service.

You can also use the API to add a CFT-enabled endpoint with a particular CFT profile name to an existing service.

This assumes that the custom L2CFT maps have previously been created on the device on which the endpoint resides. If you add a new L2CFT map to an NE you can manually resynchronize Navigator MC and the node to immediately update Navigator MC’s view of the available L2CFT maps on a given NE.

The API call below shows a service being provisioned that has CFT enabled on one endpoint, and CFT disabled on the other endpoint.

POST NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample request:

        "name": "rm-cft",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n2",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            333
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                                        "ingressCosPbit": 3
                                    },
                                    "location": {
                                        "slot": "1",
                                        "port": "1"
                                    },
                                    "controlFrameTunneling": "enabled",
                                    "controlFrameTunnelingProfileName": "profile-name"
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n4",
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            333
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",

                                    },
                                    "location": {
                                        "slot": "1",
                                        "port": "1"

                                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled"

}

Provision service OAM configuration (802.1ag and Y.1731)

To provision service OAM configuration (802ag and Y.1731), use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the following attributes in the properties section:

  • "oamEnabled": true

  • (Optional) "ccmInterval": <CCM Interval value>

  • (Optional) "ccmPriority": <CCM Priority value between 0-7>

  • (Optional) "mdLevel": <MD Level value between 0-7>

  • (Optional) "maName": <MA Name in string format, same as CFM Service name, if not given, the service name is used>

  • (Optional) "maNameInteger": <MA Name in integer format between 0-65535>

Specify the following attributes in the settings sections of both the endpoints in the request body, for example:

  • "oamEnabled": true

  • "ccmTransmitEnabled": true

  • "dmmEnabled": true

  • "dmmInterval": "10sec"

  • "dmmPriority": 5

  • "slmEnabled": true

  • "slmInterval": "10sec"

Set the default DSCP CoS mapping

To set the default DSCP CoS, use the Market API.

The ingress class of service (CoS) policy is one parameter that the user needs to explicitly set — per endpoint — on the fiber of the network side, during service provisioning. The CoS mapping applies to the frame on the ingress device.

The following ingress CoS policies are supported: fixed, L2PcpCos, and L3DscpCos.

The following are samples of L3DscpCos.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the following attribute in the endpoint settings section of the request body:

  • "ingressCosSetting"

    • "ingressCosPolicy"

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serverTrailList": [],
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "name": "EVPL_Facade_postman",
                "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "customerName": "DefaultCustomerName",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n7",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [

Delete an E-Line service

This topic provides instructions on how to delete a service. You can also use this API call to delete any L2 service.

  1. Using the Services inventory (FREs) API, get the FRE_ID of the service that you want to delete.

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/nis/api/fres

  2. Using the Market API, get the ManagedServiceContainer resource ID:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ManagedServiceContainer

  3. Using the Market API, delete the service by invoking the operation of the resource using the following API call and inputs:

    POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/<ManagedServiceContainer RESOURCE_ID>/operations

{
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "managedOperation": "Delete",
      "freId": "<FRE_ID>"
    }
  },
  "interface": "manageService"
}

Delete an E-Line service by provisioning intent

You can also use this API call to delete an E-LAN service and an E-Tree service.

Considerations

  1. Best effort cleanup of configuration during undeploy/delete (failure in deletion of 1 NE or config will not prevent deletion of config on the rest of the NEs).

  2. If a service deployment has failed (it is in INCOMPLETE_DEPLOYMENT state), then trying delete will do the following:

    • Best effort cleanup of all devices will be attempted, including partial configs on NEs for which deployment failed.

    • All resources (facade, intent, expectations) will be deleted even if there are failures during undeploy.

  3. If service was deployed properly, attempting delete will do the following:

    • Best effort cleanup of all devices will be attempted.

    • If delete fails on a device then the resources (façade, intent, expectations) will NOT be deleted. The user will still see a Service in INCOMPLETE_UNDEPLOYMENT state.

To delete a provisioned E-Line or E-Access service, use the Market API.

Sample request

DELETE {{Navigator MC Server}}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the ID of the previously provisioned service as part of the URL.

https://<server>/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/58cae7f0-434c-40e2-b6e4-417108f47cc3

Sample response

No response body. HTTP status code 204

Modify BPO-IFD properties

Navigator MC uses a set of properties to customize some aspects of Navigator MC’s behavior. These properties can be modified using the REST API.

Viewing the list of current properties

To view the current set of BPO-IFD properties, use the Market API.

Issue a GET call with the following syntax:

BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.resourceTypes.IfdConfig

The response will resemble the following:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "58a5fc80-e348-46a1-aa65-c05d4bdbfe0a",
      "label": "ifd_properties",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.resourceTypes.IfdConfig",
      "productId": "58a5c8f2-42e1-418b-a83b-b546476197b2",
      "tenantId": "a8fe33bc-bb0e-4cb8-9371-5dca8ffe0ad2",
      "shared": false,
      "properties": {
        "configurationProperties": {
          "ifd.l2.managementVlans": {
            "default": "127",
            "value": "918"
          },
          "ifd.l0.setExplicitFrequency": {
            "default": "true",
            "value": "true"
          },
          "ifd.l2.truncateSubportName": {
            "default": "True",
            "value": "False"
          },
          "ifd.l2.maximumTransmissionUnit": {
            "default": "2000",
            "value": "2000"
          },
          "ifd.l2.statusTlv": {
            "default": "on",
            "value": "on"
          }
        }
      },
      "discovered": false,
      "differences": [],
      "desiredOrchState": "active",
      "orchState": "active",
      "reason": "",
      "tags": {},
      "providerData": {},
      "updatedAt": "2020-02-16T19:35:58.179Z",
      "createdAt": "2020-02-16T19:24:49.103Z",
      "autoClean": false
    }
  ],
  "total": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 1000
}

Note the Resource ID returned at the start of this response. This is the ID of the active IFD configuration.

Modifying properties

To modify a BPO-IFD property, issue an API call with the following syntax:

BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RESOURCE_ID}

where the RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID of the active IFD configuration, which you can obtain by viewing the current configuration as described above.

The body of the request must contain:

  • the name of the property you want to change, included as the key in the configurationProperties object

  • the value to which the property should be set, included as the "value" key of the named property

For example:

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.l0.setExplicitFrequency": {
        "value": "false"
      }
    }
  }
}
Specific properties affecting Navigator MC Packet service management

One of the BPO-IFD properties that can be modified in this way is the following property that governs the E-Line service types for which CFM-based VLLI can be enabled:

ifd.l2.elineEvplVlli

Normally, CFM-based VLLI can be enabled only for EPL E-Line services. To enable CFM-based VLLI for EVPL E-Line services as well, set this property to "true". For example:

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.l2.elineEvplVlli": {
        "value": "true"
      }
    }
  }
}

Status notifications for Layer 2 service creation, modification, and deletion using the API

Navigator MC generates status messages regarding its progress when creating, deleting, or modifying Packet services. If you subscribe to these Navigator MC messages using a web socket connection (Kafka Comet), you will receive status messages and can check that list to see the latest status of your request.

Below you can see the status messages that Navigator MC generates during service provisioning, creation, or deletion, and elements of those messages that indicate the operation’s success or failure.

Note 1: This feature applies to E-line services.

Note 2: Navigator MC supports E-Line service provisioning using the API that includes an instruction to automatically create any dynamic MPLS tunnels the service requires. This status notification capability does not yet support such automatic tunnel creation, so it is not yet possible to check the status of automatically created tunnels.

Note 3: For details related to status notification for tunnel creation, modification, and deletion, see Status notifications for tunnel creation, modification, and deletion using the API

This topic describes Navigator MC’s status messages in the following cases:

  • Service provisioning

  • Service modification

  • Service deletion

Service provisioning

When provisioning a new Layer 2 service, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to the market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" using Kafka Comet.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Facade Creation Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade"

  • Resource id is L2ServiceIntentFacade Id

  • Resource Orch State is "failed"

Facade Creation Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade"

  • Resource id is L2ServiceIntentFacade Id

  • Resource Orch State is "active"

Relationship Creation Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is RelationShipCreated

  • relationshipTypeId is "ifd.v6.relationshipTypes.FcHasFacade"

  • relationship.sourceId is "L2ServiceIntentFacade Id"

  • Resource Orch State is "failed"

Relationship Creation Success

  • The Kafka message event type is RelationShipCreated

  • relationshipTypeId is "ifd.v6.relationshipTypes.FcHasFacade"

  • relationship.sourceId is "L2ServiceIntentFacade Id"

  • Resource Orch State is "active"

Service Provisioning Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntent"

  • Resource id is L2ServiceIntent Id

  • lastOperationStatus is "failed"

Service Provisioning Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntent"

  • Resource id is L2ServiceIntent Id

  • Deployment State is "COMPLETE_FULLY_READY"

  • LifeCyclePhase is "ASSURING"
Service modification

When modifying an existing Layer 2 service, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" using Kafka Comet.

When you issue the API call for the Layer 2 service edit operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "ServiceEditOperation Id". Use that ID to identify a particular edit operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Service Edit Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is "ServiceEditOperation Id"

  • Interface is "Modify"

  • Operation State is "failed"

Service Edit Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is "ServiceEditOperation Id"

  • Interface is "Modify"

  • Operation State is "successful"
Service deletion

When deleting a Layer 2 service, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" via kafka comet.

This section describes Navigator MC’s status messages in the following cases:

  • Service deletion (using L2ServiceIntentId)

  • Service deletion (using ManagedServiceContainer)

Service deletion (using L2ServiceIntentId)

When you issue the API call for the service deletion operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "L2ServiceIntent Id". Use that ID to identify a particular deletion operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Service Deletion Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntent"

  • Resource Id is "L2ServiceIntent Id"

  • LastOperationStatus State is "failed"

Service Deletion Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntent"

  • Resource Id is "L2ServiceIntent Id"

  • deployment State is "UNDEPLOYED"

Service deletion (using ManagedServiceContainer)

When you issue the API call for the service deletion operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "ServiceDeleteOperation Id". Use that ID to identify a particular deletion operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Service Deletion Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is "ServiceDeleteOperation Id"

  • Interface is "manageService"

  • Operation State is "failed"

Service Deletion Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is "ServiceDeleteOperation Id"

  • Interface is "manageService"

  • Operation State is "successful"

Retrieve details for an E-Line service carried over G.8032 rings

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve information about an E-Line service that is being carried over G.8032 ring infrastructure.

This topic addresses two cases:

  • Retrieving details of an E-Line service carried exclusively over one or more G.8032 rings

  • Retrieving details of an E-Line service carried over ring(s) and a linear spur

Retrieving details of an E-Line service carried exclusively over one or more G.8032 rings

You will need the FRE ID of the service you wish to query.

Use the following API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v4/fres/<FRE_ID of the service over Ring>

In the response below, note the new relationship " configurationAndSwitchControl".

Provision an E-Line service over seamless MPLS

You can create an E-Line service over a Seamless MPLS network if a suitable tunnel exists. This use case covers creating an E-Line service over the following combinations of endpoints:

  • AN-AGN-AGN

  • AN-AGN-AGN-AN, and

  • AN-AGN-AN

In this case you provision an E-Line service using BGP tunnels and RSVP-TE unidirectional Utilization-based tunnels. You cannot use RSVP-TE unidirectional CAC-based tunnels.

General details

  • An E-LINE creation request/response is same for a seamless or non-seamless network.

    The standard API call for basic E-Line service creation is described in API calls for managing E-Line services.

  • If the auto create tunnel flag is True, then the required tunnels will be auto created for AGN-AGN, AN-AGN/AN services.

  • If the auto create tunnel flag is False or not in the request, then there is no change in the existing behavior.

  • Two different auto-create tunnel properties are maintained in IfdConfig: one for seamless and one for non-seamless services.

  • Seamless vs non-seamless services

    • Services over non-seamless — AGN-AGN:

      • no BGP tunnels involved

      • PW directly over RSVP tunnels

      • User constraints (such as FRR true/false, utilization/CAC, tunnel affinity) are accepted.

    • Service over Seamless — AN-AGN/AN:

      • BGP tunnels involved

      • PW over BGP tunnels

      • RSVP tunnel mesh is auto-created between AGNs (if it does not exist)

      • User constraints (such as FRR true/false, utilization/CAC, tunnel affinity) are ignored for auto-created RSVP tunnels.

Note 1: A tunnel affinity constraint or tunnel type constraint will have no bearing when Seamless MPLS is in the route. You must choose an RSVP-TE tunnel because BGP does not have the capability to process these type of constraints. As such, BGP will choose a RSVP-TE unidirectional tunnel of any affinity and will also prefer a unidirectional utilization-based tunnel that is FRR protected.

Note 2: A change in network role as described in the topic Assign a node role (Prerequisite for E-Line provisioning in seamless MPLS network) will only have bearing on newly created services.

Device support

  • 6500-T 13.05 Packet Fabric (CO) (AGN)

  • 6500-S PTS 13.05 Packet Fabric (CO) (AN/AGN)

  • 3926m 6.18 (AN)

If a suitable LSP is not available and you want to include a request to create a Dynamic MPLS RSVP-TE LSP tunnel when you provision an E-Line service, see the following topics:

  • Provision an E-Line service over seamless MPLS with automatic tunnel creation

  • Provision an E-Line service with automatic tunnel creation

  • Provision an E-Line service over seamless MPLS with automatic tunnel creation

  • Provision an E-Line service with automatic tunnel creation

Provision an E-Line service over seamless MPLS with automatic tunnel creation

You can use the Navigator MC API to create an E-Line service over a seamless MPLS network, and include a request to create a Dynamic MPLS RSVP-TE LSP tunnel if a suitable LSP is not available. As part of this request, you can specify the type and configuration of the LSP to be automatically created.

An E-LINE creation request/response is same for a seamless or non-seamless network.

The standard API call for basic E-Line service creation is described in API calls for managing E-Line services.

This case describes service provisioning between AGN-AGN, including a request to automatically create an RSVP-TE MPLS tunnel between the two AGNs if required.

You can request tunnel auto-creation as part of the service-provisioning call by including the "autoCreateInfrastructure" attribute, and setting its value to "True":

"autoCreateInfrastructure": true,

This is an optional attribute. Whenever it is absent from a service provisioning request, Navigator MC proceeds as though its value is "false".

Note that:

  • If the value provided for the auto-create infrastructure option is "false", and no existing LSP is available, then service creation will fail.

  • When a suitable LSP is already present, the auto-create LSP option has no effect; the operation will succeed using the existing LSP, and no new LSP will be created.

When creating an E-Line service over seamless MPLS (AN-AN, AN-AGN), Navigator MC’s tunnel selection criteria will select protected RSVP-TE uni-directional tunnels if they are available.

If protected uni-directional RSVP-TE tunnels are not available, and tunnel auto-creation is specified in the service creation request, then Navigator MC will automatically create a new mesh of protected, unidirectional RSVP-TE tunnels to support the E-Line service (even if pre-existing, unprotected unidirectional tunnels were available).

Navigator MC supports this capability on the following devices:

  • 6500-T 13.05 Packet Fabric (CO) (AGN)

  • 6500-S PTS 13.05 Packet Fabric (CO) (AN/AGN)

  • 3926m 6.18 (AN)

Contrasting AGN-AGN vs. AN-AN/AGN cases

Service provisioning between AGN-AGN will not use any Seamless MPLS BGP tunnels; only RSVP tunnels are used or newly created between these AGNs. Pseudowires will traverse these selected or newly created RSVP tunnels. For details, see Provision an E-Line service with automatic tunnel creation

Service provisioning between AN-AN/AGN will use Seamless MPLS BGP tunnels. RSVP tunnels between AGNs will be used or newly created. Pseudowires will traverse the BGP tunnel.

Configurable parameters when automatically creating tunnels

If the original service creation request contained a transport protection constraint and/or an affinity constraint, Navigator MC will ignore these constraints when automatically creating tunnels. Instead, Navigator MC will use system-configurable defaults specifically for use during automatic tunnel creation.

These configuration parameters include:

  • FRR yes/no

    Note: For Seamless MPLS case, auto created tunnels will be always Dynamic unidirectional utilization based FRR protected tunnels. FRR protection and auto-size mode attributes will not be configurable in this case.

  • Affinity

    Note: User-provided affinity constraints will be ignored; however, tunnel affinity constraints can be configured in IfdConfig for auto-created tunnels over Seamless MPLS BGP.

  • Auto-size (yes/no)

  • Min (Mbps)

  • Max (Mbps)

  • Increment (Mbps)

  • Auto-resize interval timer (seconds)

See also the following section.

Auto-created tunnel properties over pure RSVP-TE tunnels

            "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelReOptimizationIntervalUnitEthOverBGP":{
                "default": "minutes",
                "supportedValues": "minutes",
                "description": "Re-optimization interval units,, in case of auto created tunnels during l2 ethernet service provisioning Over Seamless MPLS BGP Tunnels."
            },
            "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelIncludeAllResourcesColorGroupEthOverBGP":{
                "default": "",
                "supportedValues": "^[^\\s!%,?*\"\\\\]{0,31}$",
                "description": "Auto create tunnel affinity include all resources with specific color-group for l2 ethernet service provisioning Over Seamless MPLS BGP Tunnels."
            },
            "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelIncludeAnyResourcesColorGroupEthOverBGP":{
                "default": "",
                "supportedValues": "^[^\\s!%,?*\"\\\\]{0,31}$",
                "description": "Auto create tunnel affinity include any resources with specific color-group for l2 ethernet service provisioning Over Seamless MPLS BGP Tunnels."
            },
            "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelExcludeAnyResourcesColorGroupEthOverBGP":{
                "default": "",
                "supportedValues": "^[^\\s!%,?*\"\\\\]{0,31}$",
                "description": "Auto create tunnel affinity exclude any resources with specific color-group for l2 ethernet service provisioning Over Seamless MPLS BGP Tunnels."
            }

Configuring the BPO-IFD configurable properties:

  • Getting the BPO-IFD configuration properties

  • Editing BPO-IFD configuration properties

Getting the BPO-IFD configuration properties

To view the current list of BPO-IFD configuration properties, send a GET request to 'BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig'.

This request will return the list of all resources linked to the IfdConfig resource type. Although the Ifd Configuration is a singleton resource, other instances of the resources can be created by the orchestrator; however validation in BPO-IFD ensures that extras will have a 'failed' orchestration state. The relevant config is the one in 'active' state; this resource’s resource id should be used in PATCH requests, as indicated below.

Editing BPO-IFD configuration properties

The BPO-IFD configuration properties are pulled in from /bpo-ifd/resources/model-definitions/plans/ifd/config/default_config.json and are generated as part of an IfdConfig resource.

To modify the configuration properties, send a PATCH request to BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RESOURCE_ID} where resourceId is the resource id of the active IfdConfig resource in Market.

Ensure that the body of the request contains the name of the property you want to edit as the key in the configurationProperties object, and that the 'value' key of the property object is being modified, for example:

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.l0.setExplicitFrequency": {
        "value": "false"
      }
    }
  }
}

Resetting ifdConfig

To reset ifdConfig to the default values, perform the following steps:

  1. Fetch the ifdConfig product ID.

  2. Delete the existing:

    "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig"

  3. Create a new resource:

    BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

    {
    "properties": {},
    "productId": "{{ifdConfig product ID}}",
    "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig",
    "label": ""
}
Auto-created tunnel naming

If Navigator MC automatically creates a tunnel as part of service provisioning, it will assign the tunnel an automatically generated name using the following format:

PREFIX_SUFFIX

where:

  • PREFIX: This is a tunnel prefix name defined by the "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelNamePrefixEthOverBGP" IfdConfig property. It is a 10-character string.

  • SUFFIX: This is a 16-digit value representing the current time in microseconds.

The result will be a tunnel name resembling the following (for AN-AGN and AN-AN):

AUTO_LSP_B<16-digit-time-microseconds>

Auto-created tunnel naming with Tids Format

If Navigator MC automatically creates a tunnel as part of service provisioning, it will assign the tunnel an automatically generated name using the following format:

PREFIX_AEndTID_Index_ZEndTID

where:

  • PREFIX: This is a tunnel prefix name defined by the "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelNamePrefixForTidFormat" IfdConfig property. It is a 5-character string.

  • AEndTID: AEnd Tid Name where LSP head End resides

  • ZEndTID: ZEnd Tid Name where LSP tail End resides

  • Index : It’s an Navigator MC internal unique auto-generated number

The result will be a tunnel name resembling the following (for AN-AGN and AN-AN):

MCP_AEnd_1_ZEnd

Maximum Tunnel Name length allowed on NEs is 31. In case, tunnel name exceeds this limit, then tunnel name will resemble the following:

MCP_to_1_ZEnd

By default, this feature is disabled. To enable this feature, user need to set "ifd.l2.useTidForAutoCreateTunnelName" as "true" in IfdConfig.

Provision an E-Line service with automatic tunnel creation

When you use the Navigator MC REST API to create an E-Line service, you can specify that Navigator MC should automatically create the supporting MPLS tunnel if a suitable LSP in the Dynamic MPLS RSVP-TE is not already available.

The standard API call for basic E-Line service creation is described in API calls for managing E-Line services. This case describes service provisioning between AGN-AGN, including a request to automatically create an RSVP-TE MPLS tunnel between the two AGNs if required.

Note: For details describing service provisioning between AN-AN/AGN, which uses Seamless MPLS BGP tunnels, see Provision an E-Line service over seamless MPLS with automatic tunnel creation.

You can request tunnel auto-creation as part of the service-provisioning call by including the "autoCreateInfrastructure" attribute, and setting its value to "True":

"autoCreateInfrastructure": true,

This is an optional attribute. Whenever it is absent from a service provisioning request, Navigator MC proceeds as though its value is "false".

As part of this request, you can also specify some details about the tunnel to be created:

  • Tunnel protection level (either Protected or Unprotected)

  • Tunnel directionality (only unidirectional tunnels are currently supported; a request for a bidirectional tunnel will be rejected)

  • Tunnel signaling (only dynamic tunnels are currently supported; a request for a static tunnel will be rejected)

  • Tunnel affinity constraints (tunnel creation will be use the affinity specified in the request; see Applying affinity constraints.

There are some restrictions placed on the service when using the tunnel auto-creation option:

  • The service must be provisioned over dynamic, unidirectional tunnels

  • The service endpoints must be located on the following devices:

    • 6500-T 13.05 Packet Fabric

    • 6500-S PTS 13.05 Packet Fabric

  • The service must travel directly over the MPLS tunnel; no BGP or QinQ segements can be included in the path

Additional limitations of tunnel auto-creation are described below in Limitations.

Note 1: If you include an existing tunnel’s name as part of your service-creation API call, then no new tunnel(s) will be created even if the autoCreateInfrastructure attribute is set to "yes" as part of the same call. This supersedes all other behaviors for tunnel auto-creation.

Note 2: After a configurable timeout period, if the service you are creating with “auto create tunnel” enabled has not yet been deployed successfully, Navigator MC will stop attempting to provision the service and will mark the operation as an “incomplete deployment”.

The IfdConfig property "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelDeployTimeoutInMinutes" determines the default timeout period:

"ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelDeployTimeoutInMinutes": {
    "default": "15",
    "supportedValues": "1-60",
    "description": "Service deploy timeout in minutes in case of auto create tunnels."
}

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Auto-created tunnel naming

  • Tunnel affinity constraints support

  • Limitations

  • Dedicated Infrastructure Tunnel Per Infrastructure Service

Auto-created tunnel naming

If Navigator MC automatically creates a tunnel as part of service provisioning, it will assign the tunnel an automatically generated name using the following format:

PREFIX_SUFFIX

where:

  • PREFIX: This is a tunnel prefix name defined by the "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelNamePrefix" IfdConfig property. It is a 10-character string.

  • SUFFIX: This is a 16-digit value representing the current time in microseconds.

The result will be a tunnel name resembling the following (for AGN-AGN):

AUTO_LSP_<16-digit-time-microseconds>

Tunnel affinity constraints support

You can specify affinity constraints (in the form of resource colour groups) for the tunnel you would like to be auto-created for your service.

Example of tunnel affinity constraints

"dynamicTunnelPathConstraints": {
    "includeAllResourcesColorGroup": "CG_RG",
    "includeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "CG_RG",
    "excludeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "CG_B"
}

If you include affinity constraint values in a service provisioning request that includes the autoCreateInfrastructure attribute, Navigator MC will attempt to create a tunnel using these constraints. The specified color groups must already be defined on the nodes participating in the tunnel; if not, the provisioning attempt will fail.

If you do not include any tunnel affinity constraints, Navigator MC will check whether default affinity constraint values have already been defined for the endpoint nodes. If such default constraints have been configured, Navigator MC will use those values; if no defaults are configured, then Navigator MC will not apply any affinity constraints to the tunnel.

Below is a sample payload for an API call creating an E-Line service, which includes the autoCreateInfrastructure and affinity constraints for the auto-created tunnel.

Sample request for automatic tunnel creation including tunnel affinity constraints

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "discovered": false,
    "properties": {
    "type": "FDFR",
    "structure": "P2P",
    "routeMeta": {
        "originator": "BP2"
    },
    "serviceType": "EVPL",
    "protectedPseudowire": false,
    "oamEnabled": false,
    "linearOnly": false,
    "allowQinQSpur": false,
    "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_ONLY",
    "constraints": {
     "transport": {
       "directionality": "unidirectional",
       "dynamicTunnelPathConstraints": {
            "includeAllResourcesColorGroup": "CG_RG",
            "includeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "CG_RG",
            "excludeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "CG_B"
        }
     },
     "routes": [
        {
          "protection": "unprotected",
          "direction": [
            "A",
            "Z"
          ]
        },
        {
          "protection": "unprotected",
          "direction": [
            "Z",
            "A"
          ]
        }
      ]
   },
   "interactive_mode": "true",
   "autoCreateInfrastructure": true,
   "endpoints": [
     {
       "settings": {
         "role": "A_UNI",
         "details": [
           {
             "flowSettings": [
               {
                 "filter": {
                   "outerVlanId": [
                     767
                   ]
                 },
                 "profiles": [],
                 "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                 "location": {
                   "shelf": "4",
                   "slot": "3",
                   "port": "1",
                   "eqptGrp": "7"
                 }
               }
             ]
           }
         ],
         "node": "GSIM-HAX13-004"
       }
     },
     {
       "settings": {
         "role": "Z_UNI",
         "details": [
           {
             "flowSettings": [
               {
                 "filter": {
                   "outerVlanId": [
                     767
                   ]
                 },
                 "profiles": [],
                 "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                 "location": {
                   "shelf": "5",
                   "slot": "3",
                   "port": "1",
                   "eqptGrp": "7"
                 }
               }
             ]
           }
         ],
         "node": "GSIM-HAX13-005"
       }
