   "name": "AUTO_ELINE",
   "userLabel": "LABEL",
   "customerName": "CIENA"
 }
}
Limitations

Tunnel directionality: Only unidirectional tunnels are supported for automatic tunnel creation. If the service provisioning request specifies that tunnel directionality is bidirectional, Navigator MC will return an error and service provisioning will fail.

Tunnel signalling: Only Dynamic tunnels are supported for automatic tunnel creation. If the service provisioning request specifies that the tunnel signaling is "Static", Navigator MC will return an error and service provisioning will fail.

Delayed provisioning: When you schedule the future creation of a service for which the "autoCreateInfrastructure" flag is enabled, the need to create any supporting tunnels is determined at the time you submit the request. It is not re-evaluated at the scheduled deployment time.

As a result, if tunnels are required when you submit the service creation request, then tunnel creation will be scheduled and will occur at the deployment time. If in the interval new tunnels are created, this will not affect the already-scheduled tunnel creation (even if those new tunnels could have carried the requested service).

No TDM: Tunnel auto-creation is supported only for Ethernet services. A request to provision a TDM service with tunnel auto-creation will return an error and service provisioning will fail.

No protected services: Tunnel auto-creation is supported only for unprotected, point-to-point E-Line services. Attempting to provision other service types (such as protected E-Line, dual-homed E-Line, or E-LAN) will return an error and service provisioning will fail.

Dedicated Infrastructure Tunnel Per Infrastructure Service

There will be an option during infrastructure service create, based on includeAll affinity value to automatically drive the forced auto-creation of an RSVP-TE tunnel for a new service create request.

A global system policy would allow the user to configure either a single or a set of includeAll affinity value(s). When a service create request contains that affinity as includeAllResourcesColorGroup transport constraint, then a dedicated RSVP-TE tunnel per PW (Pseudowire) is to be auto-created. If service create request doesn’t have includeAllResourcesColorGroup transport constraint, then Navigator MC default configured (IfdConfig value of "ifd.l2.autoCreateTunnelIncludeAllResourcesColorGroupEth" property) value will be picked.

This means even if there are other tunnels available in the network, a new tunnel will be auto-created specifically to be used with this service. Basically, the user is blocking the reuse of any existing tunnel thus forcing the auto-creation of a new tunnel for the service.

When deleting a service to have the system auto-delete the service’s RSVP-TE tunnel which was auto-created in the service create request due to a matching global configuration policy

Global Configuration Policies:

BPO-IFD Config Property for enable/disable dedicated tunnel auto create/delete
"ifd.l2.createDedicatedInfraForService":{
    "default": "false",
    "supportedValues": "true, false",
    "description": "Flag to allow dedicated tunnel to be auto created/deleted for Infrastructure services upon matching affinity."
}

BPO-IFD will define a new configurable IfdConfig property to Turn "ON" and "OFF" dedicated tunnel auto-creation/deletion for Infra services. Default value is 'false', which doesn’t allow the auto-creation/deletion of dedicated tunnels. However, changing this to '`false`, will disable this feature and tunnels will be auto created only if not available.

BPO-IFD Config Property for includeAll affinity
"ifd.l2.includeAllResourceCGForServiceWithDedicatedInfra":{
    "default": "",
    "supportedValues": "^[^\\s,\"\\\\]{0,31}$",
    "description": "Comma separated List of includeAllResourceColorGroup for Infrastructure services to allow dedicated tunnel auto create. Each value should match regex given in supportedValues"
}

Sample values for this property can be as below:

  • infrastructure

  • infrastructure_plane1,infrastructure_plane2, infrastructure_plane3

  • infrastructure_plane1

User input 'includeAll' affinity (in case of provisioning) and underlying tunnel’s 'includeAll' affinity (in case of deletion) will be exact matched with any of the above configured value(s). i.e. if the above property has value as "infrastructure_plane1, infrastructure_plane2, infrastructure_plane3" and user input value is "infrastructure" then it will not be considered as matched while the value "infrastructure_plane1" will be considered as matched.

Auto Deletion of dedicated Infrastructure tunnels:

Auto deletion of the tunnel(s) for infrastructure services will be supported for both Deployed and Discovered services. In a single workflow if service and tunnel(s) are to be deleted, then first, service should be deleted successfully from the nodes, then tunnel(s) deletion should be attempted. This is to avoid any CLI failure during tunnel(s) deletion because of the dependency of PW over tunnel. Deletion of underlying tunnel(s) will be done only in case all below 3 conditions are satisfied:

  1. Tunnel(s) is UniDirectional - Auto create/delete support is only for Unidirectional tunnels for now

  2. Tunnel(s) has the matching includeAll affinity, with the IfdConfig configured includeAll affinity

  3. Tunnel(s) has only one service going over - Ideally only one PW ridding over this tunnel - This is to avoid any CLI failure during tunnel deletion.

Auto-deletion of underlying tunnels will be ignored for E-LAN, E-TREE, D&C, TDM, Protected PW and MS-PW services, because there is no auto-create tunnel support for these types of services.
Auto-deletion of underlying tunnels is done implicitly during service delete (upon above mentioned conditions) and there is no explicit user input for tunnel auto-deletion. Because of this, user will not be informed about the success/failure of auto-deletion of tunnel(s).
As there is no explicit user input for auto-deletion of underlying tunnels, so auto-deletion will be done for both Discovered and Deployed services(s) or tunnel(s), if above mentioned conditions are true.

Provision an E-Line service with L2CFT ACLs to block protocols

You can create an E-Line Infrastructure (CO-CO [6500/PTS to 6500/PTS]) service and configure a custom Layer 2 Control Frame Tunneling (L2CFT) profile to block certain protocols to ensure that these protocols do not reach the far-end of the service.

The current 6500/PTS L2CFT capabilities do not support explicitly discarding the Cisco and ELMI protocols. As such, the use of Access Control Lists (ACL) on a per-service basis is required to discard frames with these protocols.

Device support

  • 6500-T 13.0+ Packet Fabric (CO)

  • 6500-S PTS 13.0+ Packet Fabric (CO)

When a service create request arrives with L2CFT enabled, and it specifies the name of the custom L2CFT profile that matches the name of the L2CFT profile named in the new BPO-IFD Config property, in addition to setting L2CFT, the system will also configure the ACLs on the device to block a set of Cisco and ELMI protocols.

You can set the profile at either or both endpoints, as required.

Three custom L2CFT profiles now exist for Verizon:

  • Default profile - changed to be MEF aligned

  • MEF custom profile

  • Infrastructure custom profile, where the ACLs are applied (on 6500/PTS devices for CO-CO infrastructure services), which is covered in this topic

Before you start this procedure, make sure that the L2CFT profiles are configured on the node. Next you will configure the same profile in Navigator MC using the details presented in this topic.

The new BPO-IFD config property required to configure the L2CFT profile for ACLs follows.

Note: The default is "Infra", which matches Verizon’s planned L2CFT custom profile name associated with ACLs.

"ifd.l2.l2cftProfileForAcl":{
"default": "Infra",
"supportedValues": "^[^\\s!%,?*\"\\\\]{0,31}$",
"description": "L2CFT profile name which require ACLs To Block Cisco Protocols For Verizon Infrastructure Services."
}

The new BPO-IFD config property required to block the list of destination MAC Addresses follows.

"ifd.l2.l2cftAclBlockedDaMacAddressList":{
"default": "01-00-0C-CC-CC-CC, 01-80-C2-00-00-07",
"description": "Comma separated List of DA MAC ADDRESS to be blocked during L2CFT ACL configurations."
}

Use the Market API to edit the BPO-IFD configuration properties.

Sample request

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

where the resourceId is the resource id of the active IFDConfig resource in Market.

Specify the IFD_CONFIG_RESOURCE_ID (which you obtain from the Response of Retrieve configuration resources.)

Ensure that

  • the body of the request contains the name of the property that you want to edit in the configurationProperties object, and

  • the value of the property object that you want to edit

For example:

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.l0.setExplicitFrequency": {
        "value": "false"
      }
    }
  }
}

Navigator MC will perform the following actions:

  1. After the sub-port is created, Navigator MC will choose classifier-precedence value 10 for the action deny as follows.

    classifier-precedence - For 'deny' filter-action, it will be 10.

    (As during service creation, only the sub-port will be created; the classifier-precedence never exists for requested node.)

  2. Navigator MC will then have classifier-precedence as well as a sub-port value, which is required in the following CLI command to create the access control list (ACL) on the node.

To make the access flow name unique, Navigator MC constructs the access flow name using the sub-port name. If the length of the access-flow name exceeds the supported character limit, the access flow name will be truncated.

access-flow create access-flow <access-flow-name> parent-sub-port 1_6_3_service1 classifier-precedence 10 filter-action deny
access-flow add access-flow <access-flow-name> class-element 10 c-mac-da <DA_MAC_ADDRESS_1>

access-flow add access-flow <access-flow-name> class-element 20 c-mac-da <DA_MAC_ADDRESS_2>

Note: The class-element starts at 10 and increments by 10 (for example, 10, 20, 30) for the 'deny' filter-action.

Delete an E-Line service with L2CFT ACLs to block protocols

You can delete an E-Line Infrastructure (CO-CO [6500/PTS to 6500/PTS]) service that was configured with a custom Layer 2 Control Frame Tunneling (L2CFT) profile to block certain protocols.

This topic provides instructions on how to delete a service that was originally created based on details in the following topic: Provision an E-Line service with L2CFT ACLs to block protocols.

Device support

  • 6500-T 13.0+ Packet Fabric (CO)

  • 6500-S PTS 13.0+ Packet Fabric (CO)

As part of the service deletion request, the Access Control Lists (ACL) are deleted, which ensures that all ACL remnants are removed from the device after the service is deleted.

  1. Using the Services inventory (FREs) API, get the FRE_ID of the service that you want to delete.

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/nis/api/fres

  2. Using the Market API, get the ManagedServiceContainer resource ID:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ManagedServiceContainer

  3. Using the Market API, delete the service by invoking the operation of the resource using the following API call and inputs:

    POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/<ManagedServiceContainer RESOURCE_ID>/operations

{
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "managedOperation": "Delete",
      "freId": "<FRE_ID>"
    }
  },
  "interface": "manageService"
}

During service deletion, the configured ACL must be deleted from the node. Navigator MC receives the acl flag for each endpoint CTPs and figures out the list of access-flow name(s) configured for the sub-port. Navigator MC uses the following CLI command to delete the list of access-flow names from the device.

access-flow delete access-flow <access-flow1>, <access-flow2>

Provision an E-Line service Y.1731 in MEF 35.1 mode

To provision an E-Line service and configure Y.1731 DMM/SLM in MEF 35.1 mode, use the Market API.

The Y.1731/MEF35.1 configuration can be achieved with or without predefined Navigator MC service profiles.

Note the following:

  • If you want to use a profile, you must first commission the bin profile. If you do not commission it, Navigator MC will not validate against the profile, in which case an error from the device will be propagated.

  • ‘testId’ will be generated on the basis of the new property cfmSetTestIdEqualPriorityMEF351. Otherwise, it will be node generated. 'testId' will be equal to priority if cfmSetTestIdEqualPriorityMEF351 is true.

  • Currently, multiple simultaneous Y.1731 sessions are not supported by Navigator MC. That is, for a given service the following are provisioned separately (mutually exclusively). They cannot be provisioned together because the testId counter is used in sharing mode; attempting to provision them together causes a conflict.

    • Y1731 in legacy

    • Y1731 in MEF mode

  • Single test sessions are supported for dmm/slm in legacy and mef mode aligned with node capabilities. For example, for a given service, you can configure delay measurement in MEF35.1 mode and synthetic loss measurement in legacy mode or vice versa.

  • For Y1731 setting reference( profileType) the existing maName functionality can be used: you can overwrite the cfmServiceName by providing the maName. The proposed format of the ma-name in this case is ServiceName==ProfileType Note that the current maName length restrictions apply. Select the serviceName and profileTypeName accordingly.

To configure the SLM responders on 6500 node running saos version 12.1 or onwards, the following limitations and assumptions should be considered:

Limitation

  • 'testId' on the generator and responder sides should match. As Navigator MC currently supports only one Y.1731 SLM test session, the default test-id is assumed as 1.

Assumptions

  • If testId and slmRemoteId are not present on A-end, then no value of testId and remoteMepId will be added in slmResponder package of Z-end.

  • slmTestId would be decided on the following factors:

    • If the User has provided the value, then user given value would have higher precedence.

    • if slmMode is MEF351, then slmTestID would be:

      • the same value as l2.ifd.cfmSlmTestId If ifd.l2.cfmMef351SetTestIdEqualPriority is false.

      • equal to slmPriority if ifd.l2.cfmMef351SetTestIdEqualPriority is true.

    Note: An upgrade impact will occur where hardware responders are already configured on the node. As a workaround, you must soft delete the services that have the hardware SLM responder configured on the node and then promote them.

  • dmmTestId would be decided on the following factors:

    • If the user has provided the value, then the user-given dmmTestID would have higher precedence.

    • If dmmMode is not MEF351, and dmmTestId is not provided by the user, then dmmTestId would be the same as per l2.ifd.cfmDmmTestId value.

    • if dmmMode is MEF351 and dmmCosMode is true, then dmmTestId would be the same as dmmPriority.

If a user has provided the dmmTestID value other than dmmPriority along with dmmCosMode as true then an exception will be raised.

Device Support

  • 6500-T 15.1+ as AN node

  • 6500-PTS 15.1+ as AN node

  • 3926m SAOS 6.18+ as AN node

Sample request

POST /{NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

If you want to use a profile, you must first commission the bin profile. Next, in addition to specifying the attributes in the following list, you must also do the following.

For the Y1731 setting reference (profileType) the existing maName functionality can be used: you can over-write the cfmServiceName by providing the maName. The format of the ma-name in this case is ServiceName==ProfileType. Note: The current maName length restrictions apply. Select the serviceName and profileTypeName accordingly.

Whether you are using a profile or not, you must specify the following attributes in both settings sections of the endpoints in the request body, for example:

  • "dmmMode": "MEF35.1",

  • "slmMode": "MEF35.1",

Provision an E-Line service with burst size auto assignment

You can use the Navigator MC API to create

  • an E-Line single Class-of-Service (CoS) service, or

  • an E-Line untagged-only service

to have the burst size(s) automatically assigned to each service endpoint’s policer that has policing enabled based on Burst Size look-up table(s).

To do so, you must provide the CIR (and/or EIR) and PCP priority in the service request, which are used to locate the burst size (CBS/EBS) to auto-assign.

The following new properties have been added in IFDConfig. (Details follow in the related sections.)

  • ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment

  • ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignmentMappingWithPriorityBit

Auto Burst assignment will be applied to the following E-Line service combinations:

  • Auto Burst Assignment will only be done for EPL and EVPL with fixed Cos mapping services.

  • Auto Burst Assignment will be done for both UNI and ENNI ports.

  • Auto Burst Assignment also works for a Promoted service.

Note: If "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" and "policer" are enabled, then the service can only be created with ingress cos policy as fixed. All other scenarios (None/Empty/Multi-Cos) will result in an error and service creation/modification will fail.

Important validations for Auto Burst Assignment

  • The following validations are true if "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" is enabled:

    • If a CIR (or EIR) and PCP priority combination cannot be found in the look-up table, the service creation/modification request will fail.

    • If CBS and/or EBS are provided in the service creation/modification request, then the service request will fail.

    • A service creation/modification request Cos Policy should be Fixed and Priority Bit should be given explicitly.

    • If Cos Policy or Priority Bit is not specified by the user in the service creation/modification request, then by default the service is created with Cos Policy as "Fixed" and Priority Bit as "5". Service modification of such services will not be allowed if "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" is enabled and Policer/CIR/EIR is modified.

  • If "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" is disabled, then there is no change in the existing behavior.

  • Whenever the user creates a new autoburst resource, the default table values for burst assignment will be used.

  • For auto burst assignment lookup during service creation/modification, the count of the AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource should be equal to 1 and orchState should be "Active".

"ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment"

"ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment": {
"default": "disable",
"supportedValues": "enable, disable",
"description": "Enable/Disable Auto Burst Assignment of CBS and EBS values from Mapping Tables for L2 Service Creation and Modification. Default Value of this flag is disable."
}

You can update the default value to enable/disable the Auto Burst Assignment of the CBS and EBS values from the Mapping Tables for L2 service creation and modification.

"ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignmentMappingWithPriorityBit"

 "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignmentMappingWithPriorityBit":{
     "default": "0:eline_Basic,2:eline_PD,3:eline_RT",
     "supportedValues": "^([0-7]:\\w+,*)+$",
     "description": "Mapping of various Eline Services table with priority Bit for Auto Burst Assignment."
     }

  • The mapping of the Priority Bit with the Burst Size Table is defined in the IfdConfig file as ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignmentMappingWithPriorityBit.

  • The "default" is as follows:

    ""0:eline_Basic,2:eline_PD,3:eline_RT","

  • The mapping (in the "default") is defined as follows:

    <Priority Bit>:<Name of Burst Size Table>

    • 0 maps to the eline_Basic table

    • 2 maps to the eline_PD (eline Priority Data) table

    • 3 maps to the eline_RT (eline Real Time) table

  • "supportedValues" is as follows: <Value between 0-7> <Delimiter as:> <all alphabets, numeric, & "_"> and multiple entries must be separated with ","

  • There is no limit on the length of the table name.

  • Only one table can be mapped to one priority bit value.

  • Duplicate table names are not allowed (for example, "0:eline_Basic,2:eline_PD,5:eline_Basic,3:eline_RT").

  • Duplicate priority bit values are not allowed (for example, "0:eline_Basic,2:eline_PD,3:eline_RT,2:eline_PD").

  • Using the following API call, you can update the table-priority bit mapping or add/delete tables at any time. The new mappings will be effective for the next service creation/modification request.

    PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RESOURCE_ID_IFDCONFIG}?validate=false

Note: If new table entry is added in this property, then you must modify the AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource with the new table mappings using the modify resource operation. See Resource modification.

Actions

  • Prerequisite actions for Auto Burst Assignment

  • Service provisioning

Prerequisite actions for Auto Burst Assignment

ATTENTION

Before creating an E-Line service with Auto Burst Assignment, you must perform the following initial set-up.

  1. Change the ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment property value in the IfdConfig Resource as follows.

    1. Check that the IfdConfig Resource includes the ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment property:

      GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?productId={PRODUCT_ID_IFDCONFIG}&limit=1000

      Its default value is currently "disable" by default.

    2. Check the Auto Burst Assignment Mapping Resource:

      GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/productId={PRODUCT_ID_AUTOBURST}&limit=1000

      No Auto Burst Assignment Resource will be available yet.

    3. Patch the ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" property by changing the "value" to "enable":

      PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RESOURCE_ID_IFDCONFIG}?validate=false

    4. Check that the value of "ifd.l2.autoBurstAssignment" property (in the IfdConfig Resource) has changed to "enable":

      GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?productId={PRODUCT_ID_IFDCONFIG}&limit=1000

    Its default value has changed to "enable".

  1. Create the new AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource explicitly by using the Market API as follows.

    ATTENTION

    It is recommended that you create AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource only once.

    Later, if you want to update the Resource or property, add a new row, delete a row, you must use the modify resource operation. (See Resource modification.)

    However, note that if you choose to you can re-create the AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource. Doing so will result in an error. See Important validations for Auto Burst Assignment.

    1. Use the Market API as follows.

      POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?validate=false

      Specify the "productId" and the "resourceTypeId".

      {
    "properties": {}.
    "productId": "{{PRODUCT_ID_AUTOBURST}}",
    "resourceTypeId": "{{RESOURCE_TYPE_ID_AUTOBURST}}",
    "label": ""
}

    2. Check the Auto Burst Assignment Mapping Resource:

      GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/productId={PRODUCT_ID_AUTOBURST}&limit=1000

      The new AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource is created with orchState as "Active", which includes the three following tables with their associated mappings of cbs and ebs:

      • eline_Basic table

      • eline_PD table

      • eline_RT table

Service provisioning

  1. After performing the initial set-up, you can now proceed to provisioning the E-Line service by defining the service create request.

    Sample request

    POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?validate=false

    For a sample request, see the appropriate topic in API calls for managing E-Line services.

    and

    specify the following attributes in the service create request, as required:

    • ingressPolicer "cir" and/or "eir" value

    • "ingressCosPolicy"

    • "ingressCosPbit"

            "flowSettings": [
          {
            "filter": {
              "outerVlanId": [
                {{CVID}}
                ]
            },
            "ingressPolicer": {
              "cir": 1000000
              "eir": 2000000
             },
            "ingressCosSetting": {
              "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed"
              "ingressCosPbit": 2
             },

  2. Get the Service facade Id.

  3. Get the Service Intent Id.

  4. Get the FRE by Name (for this particular E-Line service).

Modify an E-Line service with burst size auto-assignment

Similar to regular E-Line service modification, you can use the Navigator MC API to modify an E-Line service that you created with burst assignment (based on instructions in Provision an E-Line service with burst size auto assignment. )

Resource modification

Similar to service modification, AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource modification is performed using the Market API.

You can modify the 'Burst Size' CIR/EIR by modifying the AutoBurstMappingTable Resource.

Note 1: A modified 'Burst Size' table only applies to new service creations: existing services cannot be updated retroactively.

Note 2: No support is provided for existing/native API for resource modification.

Sample request

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/operations

You can update the resource using two methods:

  • Method 1: Modify the Resource using a PUT call or

  • Method 2: Modify the Resource using RFC 6902 Json Patch

Method 1: Modify the Resource using a PUT call

Using this method, the existing AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource properties will be deleted and then the properties that you specified are used as new properties.

  • Update Resource Using Resource Properties — Format

    {
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties": {
      "autoBurstProperties": {
        /< Various Table Data to be used as Auto Burst Mapping Resource Properties />
      }
    }
  }
}

  • Update Resource Using Resource Properties — Sample request

    {
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties": {
      "autoBurstProperties": {
        "table 1": {
          "cir": {
            "cir value1": {
              "cbs": {
                "value": "cbs value1"
              }
            },
            "cir value2": {
              "cbs": {
                "value": "cbs value2"
              }
            }
          },
          "eir": {
            "eir value1": {
              "ebs": {
                "value": "ebs value1"
              }
            },
            "eir value2": {
              "ebs": {
                "value": "ebs value2"
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "table 2": {
          "cir": {
            "cir value1": {
              "cbs": {
                "value": "cbs value1"
              }
            },
            "cir value2": {
              "cbs": {
                "value": "cbs value2"
              }
            }
          },
          "eir": {
            "eir value1": {
              "ebs": {
                "value": "ebs value1"
              }
            },
            "eir value2": {
              "ebs": {
                "value": "ebs value2"
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Note:

  • Newly constructed AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource properties will be validated against the AutoBurst Schema.

  • If the Schema validation is successful, then the AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource is updated with Active State. Otherwise, an error will be reported.

Method 2: Modify the Resource using RFC 6902 Json Patch

The existing AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource properties will be modified with the input properties that you specified.

  • Update Resource Using Resource Properties Json Patch — Format

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": <path of the property to be changed>,
        "op": "add|remove|replace",
        "value": "value to be replaced"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Update Resource at Properties Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties",
        "op": "add|replace",
        "value": {
          "table 1": {
            "cir": {
              "cir value1": {
                "cbs": {
                  "value": "cbs value1"
                }
              },
              "cir value2": {
                "cbs": {
                  "value": "cbs value2"
                }
              }
            },
            "eir": {
              "eir value1": {
                "ebs": {
                  "value": "ebs value1"
                }
              },
              "eir value2": {
                "ebs": {
                  "value": "ebs value2"
                }
              }
            }
          },
          "table 2": {
            "cir": {
              "cir value1": {
                "cbs": {
                  "value": "cbs value1"
                }
              },
              "cir value2": {
                "cbs": {
                  "value": "cbs value2"
                }
              }
            },
            "eir": {
              "eir value1": {
                "ebs": {
                  "value": "ebs value1"
                }
              },
              "eir value2": {
                "ebs": {
                  "value": "ebs value2"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}
}

  • Update Resource at Table Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename",
        "op": "add|replace",
        "value": {
          "cir": {

              "cbs": {

            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Update Resource at CIR or EIR Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename/cir",
        "op": "add|replace",

            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Update Resource at CIR Value or EIR Value Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename/cir/cir value",
        "op": "add|replace",
        "value": {
          "cbs": {
            "value": "cbs value"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Update Resource at CBS or EBS Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename/cir/cir value/cbs",
        "op": "add|replace",
        "value": {
          "value": "cbs value"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Update Resource at CBS Value or EBS Value Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename/cir/cir value/cbs/cbs value",
        "op": "add|replace",
        "value": "value to be replaced"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

  • Delete Resource at CBS Value or EBS Value Level — Sample request

    {
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/autoBurstProperties/tablename/cir/cir value/cbs/cbs value",
        "op": "remove"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

Note:

  • Using either the Put method or the RFC 6901 Json Patch method, the newly constructed AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource properties will be validated against AutoBurst Schema.

  • If the Schema validation is successful, then the AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource will be updated with Active State. Otherwise, an error will be reported.

AutoBurst Schema

{
  "definitions": {},
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "autoBurstProperties"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "autoBurstProperties": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "patternProperties": {
        "^[a-zA-Z_0-9]*$": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "required": [
            "cir",
            "eir"
          ],
          "properties": {
            "cir": {
              "type": "object",
              "additionalProperties": false,
              "minProperties": 1,
              "patternProperties": {
                "^[0-9]*$": {
                  "type": "object",
                  "required": [
                    "cbs"
                  ],
                  "additionalProperties": false,
                  "properties": {
                    "cbs": {
                      "type": "object",
                      "required": [
                        "value"
                      ],
                      "additionalProperties": false,
                      "properties": {
                        "value": {
                          "type": "string",
                          "pattern": "^[0-9]*$"
                        }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            },
            "eir": {
              "type": "object",
              "additionalProperties": false,
              "minProperties": 1,
              "patternProperties": {
                "^[0-9]*$": {
                  "type": "object",
                  "required": [
                    "ebs"
                  ],
                  "additionalProperties": false,
                  "properties": {
                    "ebs": {
                      "type": "object",
                      "required": [
                        "value"
                      ],
                      "additionalProperties": false,
                      "properties": {
                        "value": {
                          "type": "string",
                          "pattern": "^[0-9]*$"
                        }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

  4. Create New AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable Resource

    {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AutoBurstAssignmentMappingTable

Retrieve Burst Size Values from a Specific Burst Size Table

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve burst size values from a specific burst size table of auto burst assignment mapping table resource. See Step 2 of Prerequisite actions for Auto Burst Assignment

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • Table Name (from which burst size should be retrieved). This is mandatory attribute.

  • CIR Value is optional

  • EIR Value is optional

Specifying either CIR or EIR is mandatory

Configure properties in BPO-IFD through NBI

You can maintain new properties having encrypted values in BPO-IFD through NBI

The values of newly defined properties are stored in an encrypted format using Fernet’s encryption algorithm

Use the bpoifdnbi API to create/update/delete the properties in BPO-IFD:

REST API URL

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpoifdnbi/api/v1/config

Note 1: Creation of property would not be allowed if there is an existing property with the name

Note 2: Updating and Deletion of property would only be allowed if there is an existing property with the name

Supported Properties Following properties can be created using new API:

  • tldpPassword

  • tldpPasswordPWHandoff

Sample Request

For e.g. You can configure T-LDP password

Password Creation Request

{
  "name" : "tldpPassword",
  "value" : "password1",
  "operation" : "create"
}

Password Updation Request

{
  "name" : "tldpPassword",
  "value" : "password2",
  "operation" : "update"
}

Password Deletion Request

{
  "name" : "tldpPassword",
  "operation" : "delete"
}

Provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS

To provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS, use the Market API

This will cover creating an E-Line service over the following combinations of endpoints:

  • AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL

  • AN-ASBR-MSE/TL

A single node service having Ethernet Attachment Circuit and PW (l2-vpn) attachment with a Virtual Switch will be created on AN Node. The PWHE peer IP is MSE/TL/3rdParty (or far end AN loopback IP in case of inter-region service). For AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL the network must have IGP tunnels to reach ASBR loopback from AGN loopback and vice versa.

Device Support

  • 6500-T 13.06 & 13.3+ as ASBR node

  • 6500-T 13.06 & 13.3+ as AGN node

  • 6500-S PTS 13.06 & 13.3+ AN node

  • 3926m SAOS 6.18 & 6.19+ as AN node

Sample request with CFM enabled

For 10.x interop CFM configuration, new endpoint attribute "taggedCFM" can be used with values (enable/disable) to configure tagged CFM on the endpoint. Default value is "disable". This is done because as of now 10.x devices support tagged CFM only.

PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS request parameters

  • PWHE Endpoint

Parameter Required? Description

pwHeadEndSettings.pwName

Optional

Virtual Circuit (l2-vpn) name

pwHeadEndSettings.pwId

Mandatory

PW Identifier (1-2147483647 for Ciena NE’s). Must match on both sides.

pwHeadEndSettings.pwType

Optional

PW type i.e. raw/tagged

pwHeadEndSettings.mtu

Optional

PW Maximum Transmission Unit Size (bytes)

pwHeadEndSettings.pwConnectivityMode

Optional

PW Mode i.e. mesh or spoke

pwHeadEndSettings.peerIp

Mandatory

Loopback IP address of PWHE peer i.e. MSE/Thirdparty Node

pwHeadEndSettings.tldpAuthentication

Optional

PW T-LDP session authentication enabled or not for the peer i.e. on or off

pwHeadEndSettings.bgpSettings.asbrNodeList

Optional

(It is expected that asbrNodeList is not given or empty only when underlying infrastructure is ready because system has no way to figure out the existence of tunnels as there are no ASBR node provided.)

Autonomous System Border Router’s i.e. IGP boundary for AS. Node name is must for PW transport as bgp-tunnel

pwHeadEndSettings.bgpSettings.bgpRemoteCommunityList

Optional

List of remote communities

pwHeadEndSettings.tunnelType

Optional

The tunnel type acting as server of PW

  • Service (Only when CFM is enabled)

Parameter Required? Description

properties.mdLevel

Optional

CFM Maintenance Domain Level (0-7), default value will be picked from IfdConfig property "ifd.l2.cfmMdLevel"

  • UNI/ENNI endpoint (Only when CFM is enabled)

Parameter Required? Description

settings.mepId

Optional

Allocated MEP Identifier (1-8191) for local endpoint. Must when CFM is enabled on this endpoint

settings.remoteMepId

Optional

Allocated MEP Identifier (1-8191) for remote endpoint. Must when DMM/SLM/SLM Responder is enabled on this endpoint

settings.taggedCFM

Optional

enable/disable. Tagged CFM to be enabled or disabled on this endpoint

settings.slmResponder

Optional

enable/disable. SLM Responder to be enabled or disabled on this endpoint

settings.slmResponderTestId

Optional

* and 1 to 2147483647. SLM Responder Test Id should be used for single-ended/inter-region PW Hand-off services.

settings.slmTestId

Optional

1 to 4294967295. CFM SLM Test ID.

settings.dmmTestId

Optional

0 to 4294967295. CFM DMM Test ID.

settings.cfmAlarmPriority

Optional

1 to 5. CFM Alarm Priority.
CFM alarm priority is a fre level entity, hence it will be visible on dual root port as well.
dmmTestId value "0" is not supported for 6500 devices.
SLM responder test id as a wild card(*) is only supported for 6500 15.1+ CTM and PTS devices.

For AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL, user can request tunnel auto-creation as part of the service-provisioning call by including the "autoCreateInfrastructure" attribute, and setting its value to "true":

"autoCreateInfrastructure": true
For Intra-Region PW Handoff service provisioning same service create request (as given above for inter-region services) would be used. This is applicable only for seamless intra-region services i.e. for AN-AGN and AN-AN configurations. However, autoCreateInfrastructure is not supported for intra-region PW Handoff services.

Inter-Region PW Handoff Service Discovery and Inventory

Below will be the supported configuration:

  • AN-AGN-ASBR (Region1)-TL-TL-ASBR-AGN-AN (Region2)

  • AN-AGN-ASBR (Region1)-TL-TL-ASBR-AN (Region2)

  • AN-ASBR (Region1)-TL-TL-ASBR-AGN-AN (Region2)

  • AN-ASBR (Region1)-TL-TL-ASBR-AN (Region2)

When both the regions are in different-different Autonomous Systems (i.e. has different-different AS numbers in BGP configuration) then both the services will not be stitched by Navigator MC when stitcher application GCS property "stitchPwInDifferentASN.enabled" has value "false". In this case there will be two services in Navigator MC for each region. Default value of this property is "true" which is pushed by stitcher application. Service names may or may not be same in both the regions. However, other attributes like PWID, CVID (in case of EVPL service) and CFM service name (maName) should be same in both the regions.

REST API to configure/update this property in GCS

  • Run the REST PATCH request on the URL: https://<server>/gcs/api/v1/config with below JSON Body, to update the property value to "false".

  • Run the REST POST request on the URL: https://<server>/gcs/api/v1/config with below JSON Body, to create the property, if the property doesn’t exist.

[
  {
    "application": "stitcher",
    "instance": "-",
    "partition": "bptopostitcher",
    "name": "stitchPwInDifferentASN.enabled",
    "title": "Stitch PW in different AS",
    "description": "Bootstrap property to stop Stitcher from stitching PW CTPs in different ASN. Value 'false' means not to stitch the PW CTPs of different AS.",
    "tags": [
      "bootstrap"
    ],
    "value": "false",
    "key": "stitcher/-/bptopostitcher/stitchPwInDifferentASN.enabled",
    "id": "stitcher---stitchPwInDifferentASN.enabled-bptopostitcher-undefined"
  }
]
In-case of Active-Standby GR cluster setup, update above GCS property on active server only. No need to update it on standby server as it will automatically get replicated on standby server.
This GCS property is a bootstrap property in nature i.e. changes in the flag value (or configure in GCS for the first time) will require restart of Stitcher application.

Steps to restart Stitcher application:

  1. Stop Stitcher instance (For Active-Standby GR cluster setup, do it for all the stitcher containers on active site)

    sudo solman
api containers stitcher_[TAB] stop post

  2. Start Stitcher instance (For Active-Standby GR cluster setup, do it for all the stitcher containers on active site)

    sudo solman
api containers stitcher_[TAB] start post
    where

    [TAB]

    means hit the [TAB] key — solman will autocomplete to select the current deployed stitcher application version and instance(s). Example: stitcher_3.9.6_0, stitcher_3.9.6_1 etc.

  3. For Active-Standby GR cluster setup, repeat above steps 1 and 2 for all the stitcher containers on standby site. Same need to do after Backup and Restore also.

Intra-Region PW Handoff Service Discovery and Inventory

Once both the regions are provisioned using multi-step, then end-to-end service will be stitched to one service. Service deployment state will be Discovered and not Deployed. Due to this, no edit support would be there on this stitched service. Both the segments can be modified independently similar to inter-region service segments. Same is applicable for service delete also.

Service promotion/demotion operations are not supported on this stitched Discovered service. Service assurance would work same as dual-ended services.

Table Map Update

During PW-Handoff service create, if AN endpoint node is SAOS 6x then, on it’s neighbouring AGN node, additional table map update CLI will be executed, to add PWHE peer IP in the prefix-list, when peer IP is not already there in prefix-list.

During PW-Handoff service delete, if AN endpoint node is SAOS 6x then, on it’s neighbouring AGN node, additional table map update CLI will be executed, to remove PWHE peer IP from the prefix-list, only when this is last service with this peer IP.

Table Map Update is not applicable for intra-region PW Handoff services. Inter and intra-region PW Handoff services will be identified using PWID as there are different PWID ranges defined for both the services. It is recommended to configure and use correct PWID for both the services to avoid wrong Table Map update.

Provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over RSVP-TE Tunnels

This will cover creating an E-Line service over the following combinations of endpoints:

  • AGN-AGN

Device Support

  • 6500-T 13.06 & 13.3+ as AGN node

Service provisioning REST request is similar to Provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS with below changes:

  • For PWHE, tunnel-type would be "rsvp-te-tunnel"

  • For PWHE, "bgpSettings" are not allowed

  • "transportProtection" attribute is mandatory for AGN-AGN PW Handoff service creation to pick the correct tunnel. Possible values are MPLS_ONLY, PROTECTED_ONLY, UNPROTECTED_ONLY, PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT, UNPROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT

  • "linearOnly" should be given as "false" to consider the "transportProtection" attribute, to select the correct tunnel during service provisioning.

  • "autoCreateInfrastructure" should be given as "False" as auto create is not supported for Intra-region AGN-AGN services.

Sample request with CFM enabled

POST {{Navigator MC Server}}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

{
  "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
  "discovered": false,
  "properties": {
    "type": "FDFR",
    "structure": "P2P",
    "routeMeta": {
      "originator": "BP2"
    },
    "interactive_mode": "true",
    "autoCreateInfrastructure": true,
    "serviceType": "EVPL",
    "oamEnabled": true,
    "ccmPriority": 2,
    "ccmInterval": "10sec",
    "maName": "{{SERVICE_NAME}}",
    "mdLevel": 3,
    "linearOnly": false,
    "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_ONLY",
    "endpoints": [
      {
        "settings": {
          "role": "A_UNI",
          "oamEnabled": true,
          "mepId": 1,
          "remoteMepId": 2,
          "remoteMepMacAddress": "CD:00:1F:AB:DC:01",
          "slmResponder": "enable",
          "slmResponderTestId": "*",
          "dmmEnabled": true,
          "slmEnabled": true,
          "ccmTransmitEnabled": true,
          "taggedCFM": "enable",
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {
                    "outerVlanId": [
                      979
                    ]
                  },
                  "profiles": [],
                  "ingressCosSetting": {
                    "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                    "ingressCosPbit": 2
                  },
                  "ingressPolicer": {
                    "cir": 300,
                    "eir": 100,
                    "cbs": 50,
                    "ebs": 50
                  },
                  "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                  "location": {
                    "shelf": "61",
                    "eqptGrp": "41",
                    "slot": "7",
                    "port": "1"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "node": "{{neAEnd}}"
        }
      },
      {
        "settings": {
          "role": "PWHE",
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "location": {
                    "shelf": "61",
                    "eqptGrp": "41"
                  },
                  "pwHeadEndSettings": {
                    "pwId": 79,
                    "peerIp": "71.71.71.71",
                    "tunnelType": "rsvp-te-tunnel"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "node": "{{neAEnd}}"
        }
      }
    ],
    "name": "{{SERVICE_NAME}}",
    "userLabel": "{{SERVICE_NAME}}",
    "customerName": "CIENA",
    "note": {
      "lastUpdatedBy": "admin",
      "lastUpdatedTime": "2018-09-04T12:45:07",
      "noteMsg": "Note"
    }
  }
}

First matching RSVP-TE tunnel will be picked which is starting from PWHE and ending on user provided peer IP. For matching the tunnel below criteria would be used:

  • Utilization based tunnels

  • PROTECTED/UN-PROTECTED tunnels (User provided value in "transportProtection" attribute)

  • Affinities (User provided value(s) in "dynamicTunnelPathConstraints" attribute)

This is an Intra-Region configuration, so Discovery, Inventory, Assurance and Table Map Update of these services are similar to Intra-Region PW Handoff Service Discovery and Inventory.

Auto Create of RSVP-TE tunnels is not supported for these PW-Handoff services. If no suitable tunnel is present then there will be an error.

Provision an E-Line service over mix of Default SR and MPLS-TP Tunnels

This will cover creating an E-Line service over the following combinations of endpoints:

  • UNI-UNI

  • ENNI-ENNI

  • UNI-ENNI

  • ENNI-UNI

In the service provisioning request, subMPLSTransportSchemes must be passed to obtain a route over a combination of Default SR and MPLS-TP tunnels. The possible values for subMPLSTransportSchemes are DEFAULT_SR and STATIC_COROUTED_TUNNEL.

Device Support

  • MPLS-TP

    • SAOS 6.x

    • SAOS 8.x

    • 6500-S Packet Fabric, eMOTR, eMOTR Edge

    • 6500-T 14.0+ Packet Fabric

    • 6500-S PTS 13.2+ Packet Fabric

    • SAOS 10.6+ and 10.7+

  • Default-SR

    • SAOS 10.6+ and 10.7+

Provision an Eline Service With CVID Stamping On Uni Endpoint Of PW Handoff Service

An EVPL Service with CVID Stamping is used on a tagged UNI service endpoint to configure an CVID stamp operations

To provision an E-Line service with CVID Stamping on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.18+

  • 6500-T/PTS 13.3+

Overview

  • A service with CVID Stamping is valid with UNI Endpoint of PW Handoff Service by providing different values of CVIDS in ingressStampVlanId and outerVlanId

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than E-Line (EVPL) with CVID Stamping

  • Navigator MC supports CVID Swapped service over MPLS transport only.

Provision an E-Line service with egress shaper rate configuration on UNI port

This use case covers creating an E-Line service with configuration of egress shaper rate on UNI port.

Device Support

  • 3926m SAOS 6.18 & 6.19 as AN node

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not have any intelligence to check if any invalid values for egress shaper rate have been sent to be set on the device. The value sent by the end-user is used as-is.

  • Navigator MC will not show any specific errors in case they occur, simply errors occurring on the device while running the command line will be shown directly to the users (if any).

  • Navigator MC will not allow modification of egress shaper rate in case of PW handoff service.

  • Navigator MC is not maintaining any inventory for the egress shaper rate because all the calculations are done at Nautilus(Customer side).

Sample request

POST \{Navigator MC Server\}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

{
 "productId": "5d8b128e-c475-4dd1-b1c9-f3269189176f",
 "discovered": false,
 "properties": {
   "type": "FDFR",
   "structure": "P2P",
   "routeMeta": {
     "originator": "BP2"
   },
   "serviceType": "EVPL",
   "protectedPseudowire": false,
   "oamEnabled": false,
   "linearOnly": false,
   "allowQinQSpur": true,
   "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT",
   "constraints": {
     "transport": {
       "directionality": "bidirectional"
     }
   },
   "interactive_mode": "true",
   "endpoints": [
     {
       "settings": {
         "role": "A_UNI",
         "details": [
           {
             "flowSettings": [
               {
                 "filter": {
                   "outerVlanId": [
                     481
                   ]
                 },
                 "egressPolicer": {
                     "shaperRate": 700000
                 },
                 "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                 "location": {
                   "port": "2"
                 }
               }
             ]
           }
         ],
         "node": "3926_0027"
       }
     },
     {
       "settings": {
         "role": "Z_UNI",
         "details": [
           {
             "flowSettings": [
               {
                 "filter": {
                   "outerVlanId": [
                     481
                   ]
                 },
                 "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                 "location": {
                    "shelf": "1",
                   "eqptGrp": "7",
                   "slot": "4",
                   "port": "2-1"
                 }
               }
             ]
           }
         ],
         "node": "OME-0980"
       }
     }
   ],
   "name": "Nautilus_se_egress"
 }
}

Provision an E-Line service with catch-all classifier on UNI endpoint

A Catch-All service can be used to carry all the traffic which isn’t carried by any other EVPL service provisioned on the same port.

To provision an E-Line service with catch-all classifier on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • 6500-T 13.3+

  • 6500-S PTS 13.3+

  • 6500-S 12.6+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-S PTS 12.6+ EMOTR/EMOTR EDGE

  • SAOS 6x 6.20+ (MPLS only)

  • SAOS 8.6.3+

  • SAOS 10.5.1+

Feature overview

  • A catch-all service can co-exist on the same port with other tagged, ranged, comma separated EVPL services.

  • If a service has a catch-all endpoint, then all the UNI endpoints have to be catch-all. However, an EVPL with Catch-all UNI - ENNI endpoint can be provisioned.

  • A catch-all service won’t be allowed if either a catch-all service or an EPL service exists on the same port.

  • Navigator MC does not allows CVID edit on catch-all service.

  • A discovered or demoted service with CVIDS [4096, 4097] will be classified as a catch-all EVPL service if one or more service(s) also exist on the same UNI port, else it will be considered as EPL.

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than E-Line (EVPL) with catch-all endpoints.

  • Navigator MC supports catch-all service provisioning only on MPLS transport for 6.x.

  • Navigator MC does not support cfm on catch-all service over 10x devices.

Catch-all service provisioning from UI

  • Catch-all service can be provisioned from UI by selecting "Catch-all (4096, 4097)" in the VID drop-down in the provisioning form.

  • Catch-all attribute can be seen on the service details/attribute page after the successful deployment of a service.

Sample request

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

To configure an endpoint as catch-all, CVIDS in the existing EVPL service request needs to be set as 4096, 4097.

{
    "productId": "5f046173-ae63-46d0-b873-613e4af033a6",
    "discovered": false,
    "properties": {
        "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "protectedPseudowire": false,
        "oamEnabled": false,
        "linearOnly": false,
        "allowQinQSpur": true,
        "constraints": {
            "transport": {
                "directionality": "unidirectional"
            },
            "routes": [
                {
                    "protection": "unprotected",
                    "direction": [
                        "A",
                        "Z"
                    ],
                    "includeRouteObjects": [
                        {
                            "locations": [
                                {
                                    "lspName": "3to4",
                                    "nodeName": "G8038-1-GSIM-0003"
                                }
                            ],
                            "objectType": "LSP_NAME",
                            "constraintType": "HARD"
                        }
                    ]
                },
                {
                    "protection": "unprotected",
                    "direction": [
                        "Z",
                        "A"
                    ],
                    "includeRouteObjects": [
                        {
                            "locations": [
                                {
                                    "lspName": "4to3",
                                    "nodeName": "G8038-1-TSIM-0004"
                                }
                            ],
                            "objectType": "LSP_NAME",
                            "constraintType": "HARD"
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        },
        "interactive_mode": "false",
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            4096, 4097
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "4",
                                        "slot": "8",
                                        "port": "2",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                    "node": "G8038-1-TSIM-0004"
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            4096, 4097
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                                    "location": {
                                        "shelf": "5",
                                        "slot": "8",
                                        "port": "2",
                                        "eqptGrp": "41"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                    "node": "G8038-1-TSIM-0005"
                }
            }
        ],
        "name": "catch-all-evpl"
    }
}

Catch-all service promotion

  • A discovered catch-all service has to be promoted with 'isCatchAllService' flag as true in the existing service promotion request. If this flag is not input then such service will be promoted as an EPL.

"isCatchAllService": true

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{<SERVICE_PROMOTION_CONTAINER_ID>}/operations

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{FRE ID}",
      "isCatchAllService": true
    }
  }
}

Provision a mix of Untagged and Tagged Ranged E-Line services over MPLS transport on same UNI port for 6.20 and above

Navigator MC will allow a mix of Untagged and Tagged/ Ranged E-Line EVPL services provisioned over MPLS transport for SAOS 6.20 and above.

Device Support

  • 6.20 and above MPLS capable devices

Feature overview

  • A mix of both Untagged and Tagged/ Ranged services over MPLS transport is now allowed on Navigator MC for SAOS 6.20 and above.

  • This feature was already supported for QinQ.

  • To turn this feature on user will have to patch IFD Config Resource with property "ifd.l2.rulesSwitchedOff" with value "UNTAGGED_ONLY_MPLS_ON_ANOTHER_MPLS, MPLS_ON_UNTAGGED_ONLY_MPLS"

  • The API calls for provisioning Untagged, Tagged and Ranged services remain the same.

Provision an E-Line Service With Untagged Vlan Id and Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

An EVPL Service with Untagged VLAN Id and Ether Type is used to PUSH/POP 802.1Q QTag along with Ether Type. This is valid for service with Untagged UNI Endpoint only.

To provision an E-Line service with Untagged Vlan Id classifier on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.18+

  • SAOS 8.6.3+

  • SAOS 8.7+

  • 6500-S 12.6+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-S PTS 12.6+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-T/PTS 13.3+(MPLS)

  • 6500-T 14.0 Packet Fabric (QinQ only)

Overview

  • A service with Untagged VLAN Id and Ether Type is valid with UNI Endpoint of Untagged Service

  • A service with Untagged VLAN Id is valid with UNI Endpoint of PW Handoff Service of Untagged Endpoint. For PW Handoff Service Creation refer to Provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than E-Line (EVPL) with Untagged VLAN Id

Provision an E-Line Service With Stag Data Vid and Stag Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

An EVPL, EPL and catch-all Service with Stag Data Vid and Stag Ether Type is used to PUSH/POP 802.1Q QTag along with Ether Type. This is valid for service with UNI Endpoint only.

To provision, an E-Line service with Stag Data Vid classifier on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.20+

  • 6500-S PTS 13.3+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-T/PTS 13.3

Overview

  • A service with Stag Data Vid and Stag Ether Type is valid with UNI Endpoint of MPLS based Service only.

  • A service with Stag Data Vid is valid with UNI Endpoint of PW Handoff Service.

  • Navigator MC does not allow the Creation of Stag data vid service on Untagged service, Service with CVID swapping and Service with ethertype stamping.

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than E-Line (EVPL, EPL) with Stag Data Vid

Sample request For Dual EndPoint Service

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

To configure an endpoint with Stag data Vid, CVIDS in the EVPL service request needs to be set as the same for both endpoints

{

Provision an E-Line Service With Ether Type Stamping On Uni Endpoint

An EVPL Service with Ether Type Stamping is used on a tagged UNI service endpoint to configure an EtherType stamp operations

To provision an E-Line service with Ether Type Stamping on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.18+

  • 6500-T/PTS 13.3+

  • 6500-S PTS 13.3+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-T 13.3+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-S 12.6+ Packet Fabric

  • SAOS 8.6+

  • SAOS 10.5+

Note: Dual Node Eline Service with Ether Type Stamping is only supported for SAOS 6.18+ and 6500-T/PTS 13.3+

EtherType would be ignored for 6x devices. Hence, in discovered data EtherType will not be present. Also on Navigator MC UI, Ether Type will not be visible under the attribute screen.

Overview

  • A service with Ether Type Stamping is valid with UNI Endpoint of Tagged Service

  • A service with Ether Type Stamping is valid with UNI Endpoint of PW Handoff Service. For PW Handoff Service Creation refer to Provision an E-Line PW Handoff service over seamless MPLS

  • A service with Ether Type Stamping is valid with UNI Endpoint of Local Switch Service

  • A service with Ether Type Stamping is valid with UNI Endpoint of Catch-All (Interceptor) Service. For Catch-all Service Creation refer to Provision an E-Line service with catch-all classifier on UNI endpoint

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than E-Line (EVPL) with Ether Type Stamping

  • Navigator MC supports Ether Type Swapped service over MPLS transport only

Provision an E-Line Service with dual-tag classifier

An EVPL Service with dual-tag classifier is used to classify ingress traffic based on outer + inner VLAN tag. Dual-tag classifier can be configured on both UNI and ENNI endpoint.

To provision an E-Line service with dual-tag classifier on UNI/ENNI endpoint, use the Market API

Device Support

  • 6500-S 12.6+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-S 12.6+ eMOTR / eMOTR Edge

  • 6500-T 14.1+

  • 6500-S PTS 14.1+

  • SAOS 6.18+ (MPLS)

  • SAOS 8.6+

  • SAOS 10.7+ (MPLS/QinQ)

Overview

  • For EVPL services, both UNI and ENNI endpoint can be configured with dual-tag classifier. However, for EPL service, dual-tag classification is applicable on ENNI endpoint only.

  • One or both endpoints can be configured as dual-tagged.

  • Outer tag transform is allowed on dual-tag classified E-Line service.

  • Hybrid classification (combination of single and dual-tag classifiers) is allowed on all supported devices except SAOS 6.x devices.

  • Untagged classifier is supported in combination with dual-tag classifiers.

  • Outer tag ether type can be configured with dual-tag classification.

  • SAOS 6.x device does not support dual-tag classification over QinQ or G.8032 rings. Navigator MC will reject QinQ/G.8032 routes having dual-tag classifier on 6.x devices.

  • SAOS 10.x device do not support untagged UP MEP in case of pure dual tagged service thus dual tagged UP MEPs would be supported when both end-points are on SAOS 10.7+ device.

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than 2-point E-Line (EVPL, EPL) with dual-tag classified endpoint.

  • MC-LAG endpoints with dual-tag classifiers are not supported.

  • Navigator MC does not support inner tag transform on dual-tag classified services.

  • MEP creation would not be allowed where all the classifiers applied are dual-tagged and one end-point is on SAOS 10x device and the other is on 6500/6x/8x/10x < SAOS10.7.

Dual-tag classification is not supported on ethernet services with a mix of MPLS and G.8032 ring(s) infrastructure. Additionally, it is not supported for services over G.8032 ring(s) for 10x devices.

Sample request For Dual EndPoint Service

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

To configure an endpoint with dual-tag classifiers, below request can be used

{
  "productId": "5f47d7f7-156b-47c3-9cb4-11aeb3c5c913",
  "discovered": false,
  "properties": {
    "type": "FDFR",
    "structure": "P2P",
    "routeMeta": {
      "originator": "BP2"
    },
    "serviceType": "EVPL",
    "protectedPseudowire": false,
    "oamEnabled": true,
    "linearOnly": false,
    "allowQinQSpur": true,
    "transportProtection": "PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT",
    "constraints": {
      "transport": {
        "directionality": "bidirectional"
      }
    },
    "interactive_mode": "false",
    "endpoints": [
      {
        "settings": {
          "role": "A_UNI",
          "oamEnabled": true,
          "ccmTransmitEnabled": true,
          "dmmEnabled": true,
          "slmEnabled": true,
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {
                    "classifierList": "100:10,100:20,101-103:1-4"
                  },
                  "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                  "location": {
                    "shelf": "4",
                    "slot": "7",
                    "port": "3",
                    "eqptGrp": "7"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "node": "GSIM-0004"
        }
      },
      {
        "settings": {
          "role": "Z_UNI",
          "oamEnabled": true,
          "ccmTransmitEnabled": true,
          "dmmEnabled": true,
          "slmEnabled": false,
          "details": [
            {
              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {
                   "classifierList": "100:10,100:20,101-103:1-4"
                  },
                  "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                  "location": {
                    "shelf": "5",
                    "slot": "7",
                    "port": "2",
                    "eqptGrp": "7"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "node": "GSIM-0005"
        }
      }
    ],
    "name": "uni_uni_service"
  }
}
Dual-tag classifiers can be given as a set of comma separated outer:inner pairs. Outer/inner VIDs can be given as a range or single value ("100:200,100:300,200-205:100-200") using 'classifierList' attribute. For ENNI endpoint, outer VID must be a single value.
outerVlanId or outervlanIdRange can not be used with classifierList in provisioning and modification of E-Line service.

Provision a PW Handoff Service with dual-tag classifier

A PW Handoff Service with a dual-tag classifier is used to classify ingress traffic based on outer + inner VLAN tag. Dual-tag classifier can be configured on both UNI and ENNI endpoints using the ClassifierList attribute.

To provision, a PW Handoff Service with a dual-tag classifier on UNI/ENNI endpoint, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.20+

  • 6500-T / PTS 14.1+

Supported Configurations

  • PW handoff Service with a dual-tag classified endpoint classifying on a single outer and single inner VID (eg 1:2)

  • PW handoff Service with a dual-tag classified endpoint classifying on a single outer and ranged inner VID (eg 1:4-5)

  • STag would be allowed along with dual-tag classification on PW handoff Service with the above two dual-tag classifier combinations

Limitations

  • Range Outer VIDs are not allowed.

  • Navigator MC does not support hybrid classifications (combination of single and dual-tag classifiers), untagged and outer/inner tag transform configurations on PW handoff service with dual-tag classifier.

Provision an E-Line service Y.1731 in MEF 35.1 mode on SAOS 10.x

To provision an E-Line service and configure Y.1731 DMM/SLM in MEF 35.1 mode, use the Market API.

The Y.1731/MEF35.1 configuration can be achieved with or without predefined Navigator MC service profiles.

Note the following:

  • ‘testId’ will be generated on the basis of the new property cfmSetTestIdEqualPriorityMEF351. Otherwise, it will be node generated. 'testId' will be equal to priority if cfmSetTestIdEqualPriorityMEF351 is true.

  • Single test sessions are supported for dmm/slm.

  • For Y1731 setting reference( profileType) the existing maName functionality can be used: you can overwrite the cfmServiceName by providing the maName. The proposed format of the ma-name in this case is ServiceName==ProfileType Note that the current maName length restrictions apply. Select the serviceName and profileTypeName accordingly.

  • MCP 5.0 will support only proactive session with start-time as immediate and stop-time as none.

Assumptions

  • Session-Id will be taken as 1 when configuring slm/dmm on node.

POST /{NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

For the Y1731 setting reference (profileType) the existing maName functionality can be used: you can over-write the cfmServiceName by providing the maName. Provision an unprotected, protected and multipoint PW handoff service

Use this procedure to provision an unprotected, protected or multipoint PW handoff service.

Retrieve L2 service intent facade it using Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID

In the response, note the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade. Use this ID as the product Id in the below request.

To create a PW handoff service, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the productId, which is obtained from the above.

Sample facade request for protected PW handoff service:

{
    "productId": "b4a5af80-57e4-11ec-9ba3-2b29c5e50128",
    "discovered": false,
    "properties": {
        "type": "FDFR",
        "structure": "P2P",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "protectedPseudowire": true,
        "oamEnabled": true,
        "serviceType": "EVPL",
        "endpoints": [{
                "settings": {
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "oamEnabled": true,
                    "ccmTransmitEnabled": true,
                    "dmmEnabled": true,
                    "slmEnabled": true,
                    "details": [{
                            "flowSettings": [{
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [555]
                                    },
                                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                                    "location": {
                                        "port": "8"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                    "node": "5144-10x-205",
                    "mepId": 1,
                    "dmmMode": "MEF35.1",
                    "remoteMepId": 2,
                    "slmMode": "MEF35.1"
                }
            }, {
                "settings": {
                    "role": "PWHE",
                    "details": [{
                            "flowSettings": [{
                                    "pwHeadEndSettings": {
                                        "pwMplsControlWordMode": "on",
                                        "tldpAuthentication": "off",
                                        "ignoreMtuMismatch": "on",
                                        "reversion": "on",
                                        "peerIp": "10.10.10.10",
                                        "pwId": 10001,
                                        "pwName": "10001_primary",
                                        "pwType": "raw",
                                        "pwConnectivityMode": "spoke",
                                        "mtu": 1500,
                                        "reversionHoldOffTimer": 20,
                                        "pwFlowLabelMode": "off",
                                        "backupPwSettings": {
                                            "pwId": 10002,
                                            "peerIp": "12.12.12.12",
                                            "pwName": "10002_backup"
                                        },
                                        "tunnelType": "default-routing"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ],
                    "node": "5144-10x-205"
                }
            }
        ],
        "name": "PROTECTED-ELINE-PW-HANDOFF",
        "userLabel": "PROTECTED-ELINE-PW-HANDOFF",
        "customerName": "Customer_Ciena",
        "note": {
            "lastUpdatedBy": "admin",

        "ccmInterval": "10ms",
        "maName": "PROTECTED-ELINE-PW-HANDOFF"
    }
}
