Supporting the global profile mode and shared hierarchical policer

The Global profile mode support consists of two parts:

  • Global profile mode support, associated parity support of global profile mode

  • Shared hierarchical metering support

The shared hierarchical metering is the solution proposed for Verizon requirements of hierarchically metering T-Mobile protected (at T-Mobile Network level) access to core connections (E-Line services).

At the access side for Verizon, it currently uses SAOS 6x box 3926. T-Mobile have close to 4 access to the core protected connections. Verizon’s requirement requires that each protected access to core connection should carry traffic up to CIR specified in ingress port parent policer of access node.

Currently, the SAOS 6x box 3926 does not allow summation of child policer CIRs to exceed parent policer CIR. Therefore, the Verizon requirement does not have any straightforward mapping with the SAOS 6x box 3926 NE’s hierarchical metering solution.

You can manage the Shared-Hierarchical Ingress Metering (S-HIM) with the following procedures:

  • Creating E-Line with S-HIM

  • Deleting E-Line with S-HIM

  • Discovering E-Line with S-HIM

  • Modifying E-Line with S-HIM

Creating E-Line with S-HIM

For policer create/update, Navigator MC performs a create/modify operation to update traffic profile on the device.

While creating E-Line, if a parent policer does not already exist it is created in the provisioning workflow.

The E-Line facade creation request is updated, and IngressPolicer has a new attribute meteringType to be used on per service Endpoint basis.

"ingressPolicer": {
"cir": 0,
"eir": 1500000,
"meteringType": "SHARED_HIERARCHICAL"
}

Other than above meteringType input, the customer requires to pass on parent policer CIR as EIR (i.e., service request has CIR =0 , EIR = <Input EIR>).

The system in return creates a parent policer with CIR = <Input EIR> and an E-Line with CIR =0 and EIR = <input EIR>. The system also applies traffic color remarking policy on such S-HIM based E-Line services.

Starting from MCP 5.3, service provisioning is supported on a port with multiple parent policers preconfigured on it. Parent policer management is excluded from service provisioning workflow. User is required to provide parentPolicerName input with meteringType to provision S-HIM service.

"ingressPolicer": {
"cir": 0,
"eir": 1500000,
"meteringType": "SHARED_HIERARCHICAL",
"parentPolicerName: "test_parent"
}
To enable service provisioning with multiple S-HIM instances GCS property 'multiSHIMProvEnabled' needs to set true, to enable this property go to System > Configuration.
Deleting E-Line with S-HIM

A S-HIM based E-Line is deleted the same as a regular E-Line. There are no changes in the Navigator MC interface.

Discovering E-Line with S-HIM

The parent policer information of an S-HIM based service can be found on service Ethernet/Lag layer termination of PTP/FTP.

Proposed changes in PTP Schema:

"parentPolicers": {
         "type": "array",
         "items": {
             "type": "object",
             "$ref": "../parentPolicers.json"
         }
},

Parent Policer Schema:

{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#",
  "title": "Parent Policer",
  "type": "object",
  "javaType": "com.ciena.bp.api.v1.tpe.ParentPolicer",
  "description": "This package stores Parent policer related info.",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Name of the parent policer"
    },
    "cir": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Committed Information rate in kbps of this parent policer"
    },
    "cbs": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Committed burst size of this Policer"
    },
    "adminState": {
      "enum": [
        "enabled",
        "disabled"
      ],
      "description": "Admin state of this parent policer"
    }
  },
  "evcList": {
    "type": "array",
    "description": "List of services attached to the parent policer",
    "items": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "cir",
    "cbs"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}

The parent policer name of a child policer, Operational/Admin state, and meteringType can be found on service CTP’s Ethernet layer termination.

Modifying E-Line with S-HIM

Modifying the EIR of an S-HIM based service request is the same as modifying a regular E-Line service EIR.

"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch" : [ {
"op" : "replace",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/eir",
"value" : 1500000
} ]
},
"interface": "modify"
}
Adding S-HIM policing on an existing regular E-Line
{
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
{
"op": "add",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer",
"value": {
"cir": 0,
"eir": 135,
"meteringType" : "SHARED_HIERARCHICAL"

}
}
]
},
"interface": "modify"
}
parentPolicerName input is required to add S-HIM policing when GCS property 'multiSHIMProvEnabled' is set to true.
Removing S-HIM policing on an existing E-Line
{
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
{
"op": "remove",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer"
}
]
},
"interface": "modify"
}
Attach parent policer to a regular policed E-Line
{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
{
"op": "add",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/meteringType",
"value": "SHARED_HIERARCHICAL"
},
{
"op": "add",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/parentPolicerName",
"value": "test_parent"
}
]
}
}

Removing parent policer from an existing E-Line

{
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
{
"op": "remove",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/meteringType"
},
{
"op": "remove",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/parentPolicerName"
}
]
},
"interface": "modify"
}
Replace parent policer on an existing E-Line
{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
{
"op": "replace",
"path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/parentPolicerName",
"value": "test_parent_new"
}
]
}
}
Modify operation on meteringType and parentPolicerName is not supported when GCS property 'multiSHIMProvEnabled' is set to false.
Auto burst assignment for S-HIM based services

The parent policer CBS is auto-assigned as per regular E-Line auto burst assignment tables provided by the customer. See Provision an E-Line service with burst size auto assignment ---

Provision a PW Handoff Service with tagged CFM on Ethernet Endpoint

Tagged CFM can be enabled on an ethernet endpoint of a PW Handoff service.

To configure PW-Handoff service with tagged cfm configuration on 6500 and 8x devices, GCS property l2AssignHighestClassElementToSmallestVid must be set as true.

To provision, a PW Handoff Service with taggedCFM, use the Market API

Device Support

  • 6500-T, 6500-S PTS - 13.06+

  • SAOS 6x - 6.18+

Feature Description

  • Tagged CFM can be enabled by including "taggedCFM": "enable" in the service endpoint in the service request.

  • Tagged CFM can be enabled on both UNI and ENNI endpoint.

  • On 6x device tagged CFM vlan ID (used on the node) is same as of service vlan Id (CVID or SVID). Applicable for non dual-tag classified service.

  • On 6500 tagged CFM vlan is not explicit. This is because 6500 does not need a specific vlan on the node to enable tagged CFM.

  • In case of ranged/bundle CVID endpoint, lowest VID will be used as CFM vlan id on SAOS 6x device.

  • For dual-tag classified service, inner VID would be used for tagged CFM if the service is configured with single outer and single inner VID and the lowest inner VID would be used for tagged CFM if the service is configured with single outer and ranged inner VID. To configure PW handoff service with a dual-tag classifier, refer to Provision an E-Line Service with dual-tag classifier

  • For services configured with STag push / QTag push, Navigator MC will use push vlan value as CFM tag vid on SAOS 6x device.

  • In case of CVID swapped service endpoint, swapped VID (ingressStampVlanId) would be used as CFM tag vid on SAOS 6x device.

  • SAOS 6x does not support tagged CFM on EPL, Catch-all and Untagged service endpoint if no STag / QTag push is configured.

  • In the discovered TPE data, for 6x endpoint tag-vid, tag-priority and tag-mode attributes will be discovered if tagged cfm is configured with additional tag (STag/QTag/CVID swap). Else, cfm package will have only vlanId. For 6500, vlanId attribute would be synced with value 0 for tagged CFM services.

  • This feature is supported from REST interface only.

Provision a MPLS MC-LAG E-Line service with constraints

To provision, a MC-LAG E-Line Service, use the Market API

Feature Description

  • This feature provides user the ability to provision MC-LAG E-Line service with MPLS/G8032 Constraints

  • Only pure MPLS/G8032 services are allowed with the feature. Spur is not supported with the feature.

  • To support constraints with MC-LAG feature, new roles A_MC_LAG_UNI/ENNI, A_MC_LAG_PRIME_UNI/ENNI, Z_MC_LAG_UNI/ENNI, Z_MC_LAG_PRIME_UNI/ENNI are introduced to identify as MC-LAG constraint request.

  • To identify, whether request for MPLS or G8032, coreTransport is mandatory.

API calls for managing E-LAN services

This section describes the API calls used to retrieve, provision, edit, and delete an E-LAN service.

  • Provision an E-LAN service

  • Add an endpoint to an existing E-LAN service

  • Edit service and endpoint attributes: You can use the same API to edit service and endpoint attributes for an E-Tree, E-LAN, or E-Line service. See Edit service and endpoint attributes.

  • Delete a single endpoint from an existing E-LAN service

  • Delete an E-Tree service: You can use the same API to delete an E-Tree, E-LAN, or E-Line service. See Delete an E-Line service by provisioning intent.

  • Provision an ELAN Service With Untagged Vlan Id and Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

  • Add Endpoint to an existing ELAN Service With Untagged Vlan Id and Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

  • Edit Untagged VLAN Id and Ether Type: You can use the same API to edit service and endpoint attributes for an E-Tree, E-LAN, or E-Line service. See Edit the UNI endpoints of a service

CVID can be given as range or single value ("200-300,545,689,1100-2111") using outerVlanIDRange. Either outervlanIdRange or outerVlanId can be used in provisioning and modification of ELAN service.

Provision an E-LAN service

To provision an E-LAN service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the "serviceType" as required: EVPLAN or EPLAN

Note the following:

  • An E-LAN service can only be created with two endpoints (min and max).

  • An E-LAN service can be created with MCLAG UNI endpoint on G.8032 only.

  • Set "allowQinQSpur" to “true” if you want the E-LAN service to support Q-in-Q spurs (a mix of linear/QinQ and pseudowire paths). Set the value to “false” (as in the above example) if you only want the E-LAN to include MPLS pseudowires.

    This setting cannot be changed when adding endpoints. The E-LAN service will remain with the same constraint settings.

  • Set "coreTransport" to "LINEAR_ONLY" if you want to provision the ELAN service on a linear path.

    If "Any" is set to "coreTransport" then ELAN may be provisioned on a linear path. ELAN service can be provisioned on the linear path in absence of "core transport" in the ELAN provisioning request.
    Navigator MC is not running a loop protection mechanism for ELAN over QinQ services. Loop prevention should be taken up by the user.

  • Core SVID can be explicitly provided instead of using auto calculated core SVID by system.

    properties.coreSvid, to provide a valid core SVID value in range [1-4094]

    If there is no path satisfying the provided core SVID then error message will contain the FIRST and NEXT available vid’s to be used as core SVID.

Specify additional attributes and their values as required.

Add an endpoint to an existing E-LAN service

To add an endpoint to an existing E-LAN service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the Sample response for Provision an E-LAN service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the E-LAN service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

The modify custom operation includes the "resource_properties_jsonpatch" array of objects that are jsonpatch compliant (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902). The “Add endpoint” use case includes:

  • Add operation; “op”: “add”

  • Add to the end of the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array: "/properties/endpoints/-” (the dash character means adding the value to the end of the array identified by the path).

  • The new endpoint value (using the same attributes as for the create request).

{
 "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "add",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
                "value": {
                    "settings": {
                        "node": "87_5783n4",
                        "role": "UNI",
                        "details": [
                            {
                                "flowSettings": [
                                    {
                                        "filter": {
                                            "outerVlanId": [
                                                111
                                            ]
                                        },
                                        "location": {
                                            "slot": "1",
                                            "port": "9"
                                        },
                                        "ingressCosSetting": {
                                            "ingressCosPbit": 7,
                                            "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed"
                                        }
                                    }
                                ]
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                }
            }
        ]
  }
}

Sample response:

Note the following:

  • coreTransport can be added with "ANY" or "LINEAR_ONLY" value in add endpoint request. If "Any" is given then a linear path may come.

  • Routing constraint would be the same as ELAN provisioning request if coreTransport is not given.

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

  • To monitor the outcome of this custom operation you can use the Market REST API:

    GET/resources/{resourceId}/operations/{operationId}

    This retrieves details for a specific operation for a given resource. In this call:

    • {resourceId} is the same as {L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}

    • {operationId} is found in the custom operation response

The response is similar to the initial response of the custom operation. The “state” may now reflect the new status of this custom operation. Refer to Orchestrate custom operation documentation for more details.

{
    "id": "5a0c63de-e89a-4610-9689-4973c24b355a",

                "op": "add",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
                "value": {
                    "settings": {
                        "node": "87_5783n2",
                        "role": "UNI",
                        "details": [
                            {
                                "flowSettings": [
                                    {
                                        "filter": {
                                            "outerVlanId": [
                                                111
                                            ]
                                        },
                                        "location": {
                                            "slot": "1",
                                            "port": "10"
                                        },
                                        "ingressCosSetting": {
                                            "ingressCosPbit": 7,
                                            "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed"
                                        }
                                    }
                                ]
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                }
            }
        ]
    },
    "outputs": {},

Configuring endpoint properties: custom CoS mapping

You can specify a customized CoS mapping to use when adding a new endpoint to an E-LAN service.

You might want to use a customized CoS mapping to rearrange adjacent service provider CoS, or to merge together existing CoS mappings. (For example, on a SAOS 6x platform a PBit of 0 and DEI of 0 are transparently mapped to an internal CoS of 0 and color of 0 in the default map.

You might also want to use a customized mapping to group both PBit 0 and PBit 1, and map them to an internal CoS of 1)

The CoS maps you refer to using this API call must have already been created on the node on which the endpoint resides.

Use the following Market API call to add an endpoint to an E-LAN service that uses a customized CoS mapping:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

For this call, SVC_RSC_ID is the Facade resource ID of the Layer-2 service.

Note in particular the following CoS parameters in the sample call provided below:

"ingressCosSetting": { "ingressCosPolicy": "custom", "ingressCosMapName": "CustomCosMap"

Sample request::

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
        "value": {
          "settings": {
            "node": "87_5783n3",
            "role": "UNI",
            "details": [
              {
                "flowSettings": [
                  {
                    "filter": {
                      "outerVlanId": [
                        1115
                      ]
                    },
                    "location": {
                      "slot": "1",
                      "port": "11"
                    },
		     "ingressCosSetting": {
                         "ingressCosPolicy": "custom",
                         "ingressCosMapName": "CosMap2"
                        }
                    }
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

This will produce a response resembling the following.

                    "settings": {
                        "node": "87_5783n3",
                        "role": "UNI",
                        "details": [
                            {
                                "flowSettings": [
                                    {
                                        "filter": {
                                            "outerVlanId": [
                                                1115

                                        },

                                        },
                                        "ingressCosSetting": {
                                            "ingressCosPolicy": "custom",

                                        }
                                    }

Delete a single endpoint from an existing E-LAN service

You can also use this API call to delete a leaf endpoint from an E-Tree service.

To delete a single endpoint from an existing E-LAN service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the Sample response forProvision an E-LAN service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the E-LAN service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

    GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

This API call involves the same modify custom operation as in the “Add endpoint”. For this “Delete endpoint” use case the following is used:

  • Remove operation; “op”: “remove”

  • The path is used to identify by Index the endpoint object to be removed in the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array.

In the sample request below, 0 means to remove the first endpoint object in the existing “/properties/endpoints“ array.

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "remove",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0"
            }
        ]
  }
}

Sample response:

Note the following:

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

  • To monitor the outcome of this custom operation you can use the Market REST API:

    GET/resources/{resourceId}/operations/{operationId}

    This retrieves details for a specific operation for a given resource. In this call:

    • {resourceId} is the same as {L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}

    • {operationId} is found in the custom operation response

The response is similar to the initial response of the custom operation. The “state” may now reflect the new status of this custom operation. Refer to Orchestrate custom operation documentation for more details.

{
    "id": "5a0c63de-e89a-4610-9689-4973c24b355a",
    "resourceId": "5a0c62cd-657f-45d0-8d01-9511cacf0ca8",
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [{
                "op": "remove",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0",
            }
        ]
    },
    "outputs": {},
    "state": "requested",

Provision an ELAN Service With Untagged Vlan Id and Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

An EVPLAN Service with Untagged VLAN Id and Ether Type is used to PUSH/POP 802.1Q QTag along with Ether Type. This is valid for service with Untagged UNI Endpoint only.

To provision an ELAN service with Untagged Vlan Id classifier on UNI port, use the Market API

Device Support

  • SAOS 6.20+

  • SAOS 8.7+

  • 6500-12.72+

Overview

  • A service with Untagged VLAN Id and Ether Type is valid with UNI Endpoint of Untagged Service

Limitations:

  • Navigator MC does not support service topologies other than ELAN (EVPLAN) with Untagged VLAN Id

Sample request For Dual EndPoint Service

POST {Navigator MC Server}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

To configure an endpoint with Untagged VLAN Id, CVIDS in the EVPLAN service request needs to be set as 4096

              "flowSettings": [
                {
                  "filter": {

  }

Add Endpoint to an existing ELAN Service With Untagged Vlan Id and Ether Type On Uni Endpoint

To add an endpoint to an existing E-LAN service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the Sample response for Provision an E-LAN service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the E-LAN service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

The modify custom operation includes the "resource_properties_jsonpatch" array of objects that are jsonpatch compliant (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902). The “Add endpoint” use case includes:

  • Add operation; “op”: “add”

  • Add to the end of the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array: "/properties/endpoints/-” (the dash character means adding the value to the end of the array identified by the path).

  • The new endpoint value (using the same attributes as for the create request).

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
        "value": {
          "settings": {
            "role": "UNI",
            "details": [
              {
                "flowSettings": [
                  {
                    "filter": {
                      "untaggedDataVid": 11,
                      "ingressEtherType": "88A8",
                      "outerVlanId": [
                        4096
                      ]
                    },
                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                    "location": {
                      "port": "8"
                    }
                  }
                ]
              }
            ],
            "node": "5142s-2_e00201"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/allowQinQSpur",
        "value": false
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

Sample response:

Note the following:

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

  • To monitor the outcome of this custom operation you can use the Market REST API:

    GET/resources/{resourceId}/operations/{operationId}

    This retrieves details for a specific operation for a given resource. In this call:

    • {resourceId} is the same as {L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}

    • {operationId} is found in the custom operation response

The response is similar to the initial response of the custom operation. The “state” may now reflect the new status of this custom operation. Refer to Orchestrate custom operation documentation for more details.

API calls for managing H-VPLS services

This section describes the API calls used to retrieve, provision, edit, and delete an H-VPLS service.

  • Retrieve a discovered/deployed H-VPLS service

  • Retrieve H-VPLS service facade product ID

  • Create an H-VPLS service

  • Edit service and endpoint attributes: You can use this API call for all types of Ethernet services (E-Line, E-LAN, H-VPLS, and E-Tree). See Edit service and endpoint attributes.

  • Delete an H-VPLS service: You can use the same API to delete an E-Tree, E-LAN, H-VPLS, or E-Line service. See Delete an E-Line service by provisioning intent.

  • Add an endpoint to an existing H-VPLS service

  • Delete a single endpoint from an existing H-VPLS service

Retrieve a discovered or deployed H-VPLS service

To retrieve a discovered or deployed H-VPLS service using FRE ID, refer to Retrieve a discovered/planned Ethernet service by FRE ID, including the related TPEs

Retrieve H-VPLS service facade product ID

To retrieve a facade product ID for an H-VPLS service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade. Use this ID as the "product Id" in Create an H-VPLS service

Create an H-VPLS service

To create an H-VPLS service facade, use the Market API.

  • H-VPLS services can either be EVPL or EPL.

  • H-VPLS service should have at least two endpoints.

  • H-VPLS service should have at least one MTU endpoint.

  • H-VPLS service with single-homed MTU should have at least one PE node, other than the Primary PE node.

  • H-VPLS service with dual-homed MTU should have at least one PE node, other than the Primary PE and Backup PE nodes.

  • The maximum number of endpoints in the service is governed by GCS property hvplsProvisioningMaxEndpointCount.

    • The creation of H-VPLS services with only up to 5 endpoints is supported.

  • H-VPLS service provisioning is only supported over static bidirectional MPLS tunnels.

  • Multi-chassis LAG (MC-LAG) as an endpoint is currently not supported.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the productId, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve H-VPLS service facade product ID

A list of H-VPLS-specific parameters and related descriptions.

Table 2. Parameters and description
Parameter Required? Type Description

role

Mandatory

String

The role can either be UNI or ENNI.

endpointRole

Mandatory

String

Represents the role of an endpoint in the service and can either be PE or MTU.

- If the endpoint role is PE (Provider Edge), endpoint level constraints are not applicable.

- If the endpoint role is MTU:

- Primary PE node name is required under the primary section of neighboringNodes for Single-homed MTU.

- Primary PE and Backup PE node names are required under primary and backup sections of neighboringNodes, respectively, for Dual-homed MTU.

- Optional Tunnel constraints are supported only between MTU and the neighboring PE node(s) in an H-VPLS service.

neighboringNodes

Mandatory, if endpointRole is MTU

Object

Represents the primary and backup node names and constraints.

- The primary object under neighboringNodes is mandatory for Single-homed MTU.

- primary and backup objects under neighboringNodes are mandatory for Dual-homed MTU.

nodeName

Mandatory

String

Represents the primary and backup PE neighboring node names of an MTU endpoint node.

constraints

Optional

Object

Constraints under the primary and backup sections of neighboringNodes are the Tunnel constraints.

Tunnel constraints are applicable when Endpoint role is provided as MTU.

Represent tunnels between the MTU and a PE node that would be considered (included/excluded) during path calculation.

The Tunnel name can be provided there along with its inclusion or exclusion constraint.

Tunnel constraints are supported only between MTU and the neighboring PE node(s) in an H-VPLS service.

coreTransport

Mandatory

String

Can only be MPLS for an H-VPLS service

signal

Mandatory

String

Can only be Static for an H-VPLS service

directionality

Mandatory

String

Can only be bidirectional for an H-VPLS service

Add an endpoint to an existing H-VPLS service

To add an endpoint to an existing H-VPLS service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the Sample response for Create an H-VPLS service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the H-VPLS service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

The modify custom operation includes the "resource_properties_jsonpatch" array of objects that are jsonpatch compliant (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902). The “Add endpoint” use case includes:

  • Add operation; “op”: “add”

  • Add to the end of the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array: "/properties/endpoints/-” (the dash character means adding the value to the end of the array identified by the path).

  • The new endpoint value (using the same attributes as for the create request).

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
        "value": {
          "settings": {
            "role": "UNI",
            "details": [
              {
                "flowSettings": [
                  {
                    "filter": {
                      "outerVlanId": [
                        56
                      ]
                    },
                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                    "location": {
                      "port": "17"
                    }
                  }
                ],
                "neighboringNodes": {
                  "primary": {
                    "nodeName": "5164-10x-212"
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "endpointRole": "MTU",
            "node": "5162-10x-209"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

Delete a single endpoint from an existing H-VPLS service

To delete a single endpoint from an existing H-VPLS service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the Sample response for Create an H-VPLS service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the H-VPLS service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

    GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

This API call involves the same modify custom operation as in the “Add endpoint”. For this “Delete endpoint” use case the following is used:

  • Remove operation; “op”: “remove”

  • The path is used to identify by Index the endpoint object to be removed in the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array.

In the sample request below, 3 means to remove the fourth endpoint object in the existing “/properties/endpoints“ array.

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "remove",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/3"
            }
        ]
  }
}

Sample response:

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

  • To monitor the outcome of this custom operation you can use the Market REST API:

    GET/resources/{resourceId}/operations/{operationId}

    This retrieves details for a specific operation for a given resource. In this call:

    • {resourceId} is the same as {L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}

    • {operationId} is found in the custom operation response

The response is similar to the initial response of the custom operation. The “state” may now reflect the new status of this custom operation. Refer to Orchestrate custom operation documentation for more details.

API calls for managing E-Tree services

This section describes the API calls used retrieve, provision, edit, and delete an E-Tree service.

  • Provision an E-Tree service

  • Add a leaf endpoint to an existing E-Tree service

  • Edit service and endpoint attributes: You can use the same API to edit service and endpoint attributes for an E-Tree, E-LAN, or E-Line service. See Edit service and endpoint attributes.

  • Delete an E-Tree service: You can use the same API to delete an E-Tree, E-LAN, or E-Line service. See Delete an E-Line service by provisioning intent.

CVID can be given as range or single value ("200-300,545,689,1100-2111") using outerVlanIDRange. Either outervlanIdRange or outerVlanId can be used in provisioning and modification of E-Tree service.

Provision an E-Tree service

To provision an E-Tree service, use the Market API.

This section includes the following topics for creating an E-Tree service over static MPLS transport with SS-PW/MS-PW, G8032(with or without QinQ Spurs) and pure QinQ.

  • Provision a single-root E-Tree service

  • Provision a dual-root E-Tree service

  • Provision a dual-root ENNI hairpin E-Tree service

  • Provision an E-Tree service with PFG(Private-Forwarding-Group) enabled.

    A dual-root E-Tree service is on the same node.

E-Tree services are supported on the following devices:

  • 6.x (leaf or root)

PFG would be ignored if E-Tree is configured with an enabled Private forwarding group and transport is MPLS.

E-Tree provisioning and adding endpoint over G.8032 (with or without QinQ Spurs) or pure QinQ would be blocked for 6x devices if the same UNI/ENNI/INNI ports that have opposite PFG roles are already configured.

  • 8700 (leaf or root)

  • 6500 Packet Fabric, eMOTR / eMOTR Edge (leaf or root)

6500 L2MOTR cannot be used as root or leaf if E-Tree is configured with enabled Private forwarding group.

  • SAOS 10.7.x+ DNX (leaf or root)

For 10.x XGS devices, PFG would be ignored if E-Tree is provisioned with Private forwarding group and transport is MPLS.

E-Tree Provisioning/Add Endpoint operation would be blocked for 10.x XGS devices, if E-Tree is provisioned with Private forwarding group and transport is G.8032 (with or without QinQ Spurs), and pure QinQ.
An E-Tree service can only be created for a single root with a leaf, or a dual root with a leaf. After you have created an E-Tree service, you can add more leaf endpoints to the service. See Add a leaf endpoint to an existing E-Tree service.
AN ENNI hairpin ETREE service can not have root on SAOS 6x.
AN ENNI hairpin ETREE leaf can be configured with stag push/pop.
Provision a single-root E-Tree service

Sample request:

POST {{Navigator MC Server}}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the endpointRole "ROOT" or endpointRole "LEAF" for a single-root E-Tree service.

Also, select the attributes and values, as applicable.

The following is an example of an E-Tree service with a single root and a single leaf on 8700 on a single tunnel (SS-PW). The same API applies to both single tunnel (SS-PW) and multiple tunnels (MS-PW). 
{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serviceType": "EVPTREE",
        "name": "etree_1R_1L",
        "userLabel": "ETree_1Root_1Leaf",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n7",
                    "role": "UNI",
                    "endpointRole": "ROOT",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            762
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "location": {
                                        "slot": "1",
                                        "port": "8"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                   "node": "87_5783n8",
                    "role": "UNI",
                    "endpointRole": "LEAF",
                    "details": [
                        {

Provision a dual-root E-Tree service

Sample request:

POST {{Navigator MC Server}}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the endpointRole "ROOT" or endpointRole "LEAF" for a dual-root E-Tree service.

For a dual-root E-Tree service, you must specify two instances of "endpointRole" "ROOT". Both roots must be on the same node but on different ports.

Specify additional attributes and their values as required.

The following is an example of an E-Tree service with dual roots and a single leaf on 8700 on a single tunnel (SS-PW). The same API applies to both single tunnel (SS-PW) and multiple tunnels (MS-PW).

Provision an ENNI hairpin E-Tree service

For a dual-root E-Tree ENNI hairpin service, specify two instancFor a dual-root E-Tree ENNI hairpin service, specify two instances of endpointRole "ROOT" and "role" "ENNI_HAIRPIN". Both roots must be on the same node and same ports. Dual-root ENNI hairpin Etree service can be configured on the local switch as well i.e. both root and leaf endpoint can be on the same node.

Specify additional attributes and their values as required.

ENNI hairpin root endpoint can be configured on SAOS8x, 6500-S Packet Fabric and SAOS 10x DNS.
ENNI hairpin is not supported on 6500 EMOTR, 6500 L2MOTR, SAOS 6.x and SAOS 10.x XGS.
ENNI hairpin ETREE service can only be configured on MPLS transport only.

The following are examples of Provisioning an E-Tree service.

Sample request for provisioning an ENNI hairpin E-Tree over MPLS transport:

    "fallback": false,
    "transportProtection": "MPLS_ONLY",
    "interactive_mode": "false",
    "endpoints": [

        "settings": {
          "role": "ENNI_HAIRPIN",

          "ccmTransmitEnabled": true,

              "flowSettings": [

                      324

Provision an E-Tree service with PFG enabled

Specify the endpointRole "ROOT" or endpointRole "LEAF", pfgRole "Root" or "Leaf" and pfgEnabled attribute as "true" for E-Tree service.

For a dual-root E-Tree service, specify two instances of endpointRole "ROOT". Both roots must be on the same node but on different ports.

Specify additional attributes and their values as required.

For 6.x/10.x XGS devices PFG value is ignored on MPLS transport as PFG with MPLS attachment is not supported on 6.x/10.x XGS devices.

10.x XGS devices can only be used as intermittent node in E-Tree Service over G.8032 (with or without QinQ Spurs), and pure QinQ

Add a leaf endpoint to an existing E-Tree service

This section includes the following topics:

  • Add a leaf endpoint with a node exclusion constraint, which includes the following samples: Facade request and response, and an Intent request and response.

  • Add a leaf endpoint with a tunnel inclusion constraint, which includes the following samples: Facade request and response, and an Intent request and response.

  • Add a leaf endpoint with PFG enabled on MPLS, G8032(with or without QinQ Spurs), Pure QinQ, which includes the following samples: Facade request.

To add a leaf endpoint to an existing E-Tree service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{(FACADE_RESOURCE_ID)}/operations

Specify the following attributes:

  • FACADE_RESOURCE_ID

    The FACADE_RESOURCE_ID is the resource ID that was returned when the service was created. (For an example, see the id in the sample response for Provision an E-Tree service.)

    If you did not capture the FACADE_RESOURCE_ID when you provisioned the E-Tree service, you can retrieve it using query-by-name (using the management name) for any given L2 facade resources:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?q=properties.name%3A{MANAGEMENT_NAME}&resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade

The modify custom operation includes the "resource_properties_jsonpatch" array of objects that are jsonpatch compliant (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902). The “Add leaf endpoint” use case includes:

  • Add operation “op”: “add”

  • Add to the end of the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade resource endpoints array: "/properties/endpoints/-” (the dash character means adding the value to the end of the array identified by the path).

  • The new endpoint value (same attributes as for the provision E-Tree request).

Note the following:

  • the "endpointRole" attribute in inputs.resource_properties_jsonpatch[0].value.settings with LEAF value

  • the "routingConstraints" attribute in inputs.resource_properties_jsonpatch[0]:

    • To allow routing constraint by explicit inclusion or exclusion of LSP (tunnel) name for the new E-Tree path between the existing root(s) and the added LEAF endpoint.

    • To allow routing constraint by explicit inclusion or exclusion of node (NE) name for the new E-Tree path between the existing root(s) and the added LEAF endpoint.

Add a leaf endpoint with PFG enabled on MPLS, G8032(with or without QinQ Spurs) and pure QinQ

  • Adding a leaf

    • If PFG is enabled on the E-Tree service, A new leaf endpoint can be added on the existing Leaf node/New Node/Root Node.

    • PFG Role as Root can only be given for new leaf endpoint on MPLS transport.

    • For Dual Node ENNI Hairpin Etree services, a new leaf endpoint can be added:

      • On the existing Leaf and same port.

      • On the existing Leaf and different port.

      • On new node

    • For Local Switch ENNI Hairpin Etree services, a new leaf endpoint can be added:

      • On the same node and different port.

    A user cannot add a leaf endpoint on a new node if E-Tree is configured with enabled PFG and transport is G.8032(with or without QinQ spurs) or pure QinQ. NOTE: A ENNI hairpin service can not have multiple ENNI Leaf on the same port. An ENNI hairpin service cannot have multiple interface types as leaf on the same node and the same port.

Sample request for Adding leaf in E-Tree service over MPLS

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
        "value": {
          "settings": {
            "role": "UNI",
            "endpointRole": "LEAF",
            "pfgRole":"Leaf",
            "details": [
              {
                "flowSettings": [
                  {
                    "filter": {
                      "outerVlanId": [
                        565
                      ]
                    },
                    "controlFrameTunneling": "disabled",
                    "location": {
                      "slot": "3",
                      "port": "15"
                    }
                  }
                ]
              }
            ],
            "node": "87m_0003"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/constraints",
        "value": {
          "transport": {
            "directionality": "bidirectional"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

Note the following:

  • As with all Orchestrate custom operations, “state” provides the server processing status of the custom operation.

  • To monitor the outcome of this custom operation you can use the Market REST API:

    GET/resources/{resourceId}/operations/{operationId}

    THis retrieves details for a specific operation for a given resource. In this call:

  • {resourceId} is the same as {L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}

  • {operationId} is found in the custom operation response

The response is similar to the initial response of the custom operation. The “state” may now reflect the new status of this custom operation. Refer to Orchestrate custom operation documentation for more details.

Edit existing etree service

This section includes the following topics:

  • Edit E-Tree sevice over mpls, which includes the following samples: Facade request.

Modification of PFG attribute is blocked on E-Tree over G8032(with or without QinQ Spurs) and pure QinQ.
Edit E-Tree service over MPLS

PFG Modification-Enable: The user can enable PFG on the service level without explicit values of PFG at the endpoint level.

For Root Node, the default value of PFG role is Root and for Leaf Node, the default value is Leaf NOTE: For ENNI hairpin ETREE, cvid swapping is not allowed on leaf endpoint.

Sample request to enable PFG with default values of pfgRole at each endpoint.

{
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [

            {
                "path": "/properties/pfgEnabled",
                "op": "add/replace",
                "value":true

            }
        ]
    },
    "interface": "modify"
}

Sample Request to enable PFG with explict value of pfgRole at each endpoint level.

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/pfgEnabled",
        "op": "add/replace",
        "value": true
      },
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/pfgRole",
        "value": "Root/Leaf"
      },
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/pfgRole",
        "value": "Root/Leaf"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

PFG Modification-Disable : If PFG is disabled on the service level, then PFG will be disabled only on the service level(VS/FD). There would not be any change in the value of PFG on the endpoint level.

Sample request

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/pfgEnabled",
        "op": "replace/remove",
        "value": false
      }
    ]
  }
  "interface": "modify"
}

PFG modification on endpoint level: The User would be able to modify the endpoint’s PFG Role for each service endpoint.

  • Validations

    • Validations would be applied on the PFG role by Navigator NCS. Error would be thrown for invalid PFG role configuration for all devices.

    • For 6.x/10.x XGS devices, PFG role modification would be applied only on Facade Resource. No changes would be done on Node.

Sample request

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/pfgRole",
        "value": "Root/Leaf"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

API calls for provisioning E-Access and E-Transit services

This section describes the API calls used to provision E-Access and E-Transit services:

  • Provision unprotected E-Access EVPL COS MPLS protected/unprotected tunnels with/without QinQ spurs

  • Provision unprotected E-Access EPL COS MPLS protected/unprotected tunnels with/without QinQ spurs

  • Provision E-Access E-Line services

  • Provision E-Transit E-Line services

CVID can be given as range or single value ("200-300,545,689,1100-2111") using outerVlanIDRange. Either outervlanIdRange or outerVlanId can be used in provisioning and modification of E-Access and E-Transit service.

Provision unprotected E-Access EVPL COS MPLS protected/unprotected tunnels with/without QinQ spurs

To provision an E-Access EVPL service over MPLS transport between two 8700 nodes using the default CoS Policy mapping with UNI CVID of 780 and ENNI SVID of 2794 (no CVID swapping supported) and ETHERTYPE = 88A8, use the Market API.

For the related Sample request and Sample response bodies, see Provision E-Access E-Line services.

Provision E-Access E-Line services

To provision E-Access E-Line services, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

You must specify the following attributes:

  • under "endpoints" in the first "settings" section, include: "role": "A_UNI"

  • under "endpoints" in the second "settings" section, include: "role": "Z_ENNI"

A_UNI and Z_ENNI are keywords used specifically for E-Access services

Below is an example of configuring an E-Access EVPL service using linear QinQ transport.

        "lastTransition": "TRANSITION_NONE",
        "interactive_mode": "false",
        "linearOnly": false,
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "oamEnabled": false,
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87c_0008",

                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            3512
                                        ]
                                    },

                                    "location": {
                                        "slot": "2",
                                        "port": "16"
                                     },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "L2PcpCos"

Provision E-Transit E-Line services

To provision E-Transit E-Line services, use the Market API.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Below is an example of configuring an E-Transit service for a SAOS 6.x EVPL service with only QinQ transport.

You must specify the following attributes:

  • under "endpoints" in the first "settings" section, include "role": "A_ENNI"

  • under "endpoints" in the second "settings" section, include: "role": "Z_ENNI"

  • to limit the supporting infrastructure to QinQ only: "linearOnly:true"

A_ENNI and Z_ENNI are keywords used specifically for E-Transit services

Above services can be provisioned with service names upto 50 characters for 6500 (15.0+)/10x(10.6.1+) devices and upto 47 characters for 6x(6.21.1+) devices. In the case of CFM-enabled services, If ma-name is given by the user then the max length of ma-name should be 31 characters for 6500 (15.0+) and 41 characters for 10x(10.6.1+)/6x(6.21.1+) otherwise ma-name would be truncated according to minimum length supported by a device among service endpoint devices.
To retrieve information, use the NSI getTPE/getFRE REST API (see Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management.

API calls for managing TDM packet services

This section describes the API calls used manage TDM services using packet transport:

  • Retrieve unprotected E1 TDM CEM over static MPLS (CES endpoints)

  • Retrieve unprotected unchannelized E1 PDH CEM service over static MPLS (3932)

  • Retrieve unprotected STS-1 TDM CEM over static MPLS (6500 PTS endpoints)

  • Retrieve an STS1 TDM CEM In/Out Local Switch Service (6500 PTS endpoints)

  • Retrieve a DS1 TDM endpoint (6500 PTS endpoints)

  • Create a TDM PTS endpoint resource

  • Create a PTS TDM service

  • Delete a PTS TDM service

  • Create/delete unprotected E1 TDM CEM service over static MPLS (CES endpoints)

  • Create/delete unprotected unchannelized E1 PDH CEM over static MPLS

  • Create/delete TDM CEM service over Dynamic Bidirectional Co-routed LSP (6500 13.3+ endpoints)

  • Create/delete TDM Eline interop service between 6500 PTS and 3926m with 16E1/DS1 FRU

  • Create/delete TDM Eline interop service between 6500 PTS and 3926m/3928m/5142m/5160m with TDM2GE SFP

  • Create/delete TDM Eline interop service between 6500 PTS and 3926m/3928m/5142m/5160m with GES101 SFP

Retrieve unprotected E1 TDM CEM over static MPLS

You can use the Navigator MC API to discover and inventory an STM-1 channelized E1 TDM CEM service using MEF8 over static MPLS. This allows you to packetize your PDH traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To discover and inventory the E1 TDM CEM service, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "layerRate" as E1 and include TPEs in the request:

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/fres?layerRate=E1&type=service&include=tpes

Retrieve unprotected unchannelized E1 PDH CEM service over static MPLS (3926m, 3932)

You can use the Navigator MC API to discover and inventory an unprotected, unchannelized E1 PDH CEM service (with CES endpoints) using MEF8 over static MPLS bi-directional, co-routed LSP. This allows you to packetize your PDH traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To discover and inventory the E1 PDH CEM service, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "layerRate" as E1 and include TPEs in the request:

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?layerRate=E1&type=service&include=tpes

Retrieve unprotected STS-1 TDM CEM over static MPLS (6500 PTS endpoints)

You can use the Navigator MC API to discover and inventory an OC-N channelized STS-1 TDM CEM service (with 6500 PTS) using CEP over Static MPLS. This allows you to packetize your TDM traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To discover and inventory the STS-1 TDM CEM service, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v4/search//fres

Specify the "layerRate" as STS-1 and include TPEs in the request:

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?layerRate=STS1&type=service&include=tpes

Retrieve an STS1 TDM CEM In/Out Local Switch Service (6500 PTS)

You can use the Navigator MC API to discover and inventory a Local Switch STS-1 TDM CEM service (with 6500 PTS). This allows you to packetize your TDM traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To discover and inventory the Local Switch STS-1 TDM CEM service, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "layerRate" as STS-1 and include PTEs in the request:

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?layerRate=STS1&type=service&include=tpes

Retrieve a DS1 TDM endpoint (6500 PTS)

You can use the Navigator MC API to discover and inventory a DS1 TDM endpoint on 6500 PTS, which allows you to packetize TDM traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To query a discovered and inventoried DS1 TDM endpoint, use the Port inventory (TPEs) API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v6/tpes

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/v6/tpes?id=267de837-45d6-3fe9-9528-e19a6765b481::TPE_1-1S1-1_D1P1_PTP_DS1_CTPServerToClient

Query all TPEs, or specify the ID of a TPE that may have been included in the response to a service FRE query:

https://<hostname>/nsi/api/v6/tpes

Create a TDM PTS endpoint resource

To create a TDM PTS endpoint resource, use the Market API.

You must create a TDM PTS endpoint before you create any PTS TDM service.
In MCP 3.0, for PTS TDM services, omit the top-level endpoints.
Packet Mapping can be provided in the endpoint creation request. It is not a mandatory attribute. Supported values are MEF3, MEF8, CEP, SATOP and CESOPSN.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the product ID for each resource type and any other required attributes.

For details on the PDH card, see Create a TDM PTS endpoint resource on a PDH card.

{
    "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.TDMPTSEndpoint",
    "label": "SIM5:Port9_S1P2-VGP1-V2P1-E1P1",
    "properties": {
        "neName": "SIM5",
        "port": "1-2-9",
        "channel": "S1P2-VGP1-V2P1-E1P1",
        "jitterBuffer": 2,
        "clockRecoveryMode": "INTERNAL",
        "rtpSetting": "ON",
        "packetMapping": "SATOP"
    },
    "productId": "5bbcbf7d-1179-4419-9e8a-8dde8240aa76"
}

Sample response:

{
    "id": "5c4876c4-8f20-47b9-8a90-958b3f2a5ae3",

After you have created a TDM PTS endpoint, make sure you resynchronize the network elements.

You can then create the TDM PTS service.

Create a TDM PTS endpoint resource on a PDH card

When provisioning a TDMPTSEndpoint resource on a PDH card, the subslot must be included in the port field in the following format as follows:

<shelf>-<slot>S<subslot>-<port>

For example,

1-3S2-9

where 3 is the slot and 2 is the subslot.

Create a PTS TDM service

To create a PTS TDM service, use the Market API.

For a Local Switched TDM, make sure that the TDM endpoints exist on the same network element and are pre-provisioned. You must create a TDM PTS endpoint before you create any PTS TDM service.

See Create a TDM PTS endpoint resource.

To provision PTS TDM over pseudowire, make sure that two distinct network elements are selected.

In MCP 3.0, for PTS TDM services, omit top-level endpoints.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the required attributes in the following TDMServiceIntentFacadeRequest.

For details on the PDH card, see Create a PTS TDM service on a PDH card.

{

    "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.TDMServiceIntentFacade",
    "productId": "5bbcbf7d-1179-4419-9e8a-8dde8240aa76",
    "properties": {
        "serverTrailList": [],

        "turnUpDateTime": "2117-11-19T11:37:29.739",
        "tdm": {
            "endPoints": [
                {
                    "signalIndex": "S1P1",
                    "shelf": "1",
                    "networkElement": {
                        "name": "SIM5"
                    },
                    "port": "13",
                    "slot": "2"
                },
                {
                    "signalIndex": "S1P1",
                    "shelf": "1",
                    "networkElement": {
                        "name": "SIM5"
                    },
                    "port": "12",
                    "slot": "2"
                }
            ],
            "layerRate": "STS1"
        },
        "endpoints": [],

        },
        "structure": "P2P",

        "linearOnly": false,

    }
}

For CEM TDM DS0 layer rate services, "signalIndex" would be "<channel path>::<comma separated values of channel numbers>" (i.e. "D3P1-D2P1-D1P1::1,2,4,5") and "layerRate" would be "DS0". Each entity of comma separated value denotes the channel number ranging from 1 to 24 for DS0 layer rate. Specifying all the channel numbers is mandatory else there would be mismatch in service as it is used in ID generation.
Create a PTS TDM service on a PDH card

When provisioning a TDM PTS service using the TDMServiceIntentFacade on a PDH card, the subslot must be included in the slot field of the relevant tdm.endPoints object in the following format:

<slot>S<subslot>

For example,

3S2

where 3 is the slot and 2 is the subslot.

Delete a PTS TDM service

To delete a PTS TDM service, use the Market API.

To delete a TDM service, you must delete the

  • TDMServiceIntentFacade resource, and

  • TDMPTSEndpoint

Sample request:

Specify the required resource ID.

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/market/api/v1/resources/{resource_id}

A successful delete request returns code 204 no content.

Create/delete unprotected E1 TDM CEM service over static MPLS (CES endpoints)

You can use the Navigator MC API to create (and delete) an unprotected E1 TDM CEM service over Static MPLS (unprotected PW and 2-endpoint protected PW) using CES devices as endpoint nodes employing AimValley CSoP Smart SFPs.

You can aggregate TDM CEM E1s at an aggregation node and hand off individual E1s or an STM-1, to be able to packetize your TDM/PDH traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet-based network.

To create (and delete) the E1 TDM CEM service, use the Market API.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Note the following TDM specific parameters used in the sample request below:

Path: properties/tdm/layerRate
Value: “E1”
Path: properties/tdm/endpoints
   Subpath: networkElement/Name
   Value: <Node Name>
   Subpath: port
   Value: <port name>
   Subpath: signalIndex
   Value: <signal index on SFP>
Path: properties/endpoints/settings/details/flowSettings/filter/outerVlanId
Value: Int range(1-4094)
Path: properties/endpoints/settings/details/flowSettings/location/port
Value: “FTP”

Create/delete unprotected unchannelized E1 PDH CEM over static MPLS

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to create an unprotected, unchannelized E1 PDH CEM service (with CES endpoints) using MEF8 over Static MPLS bi-directional, co-routed CAC based LSP. This allows you to packetize your PDH traffic and realize the benefits of using a packet based-network.

You can use the same methods described here to create and delete TDM CEM E1 or DS1 (using MEF8) unchannelized services, or E0/DS0 channelized services with endpoints on 3926 and 3932 devices running SAOS 6.17 or higher. The 3926 does not support specifying clock-mode.

To create (and delete) the E1 PDH CEM service, use the Market API.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Note the following TDM specific parameters used in the sample request below:

  • Path: properties/tdm/layerRate

    • Value: “E1”

  • Path: properties/tdm/endpoints

    • Subpath: networkElement/Name

  • Value: <Node Name>

    • Subpath: port

    • Value: <port name>

  • Path: properties/endpoints/settings/details/flowSettings/filter/outerVlanId

  • Value: Int range(1-4094)

  • Path: properties/endpoints/settings/details/flowSettings/location/port

  • Value: “FTP”

  • reuseExistingPseudowire

    • Supported values: true|false

  • tdmCosSettings: pcp

    • Supported values: INT(0:7)

  • rtpSetting

    • Supported values: ON|OFF

  • clockRecoveryMode

    • Supported values: INTERNAL|ADAPTIVE|DIFFERENTIAL|RECOVERED

  • jitterBuffer

    • Supported values: INT(2:32)

  • syncFreqProtGroup

    • Supported values: This parameter should either be included, not included, or set to the name of an existing "port tdm sync frequency protection-group" entry on the device. The "group_name" value can be any string. It must correspond to a protection-group configured on the device.

    If required, consult the CES device documentation for help creating the protection group.

Sample request:

{

Create/delete TDM CEM service over Dynamic Bidirectional Co-routed LSP (6500 13.3+ endpoints)

As a provisioning user, you want to create (and delete) a TDM CEM service over Dynamic Bidirectional Co-routed LSP using 6500 PTS as endpoint nodes. You can create TDM Services PTS to PTS only over Dynamic Bidirectional Co-routed LSPs with below rates:

  • DS1 to DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS1 → DS0 to DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

  • DS3 to DS3 (SAToP)

  • Channelized OC-3

    • STS-1 (CEP)

    • STS-3c (CEP)

    • STS-1 → DS3 (SAToP)

    • STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 (SAToP)

    • STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

To create (and delete) the service, use the Market API

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample Request
{
  "productId": "{{L2_SVC_TDM_PRODUCT_ID}}",

    "allowQinQSpur": true,
    "reuseExistingPseudowire": false,
    "profiles": [],
    "serverTrailList": [],
    "interactive_mode": "false",
    "endpoints": [],
    "globalDiversity": {
      "diversityLevel": "LINK_DIVERSE",
      "selectionCriteria": "MANDATORY"
    },
    "tdm": {
      "endPoints": [
        {
          "networkElement": {
            "name": "{{NAME_6500_M}}"
          },
          "signalIndex": "{{signalIndex}}",
          "shelf": "7",
          "slot": "1S1",
          "port": "1"

          "port": "1"

      "layerRate": "{{layerRate}}"

  }
}

For signalIndex value refer "channel" value on specific TDM port

Sample reference for signalIndex values is described in table below:

Table 3. Sample signalIndex values:
Channel Rate signalIndex

DS1(SAToP)

D1P1

DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

D1P1::1,2,4,5

DS3(SAToP)

D3P1

STS-1 (CEP)

S1P1

STS-3c (CEP)

S3P1

STS-1 → DS3 (SAToP)

S1P1-D3P1

STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 (SAToP)

S1P1-D3P1-D2P1-D1P1

STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

S1P1-D3P1-D2P1-D1P1::1,2,4,5

Limitations

  1. PW control word, PW flow Label and TLDP is not supported on TDM service

  2. Edit is not supported for TDM services, except customer, note, tag field

Create/delete TDM Eline interop service between 6500 PTS and 3926m with 16E1/DS1 FRU

As a provisioning user, you want to create (and delete) a TDM Eline interop service between 6500 PTS and 3926m as endpoint nodes. This service can be created over Static and Dynamic Bidirectional Co-routed LSPs with the below rates:

  • DS1 to DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

  • DS1 to DS3 → M13 → DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to DS3 → M13 → DS1 → DS0 (CESOPSN)

  • DS1 to EC-1 → STS1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to EC-1 → STS1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 → DS0 (CESOPSN)

  • DS1 to EC-1 → STS1 → VT1.5 → DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to EC-1 → STS1 → VT1.5 → DS1 → DS0 (CESOPSN)

  • DS1 to OC-n → STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to OC-n → STS-1 → DS3 → M13 → DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

  • DS1 to OC-n → STS-1 → VT1.5 → DS1 (SAToP)

  • DS0 to OC-n → STS-1 → VT1.5 → DS1 → DS0 (CESoPSN)

To create (and delete) the service, use the Market API

  • TDM E-Line service can be provisioned with the minimum length supported by a device among service endpoints for the service name. i.e 6x(>=6.21.4)-6x(>=6.21.4): up to 47 characters, 6x(<6.21.4)-6x(<6.21.4): up to 15 characters, 6x(<6.21.4)-6x(>=6.21.4): up to 15 characters, 6500-6500: up to 40 characters, 6x(>=6.21.4)-6500: up to 40 characters, 6x(<6.21.4)-6500: up to 15 characters.
