API calls for managing Drop-and-continue services

This section describes the API calls used to retrieve, provision, edit, and delete a Multicast Drop-and-continue service.

  • Create a Drop-and-continue service

  • Add a service endpoint to a Drop-and-continue service

  • Delete a service endpoint from a Drop-and-continue service

  • Delete a Drop-and-continue service

Create a Drop-and-continue service

You can use the REST API to create a Drop-and-continue service (either an EPDC or EVPD).

The API calls described below allow you to create an initial drop-and-continue service consisting of a single Source port and a single Drop port. You can then add further endpoints to the service using additional API calls.

Navigator MC supports the creation of drop-and-continue services with endpoints on the following devices:

  • SAOS 6.x

  • 8700

Use the Market API to create a Drop-and-continue service. The body of the call is similar to other services supported in Navigator MC.

For the "serviceType" parameter, use either "EVPDC" or "EPDC".

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample service-create body

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "serverTrailList": [],
        "serviceType": "EVPDC",
        "name": "NRMCEVC3",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "3930-25",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            2092
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                                        "ingressCosPbit": 3
                                    },
                                    "ingressPolicer": {
                                                "cir": 1000,
                                                "eir": 100,
                                                        "ebs": 128,
                                                        "cbs": 128
                                     },
                                    "location": {
                                        "port": "6"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "8700-4",
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                    "filter": {
                                        "outerVlanId": [
                                            2092
                                        ]
                                    },
                                    "ingressCosSetting": {
                                        "ingressCosPolicy": "fixed",
                                        "ingressCosPbit": 3
                                    },
                                    "ingressPolicer": {
                                                "cir": 1000,
                                                "eir": 100,
                                                "ebs": 128,
                                                "cbs": 128
                                     },
                                    "location": {
                                        "slot": "2",
                                        "port": "10"
                                    }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ],
        "primaryPathConstraints": {
              "includeRouteObjects": [{
                        "constraintType": "HARD",
                        "locations": [{
                                "lspName": "2535-UNP",
                                "nodeName": "3930-25"
                            }
                        ],
                        "objectType": "LSP_NAME"
                    }
                ]
        },
        "transportProtection": "MPLS_ONLY"
    }
}

Add a service endpoint to a Drop-and-continue service

You can use the REST API to add an endpoint to a Drop-and-continue service.

Navigator MC supports the creation of drop-and-continue endpoints on the following devices:

  • SAOS 6.x

  • 8700

Use the Market API POST request to add an endpoint to a Drop-and-continue service.

The "attachmentSource" is a node that is already a member of the Drop-and-continue service, and from which this new endpoint will receive the service traffic.

For a protected Drop-and-continue service, you can include a second attachmentSource on another node that is participating in the Drop-and-continue service.

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

Sample add-drop-point body

{
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "add",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/-",
                "value": {
                    "settings": {
                        "node": "5142-19",
                        "role": "A_UNI",
                        "attachmentSource" : {
                            "primary" : {
                                "networkElement" : {
                                    "name" : "8700-4"
                                }
                            }
                        },
                        "details": [
                            {
                                "flowSettings": [
                                    {
                                        "filter": {
                                            "outerVlanId": [
                                                561
                                            ]
                                        },
                                        "location": {
                                            "port": "1"
                                        }
                                    }
                                ]
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}

Delete a service endpoint from a Drop-and-continue service

You can use the REST API to remove an endpoint from a Drop-and-continue service.

Use the Market API POST request to remove an endpoint from the service.

The "attachmentSource" is a node that is already a member of the Drop-and-continue service, and from which this new endpoint will receive the service traffic.

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

The path/properties/endpoints/<number> parameter in this call identifies the endpoint you want to remove from the service.

In the following example, endpoint number 2 will be removed by the operation.:

"path": "/properties/endpoints/2":

Endpoint numbering is zero-indexed. If a service includes three endpoints, to remove the third end point you should identify it as "2", not "3".

Sample remove-drop-point body

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "remove",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/2"
            }
        ],
        "modifySubOperation" : "REMOVE_UNI"
  }
}

Delete a Drop-and-continue service

You can use the REST API to delete a Drop-and-continue service.

Use the Market API to delete a Drop-and-continue service. The body of the call is similar to other services supported in Navigator MC.

For the "serviceType" parameter, use either "EVPDC" or "EPDC".

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}

API calls for managing PON services

Navigator MC supports the two flavours for PON service management, one for General Market service providers and the other for a specific Tier-1 service provider. This is controlled by a GCS property pon.generalMarket.

  • PON service management for General Market service providers

  • PON service management for a specific Tier-1 service provider

PON service management for General Market service providers

This section describes the API calls used to provision a PON service or perform different operations on a PON service.

  • Retrieve a discovered/deployed PON service

  • Retrieve PON service facade product ID

  • Create a PON service

  • Edit a PON service

  • Delete a PON service

  • Only configured or registered ONUs are applicable for PON service provisioning.

  • Navigator MC supports the creation of PON services with endpoints on SAOS 10.x 10.6+ devices.

  • PON residential services are supported from SAOS 10.x 10.7+ devices.

  • Following constructs should already be pre-provisioned and available for PON service provisioning.

    • SLA Profiles.

    • ONU and ONU UNI ports.

    • RADIUS and DHCP.

  • For a PON EPL service provisioning case, vlan can be set via the below two GCS properties. Based on the PON application i.e. business or residential, you can update these properties accordingly. Their default value is 65535.

    • businessPonEplVlanId

    • residentialPonEplVlanId

Retrieve a discovered or deployed PON service

To retrieve a discovered or deployed a PON service using FRE ID, refer Retrieve a discovered / planned Ethernet service by FRE ID, including the related TPEs

Retrieve PON service facade product ID

To retrieve a facade product ID for a PON service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade. Use this ID as the "product Id" in Create a PON service

Create a PON service

A PON service can be of two types:

  • Business PON Service

  • Residential PON service

Both of the above service types share the same facade body structure except in the case of a residential PON service, you will be required to provide the below mandatory attributes in the request:

  • DHCP remote ID

  • DHCP circuit ID

  • NAS identifier

  • NAS port ID

  • NAS username override

To create a PON service facade, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the productId, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve PON service facade product ID

A list of PON specific parameters and related descriptions.

Table 4. Parameters and description
Parameter Required? Type Description

productId

Mandatory

String

Product ID for a PON service facade. (Retrieved in Retrieve PON service facade product ID)

serviceType

Mandatory

String

EVPL or EPL

slaProfileName

Mandatory

String

Represents the name of the SLA profile that a Datalink implements.

allocId

Mandatory

String

The configured ALLOC-ID of the datalink.

Applicable values are 1154 to 1535 except 1278. 1278 is system reserved.

dhcpState

Optional

String

Enable or disable DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 L2 relay processing.

Applicable values are enabled or disabled.

authenticationState

Optional

String

Enable or disable RADIUS authenticator processing.

Applicable values are enabled or disabled.

adminState

Optional

String

Enable or disable traffic on the datalink.

Applicable values are enabled or disabled.

cTag

Mandatory

String

Represents the c-tag value associated with a particular Datalink used for all upstream traffic.

  • Also applicable in NNI network/PON connection properties when tagAction is push/stamp.

  • Applicable values are 1 to 4094.

cTagPriority

Optional

Integer

Specify the 802.1p priority of the added C-Tag on this datalink.

  • Applicable values are 0 to 7

vlanId

Mandatory

String

Only applicable for PON EVPL services.

  • A maximum of 12 VLANs can be provided.

  • Applicable values are 1 to 4094.

  • Values can be provided in comma(,) separated or hyphen(-) separated form as well.

    • Example: 1,2,3,11-15,51-60,70

dhcpRemoteId

Mandatory

String

Represents the Dynamic host configuration protocol remote-id

  • Applicable only for PON residential service.

dhcpCircuitId

Mandatory

String

Represents the Dynamic host configuration protocol circuit-id.

  • Applicable only for PON residential service.

nasIdentifier

Mandatory

String

Represents the Network access server identifier.

  • Applicable only for PON residential service.

nasPortId

Mandatory

String

Represents the Network access server port identifier.

  • Applicable only for PON residential service.

nasUsernameOverride

Optional

String

Represents the Network access server username which is used for authentication in residential PON service.

  • Applicable only for PON residential service.

matchStag

Mandatory

String

Match on an 802.1ag tag. If present, this must be the first tag on the frame.

  • Applicable only in NNI network/PON connection properties.

  • Applicable values are 0 to 4094 or 65535.

matchCtag1

Mandatory

String

Match on an 802.1q tag. If present, this tag will be the first tag on the frame or will be the first tag after an S-Tag.

  • Applicable only in NNI network/PON connection properties.

  • Applicable values are 0 to 4094 or 65535.

matchCtag2

Mandatory

String

Match on an 802.1q tag. If present, this tag will be the last tag on the frame and will be the S-Tag and C-Tag1.

  • Applicable only in NNI network/PON connection properties.

  • Applicable values are 0 to 4094 or 65535.

tagAction

Mandatory

String

Represents tag action to perform on the matched frame.

  • Applicable values are: none, pop, push and stamp.

sTag

Mandatory

String

Represents 802.1ad tag to stamp or push.

  • Applicable values are 1 to 4094.

  • Only applicable when tagAction is push/stamp.

pop

Mandatory

String

Represents number of tags to pop.

  • Only applicable when tagAction is pop.

  • Applicable values are 1/2/3.

floodingLink

Mandatory

String

enabled/disabled. Represents a flooding link flag on the NNI network.

Edit a PON service

Refer Edit customer name, note and tag to edit customer name, note and tags.

To edit the service and endpoint attributes, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: 21fd2320-c9fd-11ed-ae8c-3fbc56238abf.

Sample request to edit the service and endpoint attributes:

{
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [{
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/userLabel",
                "value": "this is label"
            }, {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/trafficProfileName",
                "value": "Hsia100g"
            }, {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/ponSettings/dataLink/slaProfileName",
                "value": "Hsia1000g"
            }, {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/ponSettings/dataLink/adminState",
                "value": "disabled"
            }
        ]
    },
    "interface": "modify"
}

Using the Operation ID (id) from the Sample response, (for example, 4b376b40-c9ff-11ed-ae8c-3fbc56238abf), you can then issue a GET REST API operation to check the final result. This will show "state": "successful", or an error message if there was a problem in the modified operation.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/SVC_RSC_ID/operations/OPERATION_ID

Sample response:

{
  "id" : "4b376b40-c9ff-11ed-ae8c-3fbc56238abf",
  "resourceId" : "21fd2320-c9fd-11ed-ae8c-3fbc56238abf",
  "interface" : "modify",
  "inputs" : {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch" : [ {
      "op" : "replace",
      "path" : "/properties/userLabel",
      "value" : "this is label"
    }, {
      "op" : "replace",
      "path" : "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/trafficProfileName",
      "value" : "Hsia100g"
    }, {
      "op" : "replace",
      "path" : "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/ponSettings/dataLink/slaProfileName",
      "value" : "Hsia1000g"
    }, {
      "op" : "replace",

Delete a PON service

The procedure to delete a PON service is similar to the deletion of the G8032 ring which uses the ManagedServicesContainer resource. For reference, see Delete a G8032 Ring

PON service management for a specific Tier-1 service provider

This section describes the API calls used to provision a PON service or perform different operations on a PON service.

  • Retrieve a discovered/deployed PON service

  • Retrieve PON service facade product ID

  • Manage PON service using sync APIs

  • Create a PON service

  • Edit a PON service

  • Resync a PON service

  • Promote a PON service

  • Demote a PON service

  • Delete a PON service

  • Get PON service details

  • Navigator MC supports the provisioning of PON services on SAOS 10.x 10.6+ devices.

  • If ONU is not pre-configured, it will be configured as part of the service activation workflow.

  • PON residential services are supported from SAOS 10.x 10.7+ devices.

  • PON services with CoS-Queue-maps are supported on SAOS 10.x 10.8.1 onwards.

  • PON services provisioning specifying XGEM ports requires OLT 'auto-assigned-ids' as disabled.

  • Following constructs should already be pre-provisioned and available for PON service provisioning.

    • SLA profiles

    • PON CoS Queue maps

    • Frame CoS maps

    • Egress QoS Queue groups

    • Egress QoS Schedulers and the tap-points

    • Traffic metering profiles

    • ONU UNI ports (if ONU is pre-configured)

    • RADIUS and DHCP

    • LAG

  • For a PON EPL service provisioning case, vlan can be set via the below two GCS properties. Based on the PON application i.e. business or residential, you can update these properties accordingly. Their default value is 65535.

    • businessPonEplVlanId

    • residentialPonEplVlanId

Retrieve a discovered or deployed PON service

To retrieve a discovered or deployed a PON service using FRE ID, refer Retrieve a discovered / planned Ethernet service by FRE ID, including the related TPEs

Retrieve PON service facade product ID

To retrieve a facade product ID for a PON service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.PONServiceFacade. Use this ID as the "product Id" in Create a PON service

Manage PON service using sync APIs

Navigator MC also provides blocking synchronized APIs to manage the PON service provision, deletion, and modification use cases.

The Navigator MC will handle the request once it is received via these APIs. The request would be blocked until its completion. Once the request would be completed by the Navigator MC, the response would be returned to the calling service.

GCS properties mentioned in the below table can be used to alter some of the sync API properties.

Table 5. GCS properties related to sync APIs
GCS Property Name Type Default Value Description

serviceFreDetailsInSyncApi

Boolean

False

Specifies whether the service FRE details would be present in the sync API response(where applicable) or not.

syncApiTimeout

Integer

600

Specifies the timeout value (in seconds) which would be used by the sync APIs.

gunicornMaxWorkerCount

Integer

1

Specifies maximum workers (>= 1) in the gunicorn server in the bpo-ifd container.

It would be required to restart the bpo-ifd container to reflect the change.

  • Timeout Case

    • If the request is not completed within the GCS defined syncApiTimeout value, Navigator MC would return with response-code as 408. This would not impact the service operation at the backend and the request operation would complete after some time.

Please refer to the below sections to manage the provision, modification and deletion of the PON service via sync APIs.

  • Create a PON service using sync API

  • Edit a PON service using sync API

  • Delete a PON service using sync API

A list of API response parameters and related descriptions.

Table 6. Parameters and description
Parameter Type Description

response-code

String

Represents the HTTP status code of the request as per the below table.

Table 7. HTTP status codes and description
HTTP Status Code Description

200

Service request is successful.

400

Bad Request.

401

Unauthorized.

408

Request Timed Out.

500

Internal service error due to unknown exceptions.

503

Service Unavailable.

service_fre

JSON

Represents the complete TPE FRE data of the service.

errors

List

Represents the list of errors that happened during the processing of the request.

request

JSON

Represents the input initially provided by the user.

service_intent_id

String

Represents the service intent id.

service_facade_id

String

Represents the service facade id.

status

String

Represents the status of the request. Possible values are

  • successful

  • failed

  • timed-out

operation_time

String

Represents the total time in seconds that Navigator MC took to process the request.

The below table lists some error cases and corresponding error messages in the API response.

Endpoint on node 5164-10x-211 already has a service deployed having name '1-1-4-26-31-1-1-802-302' and FRE-ID '45f37c43-7cf3-33a9-bef7-ca6fccc4b72f::FRE_EVC_1-1-4-26-31-1-1-802-302'. EPL service is not possible.

No FRE found against the provided input TID '5164-10x-211' and AID '1-1-4-26-31-1-1'

Create a PON service using sync API

To create or provision a PON service, use below mentioned bpoifdnbi API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpoifdnbi/api/v1/sync/service/provision

Specify the productId, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve PON service facade product ID

Delete a PON service using sync API

To delete a PON service, use below mentioned bpoifdnbi API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpoifdnbi/api/v1/sync/service/delete

Following the deletion operation, Navigator MC will initiate a full NE sync. Navigator MC will delete the discovered entities of the service after the sync has been completed.

{

        "aid": "1-1-4-26-31-1-1",
        "tid": "5164-10x-211"

        }
      },
      "status": "successful"
    }
  }
}

Table 9. Parameters and description
Parameter Required? Type Description

productId

Mandatory

String

Product ID for a PON service facade. (Retrieved in Retrieve PON service facade product ID)

tid

Mandatory

String

Represents the name of the OLT complex or member NE.

aid

Mandatory

String

Represents the ONU UNI port identifier. Valid format is <rack> - <shelf> - <slot> - <port> - <onu> - <onu slot> - <uni>.

subscriberId

Mandatory

String

Represents the Subscriber ID. It should match the ONU ID in the AID.

speedCode

Mandatory

String

Represents the name of the SLA profile to be set on datalink and the Metering profile to be set on the Ethernet handoff port.

svid

Mandatory

Integer

Represents the SVLAN. Valid range is 1-4094.

cvid

Mandatory

Integer

Represents the CVLAN. The valid range is 1-4094.

authenticationState

Optional

String

Represents the enable or disable RADIUS authenticator processing. Valid values are enabled, and disabled.

serviceState

Optional

String

Represents the admin state of the service (datalink). Valid values are enabled, and disabled.

Edit a PON service

You can use the REST API to modify a PON service. PON service can be modified in the following ways.

  • PON service edit with TID and AID as inputs

  • PON service edit with JSON-patch as input

Browser refresh will be required to see the updated data.
PON service edit with TID and AID as inputs

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieve a resource

  2. Execute modification of a PON service

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the modify operation

Retrieve a resource

Specify the resource ID, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve PON operation container resource

Execute modification of a PON service

Use the Market API to submit the modify request.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Body of modify request:

{
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "tid": "5164-10x-211",
        "aid": "1-1-4-26-1-1-1",
        "speedCode": "Hsia100g",
        "authenticationState": "disabled",
        "serviceState": "disabled"
    }
}

Sample response:

{
    "id": "bd5fdd70-70a3-11ed-95bb-59fc1966d3b8",
    "resourceId": "a67152f0-6dbb-11ed-95bb-59fc1966d3b8",
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "speedCode": "Hsia100g",
        "aid": "1-1-4-26-1-1-1",
        "authenticationState": "disabled",
        "tid": "5164-10x-211",
        "serviceState": "disabled"
    },
    "outputs": {},
    "state": "pending",
    "desiredState": "successful",
    "reason": "",
    "progress": [],
    "providerData": {},
    "createdAt": "2022-11-30T11:40:07.838Z",
    "updatedAt": "2022-11-30T11:40:07.838Z",
    "revision": 670,
    "resourceStateConstraints": {},
    "executionGroup": "unrestricted"
}
The user needs to provide an empty customerName, and note to delete the attributes.
Retrieve the result to confirm the modify operation

A loop is needed at the caller side to continually check the result state is "successful".

Use the Market API to retrieve the operation status.

Sample request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

Sample response:

{
    "id": "bd5fdd70-70a3-11ed-95bb-59fc1966d3b8",
    "resourceId": "a67152f0-6dbb-11ed-95bb-59fc1966d3b8",
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "aid": "1-1-4-26-1-1-1",
        "tid": "5164-10x-211",
        "speedCode": "Hsia100g",
        "serviceState": "disabled",
        "authenticationState": "disabled"
    },
    "outputs": {
        "freId": "45f37c43-7cf3-33a9-bef7-ca6fccc4b72f::FRE_EVC_1-1-4-26-1-1-1-80-25",
        "facadeId": "bfa30c20-70a2-11ed-95bb-59fc1966d3b8",
        "messages": [
            "Successfully modified speedCode, serviceState, authenticationState"
        ]
    },
    "state": "successful",
    "desiredState": "successful",
    "reason": "",
    "progress": [
        "Successfully modified speedCode, serviceState, authenticationState"
    ],
    "providerData": {},
    "createdAt": "2022-11-30T11:40:07.838Z",
    "updatedAt": "2022-11-30T11:40:13.899Z",
    "revision": 688,
    "resourceStateConstraints": {},
    "executionGroup": "unrestricted"
}
PON service edit with JSON-patch as input

To edit the PON service attributes using JSON-patch, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is the Resource ID of the PONServiceFacade resource being modified

Sample body for modify:

{
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [{
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/speedCode",
                "value": "Hsia100g"
            }, {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/serviceState",
                "value": "disabled"
            }, {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/authenticationState",
                "value": "disabled"
            }

        ]
    },
    "interface": "modify"
}

Using the operation ID from the response, you can then issue a GET REST API operation to check the final result. This will show either "state": "successful", or an error message if there was a problem with the modify operation.

PON service resync with FRE-ID as input

The procedure to resync the PON service via FRE-ID is the same as PON service with TID and AID as inputs. Instead of providing TID and AID, provide the FRE-ID.

    "inputs": {
        "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}"

Demote a PON service

You can use the REST API to demote a PON service. PON service can be demoted via the following ways.

  • PON service demote with TID and AID as inputs

  • PON service demote with FRE-ID as input

Browser refresh will be required to see the updated data.
PON service demote with TID and AID as inputs

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieve a resource

  2. Execute demote of a PON service

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the demote operation

PON service demote with FRE-ID as input

The following steps can be used to demote a PON service. This procedure can be used to demote any L2 service.

  1. Using the Services inventory (FREs) API, get the FRE_ID of the service that you want to delete.

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/nis/api/fres

  2. Using the Market API, get the ManagedServiceContainer resource ID:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ManagedServiceContainer

  3. Using the Market API, delete the service by invoking the operation of the resource using the following API call and inputs:

    POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/<ManagedServiceContainer RESOURCE_ID>/operations

{
    "inputs": {
        "service": {
            "managedOperation": "Delete",
            "freId": "<FRE_ID>",
            "softDeleteAllowed": true
        }
    },
    "interface": "manageService"
}

Get PON service details

You can use the REST API to get the details of a PON service. The following details will be returned as its output

  • FRE ID

  • Service name

  • Deployment state (It would be the Intent deployment state for deployed services and the FRE deployment state for discovered services)

  • Intent ID (applicable only for deployed services)

  • Facade ID (applicable only for deployed services)

  • Provisioned state (This would reflect the state of the provisioned service. It could be 'successful' or 'failed')

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieve a resource

  2. Execute the request to fetch details of a PON service

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the operation

Retrieve a resource

Specify the resource ID, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve PON operation container resource

Execute the request to fetch details of a PON service

Use the Market API to submit the request. The user can either provide TID & AID or Facade ID to get the service details.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Body of getServiceDetails request with Facade ID as inputs:

{
    "interface": "getServiceDetails",
    "inputs": {
       "facadeId":"aa1ef8e0-7b75-11ed-a2d3-23c654e68d35"
    }
}

Body of getServiceDetails request with TID & AID as inputs:

{
    "interface": "getServiceDetails",
    "inputs": {
        "tid": "5164-10x-218",
        "aid": "1-1-7-27-11-1-1"
    }
}

API calls for managing packet service profiles

This section describes the API calls used manage the service profiles used to provision packet services:

  • Provision Layer 2 default profile types

  • Edit a profile

  • Delete a profile

  • Retrieve a profile (inventory and details) by ID or filter

  • Provision a Packet Service (EPL) using a profile

Provision Layer 2 default profile types

This section includes the following topic:

  • Provision endpoint-level profiles

  • Provision service-level profiles

Provision endpoint-level profiles

To provision endpoint-level profiles, use the Market API.

Sample request 1

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Provision service-level profiles

To provision service-level profiles, use the Market API.

Sample request 1:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

The sample profile below contains service-level attributes supported by a Service Facade Profile.

{
	"productId": "{{PROFILE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
	"resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ServiceFacadeProfile",
	"label": "Custom Full profile",
	"properties": {
		"name": "eth::FullServiceLevelProfile",
		"description": "An EVPL profile with gold bandwidth policers",
		"data": {
			"serviceType": "EVPL",
			"name": "eline_allAttributes_service",
			"oamEnabled": true,
			"allowQinQSpur": true,
			"maName": "maNameProfile",
			"customerName": "CustomerNameProfile",
			"protectedPseudowire": false,

Edit a profile

To edit a profile, use the Market API.

You can edit a profile either by using the PUT or the PATCH call.

Using the PUT call

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}

Specify the following attribute: SVC_RSC_ID.

The SVC_RSC_ID is the resource ID you get when creating a new service. It is available in the response message (first top-level attribute “id”).
You can also retrieve the SVC_RSC_ID with the following query (which is an example). In the query make sure that you match "resourceTypes" and "properties.name" attribute values.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade&q=properties.name:jmEvpln2n5

Using the Patch call

Get by filter

To retrieve a profile by filter, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ServiceFacadeProfile&tags=$tag_name:$tag_value

Specify the following attributes, as applicable, to get by filter:

  • profile_resource: the tag key identifying the resource that the ServiceProfile will apply to.

    Expected values are:

    • eth for l2ServiceIntentFacade

  • profile_location: the tag key identifying the location in the resource that the ServiceProfile data will apply to.

    Expected values are:

    • service: apply at service-level

    • endpoint: apply at endpoint-level (settings)

    • flowSetting: apply at endpoint-level (flow settings)

  • profile_topic: the tag key identifying the ServiceProfile topic at more granular level, to scope the intended data schema coverage.

    Expected values for L2 (eth) flow settings and endpoint are:

    • cos: for FlowSetting.ingressCosSetting

    • policer: for FlowSetting.ingressPolicer

    • bandwidth: for FlowSetting.filter

    • in_vlan_ops: for FlowSetting.vlanOperations.ingress

    • e_vlan_ops: for FlowSetting.vlanOperations.egress

    • cfm: for:

      • settings.oamEnabled

      • settings.mepId

      • settings.ccmTransmitEnabled

      • settings.cfmAlarmPriority

      • settings.dmmEnabled

      • settings.dmmInterval

      • settings.dmmPriority

      • settings.dmmTestId

      • settings.slmEnabled

      • settings.slmInterval

      • settings.slmPriority

      • settings.slmTestId

Provision a Packet Service (EPL) using a profile

To provision a Packet Service (EPL) using a profile, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

The following sample shows how to create an EPL using the profile: eth::fixed_1.

{
    "productId": "{{L2_SVC_FACADE_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "label": "L2 Sample EPL with COS Service Profile",
    "properties": {
        "turnUpDateTime": "2020-11-11T00:00:00.000",
        "name": "EPL_COS_FIXED_1",
        "routeMeta": {
            "originator": "BP2"
        },
       "serviceType": "EPL",
        "profiles": [
            {
                "profileName": "eth::fixed_1",
                "profileType": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ServiceFacadeProfile"
            }
        ],
        "endpoints": [
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n2",
                    "role": "A_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                               "location": {
                                    "slot": "1",
                                    "port": "20"
                                }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            },
            {
                "settings": {
                    "node": "87_5783n4",
                    "role": "Z_UNI",
                    "details": [
                        {
                            "flowSettings": [
                                {
                                 "location": {
                                    "slot": "1",
                                    "port": "9"
                                  }
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}

Edit service and endpoint attributes

To edit service or endpoint attributes, use the Market API.

You can use this API call for all types of Ethernet services (E-Line, E-LAN, and E-Tree).

Sample request — Example 1

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}//bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

Specify the following attribute: SVC_RSC_ID.

The SVC_RSC_ID is the resource ID you get when creating a new service. It is available in the response message (first top-level attribute “id”).
You can also retrieve the SVC_RSC_ID with the following query (which is an example). In the query make sure that you match "resourceTypes" and "properties.name" attribute values.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade&q=properties.name:jmEvpln2n5

CVID (using the POST call)

{
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/outerVlanId",
                "value": [600, 601]
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/outerVlanId",
                "value": [600, 601]
            }
        ]
    }
}

Sample response:

There is no response beyond the HTTP status code.

Alternate approach to edit an endpoint using endpoint location:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here user need not to specify the endpoint index(0/1 etc.), instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index. The interface for the new request is 'custom_modify.' Note that since the device used in the sample request below is 6x, only port is specified in the location field.

The other specifications of this approach remain the same as old approach documented above.

CVID Edit (using the POST call)

{
    "interface": "custom_modify",
    "inputs": {
        "modification_input": [
            {
                "location": {
                    "nodeName": "BUF",
                    "slot": "",
                    "shelf": "",
                    "eqptGrp": "",
                    "port": "9"
                },
                "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [

Edit the service description

To edit the service description, use the Market API.

To enable the edit of service description on transit nodes, a new GCS property serviceDescriptionOnTransitNodes is introduced. If set to true, the service-description on transit nodes would be set as well along with endpoint nodes. To maintain backward compatibility, the default value is set to false.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc"

Specify the following attribute:

  • "value" (the Modified Service Label)

{

"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/userLabel",
                "value": "Modified Service Label"
            }
        ]
}
}

Edit the ENNI endpoints of a service

To edit the ENNI endpoints of a service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc"

Specify the following attributes:

  • the "value" attributes, as follows:

    • VLAN ID: 1 - 4094

    • Ethernet type: 8100, 88a8, or 9100

{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/outerVlanId",
                "value": [901]
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/outerVLANEthertype",
                "value": "88a8"
             }
        ]
}
}

Alternate Approach to edit the ENNI endpoints of a service:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here user need not to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index. The interface for the new request is 'custom_modify.' Note that since the device used in the sample request below is 6x, only LAG is specified in the location field.

The other specifications of this approach remain the same as old approach documented above.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

    • VLAN ID: 1 - 4094

    • Ethernet type: 8100, 88a8, or 9100

Edit the UNI endpoints of a service

To edit the UNI endpoints of a service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: “5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc”

Edit Untagged Service with Untagged Data Vid

Specify the following attributes:

  • the “value” attributes, as follows:

    • Untagged Data Vid: 1-4094

    • EtherType: 8100, 88A8, or 9100

{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/untaggedDataVid",
                "value": 901
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/ingressEtherType",
                "value": "88A8"
             }
        ]
}
}

Using the Operation Id (“id”) from the Sample response, (for example, “5a947571-9a34-4b4b-ace7-a664c9816284”), you can then issue a GET REST API operation to check the final result. This will show “state”: “successful”, or an error message if there was a problem in the modify operation.

Alternate Approach to edit the UNI endpoints of a service:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here the user does not need to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index. The interface for the new request is ‘custom_modify’. The same interface can be used for modification of “untaggedDataVid” and “ingressEtherType” parameter.

                "op": "replace",

                "value": "88A8"

}

Edit MAName

Specify the MAName attributes ans its value:

{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "path": "/properties/maName",
                "op": "replace",
                "value": "CHANGED_NEW_MANAME"
            }
        ]
    }
}
This attribute(maName) can be used with add operation as well.

Using the Operation Id (“id”) from the Sample response, (for example, “5a947571-9a34-4b4b-ace7-a664c9816284”), you can then issue a GET REST API operation to check the final result. This will show “state”: “successful”, or an error message if there was a problem in the modified operation.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/SVC_RSC_ID/operations/OPERATION_ID

Sample response:

{
    "id": "5a947571-9a34-4b4b-ace7-a664c9816284",
    "resourceId": "5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc",
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
        {
                "path": "/properties/maName",
                "op": "replace",
                "value": "CHANGED_NEW_MANAME"
                }
            ]
        }
    }
        ]

Edit profile on service endpoints

To edit profile attribute, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "2a5561a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc"

Note: Operations “add” and “remove” are also supported.

{
      "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
          {
            "op": "replace",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/profiles/0/profileName",
            "value": "eth_ep::PROFILE_1"
          },
          {
            "op": "replace",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/profiles/0/profileName",
            "value": "eth_ep::PROFILE_1"
          }
        ]
      },
      "interface": "modify"
    }

Edit dual-tag classifier on service endpoints

To edit dual-tag classifier of UNI/ENNI endpoints of service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc"

Note: Only “replace” operation is supported on classifierList. Operations “add” and “remove” are not supported.

{
"interface": "modify",
"inputs": {
"resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/classifierList",
                "value": "100:10,100:20"
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/filter/classifierList",
                "value": "200:10,200:20"
            }
        ]
    }
}

Using the Operation Id (“id”) from the Sample response, (for example, “7dfb2c00-4c20-11ec-9847-13b0b6622adb”), you can then issue a GET REST API operation to check the final result. This will show “state”: “successful”, or an error message if there was a problem in the modified operation.

Edit a single-tag classified service to a dual-tag classified service and vice-versa is not supported.

Alternate Approach to edit the endpoints of a service:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here the user does not need to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index.

The interface for the new request is “custom_modify”. The same interface can be used for modification of “classifierList” parameter.

Edit the stag and stag ethertype of service

To edit stag and stag ethertype of uni endpoints of service, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc"

Edit stag and stagethertype of UNI endpoint

Specify the following attributes:

Alternate Approach to edit the UNI endpoints of a service:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here the user does not need to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index.

The interface for the new request is “custom_modify”. The same interface can be used for modification of “stagDataVid” and “stagEtherType” parameters.

Edit the Pseudowire head endpoint of a pseudowire handoff service

Starting MCP 6.0 - To edit the pseudowire head endpoint (PWHE) of a service, use the Market API.

Control Word and Flow Label attributes can be edited on a PWHE.

The supported values for Control Word are “on” and “off”.

The supported values for Flow Label are “both” and “off”.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ /bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

The “1” and “0” following the “/properties/endpoints” in the “path” in the sample request (as follows) represent the endpoints. “0” represents the first endpoint in the “endpoints” list on the resource, and “1” represents the second endpoint. 
{
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/pwHeadEndSettings/pwFlowLabelMode",
                "op": "replace",
                "value": "off"
            },
            {
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/pwHeadEndSettings/pwMplsControlWordMode",
                "op": "replace",
                "value": "off"
            }
        ]
    },
    "interface": "modify"
}

Edit E-Line service endpoint policers with bandwidth management

To edit E-Line service endpoint policers with bandwidth management, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "'5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc'"

Specify the following attribute: SVC_RSC_ID.

The SVC_RSC_ID is the resource ID you get when creating a new service. It is available in the response message (first top-level attribute “id”).
You can also retrieve the SVC_RSC_ID with the following query (which is an example). In the query make sure that you match "resourceTypes" and "properties.name" attribute values.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade&q=properties.name:jmEvpln2n5

You can also use the following API call to add or remove individual policing attributes. To add specify "add" as the "op"; to remove specify "remove" as the "op". The following example shows examples or replacing individual policing attributes.
The "1" and "0" following the "/properties/endpoints" in the "path" in the sample request (as follows) represent the endpoints. "0" represents the first endpoint in the "endpoints" list on the resource, and "1" represents the second endpoint. 
{
    "interface": "modify",
    "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/cir",
                "value": 20000
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/eir",
                "value": 5000
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/cir",
                "value": 20000
            },
            {
                "op": "replace",
                "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressPolicer/eir",
                "value": 5000
            }
        ]
    }
}

Sample response:

There is no response beyond the HTTP status code.

Alternate Approach to edit E-Line service endpoint policers with bandwidth management:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here user need not to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The interface for the new request is 'custom_modify.' Note that since the device used in the sample request below is 6x, only port is specified in the location field.

Update management VLAN configurable properties

To update management VLAN configuration properties, use the Market API.

Sample request:

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

Specify the IFD_CONFIG_RESOURCE_ID (which you obtain from the Response of Retrieve configuration resources. )

{

Rerouting services from one tunnel to another

You can use the Navigator MC API to reroute one or more packet service pseudowires from one LSP (tunnel) to another.

To do this, use the AsyncTask BPO-IFD resource.

Navigator MC does not check tunnel bandwidth when moving a service from one path to another.

First, obtain an AsyncTask product ID for this operation:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products?includeInactive=false&q=resourceTypeId%3Aifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask&limit=1000

Sample response
code = 200
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "5cafb0be-e92e-470c-8095-64ecdd0c0452",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask",
      "title": "product for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask",
      "active": true,
      "domainId": "built-in",
      "constraints": {},
      "providerData": {
        "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.AsyncTask"
      }
    }
  ],
  "total": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 1000
}

Then, create an AsyncTask for the reroute operation:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample request
{
    "productId": "{{ASYNCTASK_PRODUCT_ID}}",
    "properties": {
        "operationName": "pwRerouteLspMove",
        "input": {
            "serviceNames": ["jmEVPL2", "jmevpl"],
            "tunnelSource": {
                "lspName": "jmlsp25",
                "lspEndpointLocation": {
                    "nodeName": "87_5783n5"
                }
            },
            "tunnelTarget": {
                "lspName": "jmlsp52",
                "lspEndpointLocation": {
                    "nodeName": "87_5783n5"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

At any time, retrieve the AsyncTask with the following call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/$RID/operations

For example:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask&q=properties.operationName%3ApwRerouteLspMove&limit=1000

Cancelling the task

You can use the Navigator MC API to cancel a re-route operation that is underway. This will not affect the current service re-route within a bulk operation, but it will cancel all of the remaining operations that have not yet begun.

You can cancel the re-route task with the following call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/

There are no inputs or outputs for this custom operation. The request body is:

{
  "interface": "cancel",
  "inputs": {}
}

You can then confirm the outcome of the cancel operation by querying for the status of the operation whose ID is returned in the response.

AsyncTask data object structure

The following JSON snippet shows the schema definitions in the AsyncTask stateData object for this feature. In this structure:

  • "operations" is a list of object/dictionary for each one of the PW reroute operations covered by this LSP move task.

  • "progress" is a list of object/dictionary that provides a live view of the completed PW reroute operations per states.

{
    "operations": [{
            "operationName": "serviceName1 | A_ne_name11 - Z_ne_name12",
            "serviceName": "serviceName1",
            "serviceIntentId": "2f17c86d-a8ca-439e-8ae2-85940062c781",
            "pwId": "7efa8961-a0d4-40c2-838c-ddfc7ebe2c7e",
            "pwFreId": "-8218310471936244223",
            "pwProtectionRole": "unprotected",
            "pwEndLocations": [
                {
                    "nodeName": "A_ne_name11"
                },
                {
                    "nodeName": "Z_ne_name12"
                }
            ],
            "state": "Success",
            "startTime": "2020-04-17T20:50:26.400947+0000",
            "endTime": "2020-04-17T20:50:26.401134+0000",
        }, {
            "state": "Invalid",
            "reason": "Failed to find source LSP on all service pseudo-wires",
            "serviceName": "serviceName2"
        }
    ],
    "test_op_state_by_key": {
        "2f17c86d-a8ca-439e-8ae2-85940062c700-5558310471936244223": "failedWithoutRollback",
        "2f17c86d-a8ca-439e-8ae2-85940062c791-4448310471936244223": "Success",
        "2f17c86d-a8ca-439e-8ae2-85940062c791-3338310471936244223": "failedWithRollback",
        "2f17c86d-a8ca-439e-8ae2-85940062c781--8218310471936244223": "Success"
    },
    "progress": {
        "Success": 2,
        "Invalid": 1,
        "failedWithRollback": 1,
        "failedWithoutRollback": 1
    }
}
The content of this object is reserved for the implementation of the AsyncTask. However, BPO-IFD clients can read this content as way of tracking the specific progress of each one of the PW reroute operations included within a given bulk LSP move operation.

Each operation includes the following entries:

  • "operationName" - the unique name of the pseudowire reroute, consisting of:

    • "serviceName" the name of the service being rerouted.

    • pseudowire route A and Z end signatures (nodeName-shelf-eqptGrp).

  • "pwProtectionRole": the protection status of the service being rerouted.

  • "serviceName": the name of the packet service.

  • "serviceIntentId": the ID of the packet service intent.

  • "pwId": the ID of the pseudowire.

  • "pwFreId": the ID of the pseudowire FRE (FREAP).

  • "pwEndpointLocations": a list to identify the pseudowire by its two endpoint locations.

  • "state" will report one of the following values:

    • Pending: this is the initial state at launch of the task.

    • Invalid: signifies that the pseudowire reroute fails for the given serviceName and tunnel inputs.

    • Executing: the bulk operation is currently handling this pseudowire reroute operation.

    • Success: this pseudowire reroute was successfully completed.

    • FailedExcute: this pseudowire reroute failed before it was exercised.

    • FailedWithRollback: this pseudowire reroute failed and rollback was successful.

    • FailedWithoutRollback: this pseudowire reroute failed and rollback failed.

    • TimedOut: this pseudowire reroute failed to timeout (took too long - 45 seconds).

    • Cancelled: the AsyncTask was cancelled as this PW reroute was still Pending.

  • startTime - time when this pseudowire reroute operation started

  • endTime - time when this pseudowire reroute operation ended

At the end of the operation, the AsyncTask outputs the following:

{
    "results": {
        "failedWithoutRollback": 1,
        "failedWithRollback": 1,
        "Invalid": 1,
        "Success": 2
    }
}
Cancelling a re-route operation

You can use the API to cancel a re-route operation that is underway. This will not affect the current service reroute within a bulk operation, but it will cancel all of the remaining operations that have not yet begun.

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/

This is a custom operation performed on the given AsyncTask resource that must be cancelled. There are no inputs or outputs for this custom operation.

The body is as followed:

POST Cancel AsyncTask resource
{
  "interface": "cancel",
  "inputs": {}
}

To confirm the outcome of the cancel operation, query the status of the operation using the operation ID found in the response.

When cancelling an AsyncTask pwRerouteLspMove, Navigator MC:

  • waits for completion of the currently running PW reroute.

  • changes the state of all Pending PW reroute operations to Cancelled.

  • changes the AsyncTask pwRerouteLspMove state to Cancelled.

Reroute pseudowire

You can use the Navigator MC API to reroute the underlying tunnels that support a service’s end-to-end pseudowire.

This reroute capability is a newly supported custom operation of the L2ServiceIntent market resource (L2 packet service instance). The REST API call is the same as for all market resource custom operation:

POST on /resources/{resourceId}/operations

Only one MPLS pseudowire reroute is currently supported.

The operation accepts two inputs, as described below: "routes" and "validateOnly".

  • routes is the list of the reroute instruction objects to apply to the given L2 packet service. Each object consists of the following two mandatory objects:

    • routeEndpointLocations uniquely identifies the MPLS PW to be rerouted in the given L2 packet service. It must be defined as a list of two endpoint location objects.

      Each endpoint location object includes the following terms:

      • nodeName mandatory to identify the node (NE).

      • shelf and eqptGrp are optional when NE is 6500 TIDC.

    • routeConstraints provides constraints for the new route. It is the same object that was used in the initial service creation request.

      For reroute the following terms are supported:

      • protection can be omitted as it is by default unprotected. In case of protected MPLS PW use primary or backup to identify which path to be rerouted.

      • includeRouteObjects must at least have one route object. Refer to the same object in the creation request for all supported terms.

        Note that:

        • The one route object does not have to provide an explicit new route path.

        • An implicit path can be provided in which the included tunnel(s) identified by name and node provide a partial definition of the new route (as explicit start, middle or end of the new route).

  • validateOnly is a boolean. Set it to True to only check that a new route is found using the provided route constraints

The following is a sample of the inputs for a reroute custom operation.

Note that custom operation outputs and progress are not used. Only state and reason are supported, to issue a notification when the operation is complete.

{
    "inputs": {
        "routes": [
            {
                "routeConstraints": {
                    "protection": "unprotected",
                    "includeRouteObjects": [
                        {
                            "constraintType": "HARD",
                            "locations": [
                                {
                                    "lspName": "IFD6500Automationn1n2",
                                    "nodeName": "G4449-2"
                                }
                            ],
                            "objectType": "LSP_NAME"
                        }
                    ]
                },
                "routeEndpointLocations": [
                    {
                        "shelf": "32",
                        "eqptGrp": "9",
                        "nodeName": "G4449-2"
                    },
                    {
                        "shelf": "31",
                        "eqptGrp": "9",
                        "nodeName": "G4449-1"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ],
        "validateOnly": true
    }
}

Edit CoS Policy and CoS Priority on Service Endpoints

To edit CoS policy with CoS priority, use the Market API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{SVC_RSC_ID}/operations

where {SVC_RSC_ID} is Resource ID of the L2ServiceIntentFacade resource being modified. Example: "'5a9461a6-9eba-4f43-b105-c94fc9ec12dc'"

Specify the following attribute:

  • the “value” attributes, as follows:

    • op: add, remove, replace

    • ingressCosPolicy: fixed or L2PcpCos or L3DscpCos

    • ingressCosPbit: 0-7

    • ingressCosMapName: Default Cos Map Name or Custom CoS Map Name

ingressCosPbit can be given if the ingressCosPolicy is "fixed". ingressCosMapName is applicable only if the ingressCosPolicy is "L2PcpCos" or "L3DscpCos".

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceIntentFacade&q=properties.name:jmEvpln2n5

The "1" and "0" following the "/properties/endpoints" in the "path" in the sample request (as follows) represent the endpoints. "0" represents the first endpoint in the "endpoints" list on the resource, and "1" represents the second endpoint. 
    {
      "inputs": {
        "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
          {
            "op": "remove",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosPbit",
            "value": 7
          },
          {
            "op": "replace",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosPolicy",
            "value": "L2PcpCos"
          },
          {
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/0/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosMapName",
            "value": "DefaultFcosRcos"
          },
          {
            "op": "remove",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosPbit",
            "value": 7
          },
          {
            "op": "replace",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosPolicy",
            "value": "L2PcpCos"
          },
          {
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/properties/endpoints/1/settings/details/0/flowSettings/0/ingressCosSetting/ingressCosMapName",
            "value": "Default_ResolvedCosMap"
          }
        ]
      },
      "interface": "modify"
    }

Sample Response:

{
  "id": "9fc39820-c917-11ed-8a99-cb2d2c092b11",
  "resourceId": "4996e510-c917-11ed-8a99-cb2d2c092b11",

  "inputs": {

      {

Alternate Approach to edit E-Line service endpoint CoS policer with CoS priority:

Alternate Approach to edit the UNI endpoints of a service:

Starting from MCP 5.1 there is an alternate approach to edit the endpoints of service, here the user does not need to specify the endpoint index, instead can use the endpoint location to edit the endpoint. The clear advantage is that the user can specify the location (shelf-slot-equipmentGroup-port) and there is no need to remember the endpoint index.

The interface for the new request is “custom_modify”. The same interface can be used for modification of “ingressCosPolicy” and "ingressCosPbit" or “ingressCosMapName” attributes.

To retrieve information, use the NSI getTPE/getFRE REST API (see Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management.

Configure MTU size

Navigator MC supports configuring MTU size on the pseudo-wires in an L2 service. This feature will set the provided MTU size on all the applicable pseudo-wires in a service. This operation is supported for both discovered and deployed services.

This is a traffic impacting operation. The pseudo-wires will be administratively disabled before editing the MTU size on them. Furthermore, some devices like SAOS 8.x and 10.x don’t support editing of PW MTU. In these cases, pseudo-wire is deleted and re-created with the provided MTU size.

You can use the REST API to configure MTU size on all pseudo-wires in an L2 service.

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieving the resource ID

  2. Perform the operation

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the status of the operation

Retrieving the resource ID

Retrieve the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceOperationContainer resource and select one of the resource IDs.

Use the Market API to retrieve resource IDs.

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceOperationContainer

For example, in the case below, the resource ID (RID) is 1b231189-940e-11ee-9637-03dcdd808942.

Sample response:

{
  "items" : [ {
    "id" : "1b231189-940e-11ee-9637-03dcdd808942",

Perform the operation

Use a custom operation to configure MTU on all pseudo-wires on an L2 service using its FRE ID.

Use the Market API to submit the switch request.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Sample request:

    "inputs": {

API calls for testing packet services

This section describes the API calls used test packet services:

  • Retrieve MPLS-TP LSP status, LSP ping, and LSP traceroute

  • Retrieve operational status of pseudowire

  • Retrieve service — 802.1ag CFM & PW Ping

  • Retrieve the learned mac addresses

  • Perform an 802.1ag linktrace

  • Perform 802.1ag (CFM) loopback on a selected service

  • Perform PW ping on a selected service

  • Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service from any T-PE or S-PE to any other T-PE or S-PE

  • Perform PW ping for a MS-PW based service from either direction

  • Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service that is all MPLS

  • Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service that is MPLS with QinQ spur(s)

  • Perform pseudowire traceroute and retrieve test results

  • Perform LSP ping on a selected tunnel and retrieve its results

  • Perform LSP traceroute on tunnel retrieve results between two E-LAN endpoints

  • Perform a port facility loopback for CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP and retrieve results

  • Perform channel level facility loopback for CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP and retrieve results

  • Perform port level terminal loopback on a CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP

  • Perform channel level terminal loopback on a CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP

  • Perform pseudo random binary sequence (PRBS) on TDM services

  • Perform Benchmark tests (RFC2544, packet delay variation, latency, frame loss, throughput, Y.1564), retrieve results and cancel

  • Status notifications for benchmark tests RFC2544 or Y.1564 using the API

  • Troubleshooting services carried over BGP tunnels

Perform an 802.1ag linktrace

This section includes the following topics:

  • Perform an 802.1ag linktrace

  • Retrieve the test results

You can use this API call for a 802.1ag linktrace between two E-LAN services endpoints.
Perform an 802.1ag linktrace

To perform an 802.1ag linktrace, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/cfmOperations

For an E-Tree service, you can only run a test from root-to-leaf or leaf-to-root. You cannot run a test from leaf-to-leaf or root-to-root.

Specify linktrace as the type.

Below idType can be specified for remotePoint

  • tpes

  • macAddress

  • mepId

{
  "data": {
    "type": "linktrace",
    "localTpeId": "MockCfmCtp1",
    "remotePoint": {
      "idType": "macAddress",
      "id": ":1:2:3:4"
    },
    "testParameters": {
      "ttl" :  "20",
      "priority" : "5"},
    "userAnnotation": "example collection"
  }
}

Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service from any T-PE or S-PE to any other T-PE or S-PE

See Perform PW ping on a selected service.

Perform the PW ping, specifying the required parameters. Then retrieve the test results.

Perform PW ping for a MS-PW based service from either direction

See Perform PW ping on a selected service.

Perform the PW ping, specifying the required parameters. Then retrieve the test results.

Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service that is all MPLS

See Perform PW ping on a selected service.

Perform the PW ping, specifying the required parameters. Then retrieve the test results.

Perform PW ping on a MS-PW based service that is MPLS with QinQ spur(s)

See Perform PW ping on a selected service.

Perform the PW ping, specifying the required parameters. Then retrieve the test results.

Perform pseudowire traceroute and retrieve test results

This section includes the following topic:

  • Perform a pseudowire traceroute

  • Retrieve pseudowire traceroute results

You can use this API call for an MS-PW traceroute on an E-LAN service.
Perform a pseudowire traceroute

To perform a pseudowire traceroute, use the Testing and diagnostics API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/pwOperations

For an E-Tree service, you can only run a test from root-to-leaf or leaf-to-root. You cannot run a test from leaf-to-leaf or root-to-root.

Specify the following attribute: type as traceroute. Also, select values for testParameters, as required.

{
  "data": {
    "type": "traceroute",
    "localTpeId": "MockPwCtp3",
    "testParameters": {
      "count": "5",
      "packetSize": "114",
      "replyMode": "ipv4",
      "timeout": "500"
    },
    "userAnnotation": "example collection"
  }
}

Sample response:

    "id": "49a9f671-4e48-460e-8eb5-91fe39266737",

Perform LSP ping on a selected tunnel and retrieve its results

This section includes the following topics:

  • Perform an LSP ping test on a selected tunnel

  • Retrieve the test results of an LSP ping on a selected tunnel

LSP Ping is supported for both static and dynamic tunnels.
Perform an LSP ping test on a selected tunnel

To start an LSP ping test, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/lspOperations

For an E-Tree service, you can only run a test from root-to-leaf or leaf-to-root. You cannot run a test from leaf-to-leaf or root-to-root. 
{
  "data": {
    "type": "ping",
    "localTpeId": "MockLspCtp6x",
    "testParameters": {
      "count": "5",
      "packetSize": "98",
      "encapType": "ip/udp",
      "replyMode": "lsp",
      "timeout": "500",
      "ttl": "3"
    },
    "userAnnotation": "The testParameters can be left empty."
  }
}

Perform a port facility loopback for CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP and retrieve results

You can use the Navigator MC API to set/enable a port level Facility Loopback on a CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP endpoint of a selected TDM CEM service or a selected TDM STM-1 port.

You can also retrieve loopback configuration details, which can help to diagnose TDM CEM service problems.

This troubleshooting flow includes the following topics:

  • Enable the test

  • Retrieve the test results

  • Disable the test

Enable the test

To set/enable the port level facility loopback test, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/tdmOperations

Specify the local TPE ID, operation, mode, and type.

{
  "data" : {
    "type" : "tdmLoopback",
    "localTpeId" : "c5efbaca-8783-3471-8576-3e2145d9b5db::TPE_chTdm1_7_36_PTP_E1_CTP",
    "testParameters" : {
      "mode" : "facility",
      "channel": "36",
      "type" : "port",
      "operation" : "enable"
    },
    "freId" : "-7901343478415674956"
  }
}

Perform channel level terminal loopback on a CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP

You can use the Navigator MC API to set/enable an E1 channel level Terminal Loopback on a CES AimValley CSoP Smart SFP endpoint of a selected TDM CEM service or a selected TDM STM-1 port and E1 channel.

You can also retrieve Loopback configuration details, which can help to diagnose TDM CEM service problems.

This troubleshooting flow includes the following topics:

Perform Benchmark tests (RFC2544, packet delay variation, latency, frame loss, throughput, Y.1564), retrieve results and cancel

This section includes the following topics:

  • Perform a Benchmark test

  • Retrieve the Benchmark test results

  • Cancel the Benchmark test

  • Create or Delete Individual Reflector

  • Get Reflector

You can also use this API call for an RFC2544 test between two E-LAN services endpoints.
Perform a Benchmark test

To perform a Benchmark test, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/benchmarkOperations

For an E-Tree service, you can only run a test from root-to-leaf or leaf-to-root. You cannot run a test from leaf-to-leaf or root-to-root.

Specify one or more of the following tests, as required: rfc2544, packet delay variation, latency, frame loss, throughput or y1564. Also specify the required test parameters.

rfc2544 and y1565 can not be specified in combination with other tests.
"ethernetMixProfile" is mandatory for y1564 tests
MAC validation parameter is applicable to run benchmark using reflector TPE for 6x and 10x devices and it could not be set to off if test mode is in-service.

Benchmark tests can be run in two ways:

  • Run benchmark test using reflectorTpe

  • Run benchmark test using reflectorMacAddress

Run benchmark test using reflectorTpe
{
 "data" : {
    "type" : "benchmark",
    "generatorId" : "46682de1-0871-3f17-9a4c-34a02cf97074::TPE_5_1_CTPServerToClient_SUBPORT_5_1_tdc8xTest_1",
    "testParameters" : {
      "kpiProfile" : "test",
       "reflectorType": "UNI",
      "tests": [
        "latency",
        "frameloss",
        "throughput"
      ],
      "testMode": "in-service",
      "interval": "completion",
      "duration": "15min",
      "maxSamples": 3,
      "maxSearches": 3,
      "frameSizes": [
        "64",
        "256"
      ],
      "pduType": "ip",
      "pcp": [ "0", "1", "2", "6", "7" ],
      "tagProtocolIdentifier": "0x8100",
      "customPayload": "custompayloadasdasdasdasdasd",
      "ipDifferentiatedServiceCodePoint": "22",
      "pcpValidation": "on",
      "excessBandwidth": "50",
      "samplingInterval": 3,
      "framelossStartBandwidth": "profile-bandwidth",
      "vidValidation": "on",
      "vlanEncapType": "dot1q",
      "testConnectivity": true,
      "colourValidation": "on",
      "macValidation": "on",
      "reflectorId" : "1dc5fc42-4d80-360c-8621-3244fb221cfa::TPE_2_1_CTPServerToClient_SUBPORT_2_1_tdc8xTest_1"
    }
  }
}
Run benchmark test using reflectorMacAddress
{
 "data" : {
    "type" : "benchmark",
    "generatorId" : "46682de1-0871-3f17-9a4c-34a02cf97074::TPE_5_1_CTPServerToClient_SUBPORT_5_1_tdc8xTest_1",
    "testParameters" : {
      "kpiProfile" : "test",
      "reflectorMacAddress": "9c:7a:03:b6:78:09",
      "tests": [
        "y1564"
      ],
      "testMode": "in-service",
      "interval": "completion",
      "duration": "15min",
      "maxSamples": 3,
      "maxSearches": 3,
      "frameSizes": [
        "64",
        "256"
      ],
      "pduType": "ip",
      "pcp": [ "0", "1", "2", "6", "7" ],
      "tagProtocolIdentifier": "0x8100",
      "customPayload": "custompayloadasdasdasdasdasd",
      "ipDifferentiatedServiceCodePoint": "22",
      "pcpValidation": "on",
      "excessBandwidth": "50",
      "samplingInterval": 3,
      "framelossStartBandwidth": "profile-bandwidth",
