Retrieve the Benchmark test results

To retrieve the Benchmark test results, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request: — Retrieve

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/<testId>

Specify the testId, which is the “id” (for example, 208cc81d-8e7b-4789-b67d-0c1c5ef00af6) of the response (when you Perform an RFC2544 test).

<NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST>/tdc/api/tests/208cc81d-8e7b-4789-b67d-0c1c5ef00af6

Cancel the Benchmark test

To cancel a Benchmark test and to retrieve the partial results, use the Test and diagnostics API.

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/<testId>/cancel

Specify the testId, which is the “id” (for example, 208cc81d-8e7b-4789-b67d-0c1c5ef00af6) of the response (when you Perform an RFC2544 test).

<NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST>/tdc/api/v1/tests/208cc81d-8e7b-4789-b67d-0c1c5ef00af6/cancel

Create or Delete Individual Reflector

To create or delete an Individual Reflector, use the Test and diagnostics API.

Sample request: - Create Reflector

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/tdc/api/v1/tests/reflectorOperations

Provide type as create

reflectorParameters are mandatory for create except macValidation.
MAC validation parameter is applicable for reflector to be created on 6x and 10x devices and it could not be set to off if test mode is in-service.

      "reflectorType": "UNI",
      "testMode": "in-service",
      "reflectionLevel": "L2-only",
      "macValidation": "on"
    }
  }
}

Status notifications for benchmark tests RFC2544 or Y.1564 using the API

Navigator MC generates status messages regarding its progress when performing benchmark tests (RFC2544, Y.1564) on Packet services. If you subscribe to these Navigator MC messages using a web socket connection (Kafka Comet), you will receive status messages and can check that list to see the latest status of your request.

Below you can see the status messages that Navigator MC generates during testing and elements of those messages that indicate the operation’s success or failure.

When performing an RFC2544 or Y.1564 benchmark test, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to the testing and diagnostics (TDC) topic "bp.tdc.v1.tests" using Kafka Comet.

When you issue the API call for the RFC2544 or Y.1564 benchmark testing operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "Benchmark Task Id". Use that ID to identify a particular benchmark operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Benchmark Operation Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "bp.tdc.v1.tests.results"

  • Message.Data Id is "Benchmark Task Id"

  • message.data.attributes.testStatus is "Failed"

Benchmark Operation Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "bp.tdc.v1.tests.results"

  • Message.Data Id is "Benchmark Task Id"

  • message.data.attributes.testStatus is "Completed"

Troubleshooting services carried over BGP tunnels

The Navigator MC API supports the troubleshooting of E-Line services that are carried over BGP tunnels using the same API calls for troubleshooting services carried over static and dynamic bidirectional tunnels.

Except where otherwise noted below, these tests are supported for the following devices:

  • 6500-T Release 13.06 & 13.3+ Packet Fabric

  • 6500-S PTS Release 13.06 & 13.3+ Packet Fabric

  • 3926m with SAOS 6.19+

Pseudowire (PW) ping

The Navigator MC API supports PW ping for E-Line services that are carried over BGP tunnels. An example of the related API call is documented in Perform PW ping on a selected service. PW ping is supported in any of the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL
AN-ASBR-MSE/TL
802.1ag CCM Status

The Navigator MC API supports retrieving the CCM Status of E-Line services that traverse BGP tunnels. An example of the related API call is documented in Using the Service Inventory with Packet services management. This capability is supported in any of the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL
AN-ASBR-MSE/TL
802.1ag CFM loopback

The Navigator MC API supports the execution of an 802.1ag CFM Loopback test on an E-Line service that traverses BGP tunnels. An example of the related API call is documented in Perform 802.1ag (CFM) loopback on a selected service. This capability is supported in any of the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL
AN-ASBR-MSE/TL
802.1ag CFM Linktrace

The Navigator MC API supports the execution of an 802.1ag CFM Linktrace test on an E-Line service that traverses BGP tunnels. An example of the related API call is documented in Perform an 802.1ag linktrace. This capability is supported in any of the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL
AN-ASBR-MSE/TL
RFC2544/Y.1564 test

The Navigator MC API supports the execution of RFC2544/Y.1564 tests on an E-Line service that traverses BGP tunnels. An example of the related API call is documented in Perform Benchmark tests (RFC2544, packet delay variation, latency, frame loss, throughput, Y.1564), retrieve results and cancel. This capability is supported in any of the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN-ASBR-MSE/TL
AN-ASBR-MSE/TL
On-demand Y.1731 DMM/SLM statistics

The Navigator MC API supports the collection of Y.1731 DMM/LMM statistics on an E-Line service that traverses BGP tunnels. This includes the ability to retrieve the following information:

  • DMM stats

  • SLM stats

  • EVC topology - AN-AGN-AGN-AN

  • EVC topology - AN-AGN

  • EVC topology - AN-AGN-AN

Y.1731 real-time stats are available via the API and Navigator MC UI. Y.1731 historical stats are available via the API only.

Real-time (on-demand) service/port statistics

The Navigator MC API supports the collection of real-time performance port, queue and service statistics for an E-Line service that traverses BGP tunnels. This includes tunnels with the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN
Alarm-to-service correlation

To assist in troubleshooting, Navigator MC maintains a relationship between alarms and the services they impact. As a result, Navigator MC’s alarm information includes any affected service(s), and service information includes any impacting alarm(s). This service-to-alarm relationship is maintained for E-Line services that traverse BGP tunnels, including tunnels with the following configurations:

AN-AGN-AGN-AN
AN-AGN
AN-AGN-AN

Note: Tunnel alarms, however, do not propagate to a service carried over a BGP tunnel.

API calls for managing packet infrastructure

Navigator MC supports tunnel discovery, visualization, provisioning, and troubleshooting on the following Ciena devices:

  • 8700 nodes: SAOS 8.4 or higher

  • 5170 nodes running SAOS 8.6.1 (for static tunnels only)

  • SAOS 6.x devices with MPLS support: 6.16 or higher

  • 6500 nodes equipped with packet fabric card: release 14.0

This section describes the API calls used retrieve, provision, and manage packet infrastructure including G.8032 Rings, static and dynamic MPLS tunnels, LSPs, and pseudowires:

  • Retrieve discovered / planned static MPLS-TP LSP tunnels (protected and unprotected)

  • Retrieve the set of discovered / planned L2 services that traverse a specific LSP tunnel

  • Retrieve all discovered / planned MPLS-TP LSP tunnels

  • Refreshing properties for links and tunnels

  • Refreshing properties for Pseudowires

  • Switch protected pseudowire from active to standby path

  • Retrieve IP links

  • LAG show

  • Perform static MPLS commissioning

  • Create a static MPLS-TP tunnel

  • Delete a static MPLS-TP LSP tunnel (protected and unprotected) by provisioning intent

  • Retrieve a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

  • Create a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

  • Modify a dynamic MPLS co-routed tunnel

  • Delete a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

  • Unidirectional tunnels

  • Retrieve an inventory of unidirectional TE tunnel

  • Create a unidirectional FRR tunnel

  • Manage a unidirectional tunnel

  • Retrieve / view Ethernet link bandwidth properties

  • Edit link bandwidth properties

  • Modify static MPLS-TP co-routed LSP tunnels

  • Add a backup tunnel to an MPLS-TP co-routed tunnel

  • Modify MPLS-TP LSP tunnel bandwidth call admission control (CAC)

  • Promote discovered LSP tunnels/ G.8032 Rings/ EVCs to modify or delete - Manual

  • Perform tunnel group protection switch

  • Perform LSP protection switch on link

  • Perform LSP protection restore on link

  • Perform LSP correction on node insertion

  • Perform LSP correction on node deletion

  • Perform LSP resize for a dynamic MPLS tunnel

  • Retrieve the latest information about an MPLS tunnel

  • Manually invoke an immediate optimization for a unidirectional tunnel

  • Managing Fast Rerouting (FRR) profiles

  • Status notifications for tunnel creation, modification, and deletion using the API

  • Enable or disable automatic synchronization after tunnel events

  • Refreshing properties for G.8032 Rings

  • Create a G.8032 Ring

  • Modify a G.8032 Ring

  • Delete a G.8032 Ring

  • Retrieve an inventory of G.8032 rings in the network

  • Perform G.8032 Ring operations

  • Retrieve an inventory of FlexE groups in the network

  • Retrieve an inventory of PON Links in the network

  • Retrieve an inventory of FlexeLink in the network

  • Configure Stats Collection and Y.1731 on an IP Links

  • Embedded Ethernet link edit operation through REST API

Retrieve discovered / planned static MPLS-TP LSP tunnels (protected and unprotected)

To retrieve and view the inventory of static MPLS-TP LSP tunnels, use the Services Inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "type" as link and the "layerRate" as MPLS_PROTECTION. (For unprotected, specify the "layerRate" as MPLS.)

Sample response:

To locate each primary and backup tunnel, look for “partitionFres” in the response.

Retrieve the set of discovered / planned L2 services that traverse a specific LSP tunnel

This section provides examples of retrieving a set of L2 services that traverse a specific LSP tunnel, including

  • Retrieve tunnels associated with a specific Ethernet link

  • Retrieve all the services with layer rate ETHERNET associated with a specific Ethernet link

  • Retrieve all parent FREs of a given child FRE for specific layer rate and signal content type

Retrieve tunnels associated with a specific Ethernet link

To retrieve the tunnels associated with a specific Ethernet link, use the Services Inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Specify the "childFreId" and "signalContentType".

<NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST>/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?childFreId=-1996657695693970062&signalContentType=LSP

For details, see the following table.

Table 10. LayerRate and signalContentType by Layer
Layer layerRate signalContentType

physical

ETHERNET

mac_transport

IP Data

ETHERNET

IP

Tunnel

MPLS

LSP

MPLS Protection

MPLS_PROTECTION

none

Pseudowire

MPLS

PW

TOP Service

ETHERNET

VCE (VLAN)

Retrieve all the services with layer rate ETHERNET associated with a specific Ethernet link

To retrieve all the services with layer rate ETHERNET associated with a specific Ethernet link, use the Services Inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

Specify the "layerRate" as Ethernet and provide a "childFREId" (which you can obtain by querying using getFRE API and finding the FRE ID of the Ethernet link of interest).

Refreshing properties for links and tunnels

You can use the REST API to update Navigator MC with the latest data about an IP link or a tunnel from the network.

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieving a resource ID

  2. Refreshing data for one resource

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the refresh operation

Retrieving a resource ID

Retrieve the container resource and select one of the resource IDs. For example, in the case below, the resource ID, RID is 58991626-9a79-45e6-97df-53ecdad53ce2

Use the Market API to retrieve resource IDs.

Sample call:

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

Sample response:

Refreshing data for one resource

You can use a custom resynchronization operation to refresh tunnel or IP interface data by top FRE ID.

Use the Market API to submit the resync request.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Body of resync request:

{
  "interface": "resync",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "8044123183179859606"
  }
}

Sample response:

{

    "resourceId": "5a593763-c966-490b-8b8e-46503a5d22de",

        "freId": "8044123183179859606"
    },
    "outputs": {},

Refreshing properties for Pseudowires

You can use the REST API to update Navigator MC with the latest data about a pseudowires (PW) for a layer 2 service from the network.

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieving a resource ID

  2. Refreshing data for one resource

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the status of the refresh operation

Retrieving a resource ID

Retrieve the container resource and select one of the resource IDs. For example, in the case below, the resource ID, RID is 5dc3003a-8735-47db-8a0d-32fd3f553f82

Use the Market API to retrieve resource IDs.

Sample call:

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceOperationContainer

Refreshing data for one resource

You can use a custom operation to resynchronize with the layer 2 service using its FRE ID and optional pseudowire FRE IDs.

Use the Market API to submit the resync request.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

REST body:

  • "interface" must be "resync"

  • "freId" must be the Navigator MC-assigned ID for a discovered L2 service

  • "filter" is optional: If not included then all PWs found in the freid service will be re-sync’d

  • "partitionFreIds" is optional. If included, they must be all or a subset of the pfre-ids of the l2 service identified by freId.

REST response:

  • "id" is the operation id, OID, of the request

  • "resourceID" is the resource ID, RID, for the L2ServiceOperationContainer

  • "inputs": match the inputs provided in the REST body

Sample body of resync request without filter:

{
  "interface": "resync",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": " 7199254932809131235"
  }
}

Sample body of resync request for specific pseudowires (included in the filter attribute of request) in the layer 2 service:

{
  "interface": "resync",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "-7237763254611272599",
    "filter": {
      "partitionFreIds": [
        "7523220238655332580"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Sample response:

The response echoes the request. A sample response body is shown below for a request with no filter.

{
  "id": "5dc327b8-1559-4a7b-80d6-49c99c7c6d9a",
  "resourceId": "5dc3003a-8735-47db-8a0d-32fd3f553f82",

    "freId": " 7199254932809131235"
  },

  "executionGroup": "unrestricted"
}

Switch protected pseudowire from active to standby path

You can use the REST API to switch protected pseudowires (PW) from active to standby path for a layer 2 service from the network.

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieving a resource ID

  2. Perform switch on pseudowire

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the status of the switch operation

Retrieving a resource ID

Retrieve the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceOperationContainer resource and select one of the resource IDs. For example, in the case below, the resource ID, RID is 5dc3003a-8735-47db-8a0d-32fd3f553f82

Use the Market API to retrieve resource IDs.

Sample call:

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?resourceTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L2ServiceOperationContainer

Perform switch on pseudowire

You can use a custom operation to perform switch on layer 2 service using its FRE ID and optional pseudowire FRE IDs or pseudowire tpe ids(for PW handoff services).

Use the Market API to submit the switch request.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

REST body:

  • "interface" must be "protectionSwitch".

  • "freId" must be the Navigator MC-assigned ID for a L2 service.

  • "switchToProtectionRole" is optional: if not provided here, then mandatory to provide in filter.

  • "filter" is optional: If not included then switchToProtectionRole is mandatory along with freId.

It is mandatory to provide particular partitionFreIds and their switchToProtectionRole in case of multiple protected pseudowires need to switch.

  • "partitionFreIds" in "filter" is optional. If included, they must be all or a subset of the pfre-ids along with switchToProtectionRole of the l2 service identified by freId.

  • "pwPartitionFreId" in "partitionFreIds" is mandatory if partitionFreIds is provided. This is pfre-id of the L2 service identified by freId.

  • "tpeIds" in "filter" is optional. This is required if L2 service is pseudowire handoff service

  • "pwTpeId" in "tpeIds" is mandatory if tpeIds is provided. This is tpe id of PW endpoint of handoff service.

REST response:

  • "id" is the operation id, OID, of the request

  • "resourceID" is the resource ID, RID, for the L2ServiceOperationContainer

  • "inputs": match the inputs provided in the REST body

Sample body of pseudowire switch request without filter:

{
    "inputs": {
        "freId": "8043448713949256046",
        "switchToProtectionRole" : "primary"
    },
    "interface": "protectionSwitch"
}

Sample body of pseudowire switch request for specific pseudowires (included in the filter attribute of request) in the layer 2 service:

{
    "inputs": {
        "filter": {
            "partitionFreIds": [
                {
                    "pwPartitionFreId": "-2245969684929262379",
                    "switchToProtectionRole": "primary"
                },
                {
                    "pwPartitionFreId": "875734810605410797",
                    "switchToProtectionRole": "backup"
                }
            ]
        },
        "freId": "3016335647050755352"
    },
    "interface": "protectionSwitch"
}

Sample body of pseudowire switch request for handoff service:

{
    "interface": "protectionSwitch",
    "inputs": {
        "freId": "3c1e2c55-c54e-3b6d-abce-65a27a043cc1::FRE_EVC_Handoff_service",
        "filter": {
            "tpeIds": [
                {
                    "pwTpeId": "3c1e2c55-c54e-3b6d-abce-65a27a043cc1::TPE_CTPServerToClient_PW_Handoff_service_1",
                    "switchToProtectionRole": "primary"
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}

Sample response:

The response echoes the request. A sample response body is shown below for a request with no filter:

{
  "id" : "5001f748-8927-11ee-8e22-8399ce4e56c6",
  "resourceId" : "949ced48-6754-11ee-8e22-d315d2234946",
  "interface" : "protectionSwitch",
  "inputs" : {
    "freId" : "8043448713949256046",
    "switchToProtectionRole" : "primary"
  },
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "executing",
  "reason": "",
  "progress": [],
  "providerData": {},
  "createdAt": "2020-11-06T20:06:16.825Z",
  "updatedAt": "2020-11-06T20:06:16.825Z",
  "resourceStateConstraints": {},
  "executionGroup": "unrestricted"
}
Retrieve the result to confirm the status of the switch operation

A loop is needed at the caller side to continually check that the result state is "successful" or "failed".

Use the Market API to retrieve the operation status.

LAG show

You can use Navigator MC API to view a information about all Link Aggregation Groups (LAGs) in the network.

Use JOB POST API of Network Element Configuration in Navigator MC to invoke the request:

/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Elements of the call:

Include the following attribute and value as part of the call:

"scriptName": "lagShow"

Sample request payload:

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2020-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "lagShow",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                         {
                                    "type":"networkConstructs"
                          }
                ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}",
        "ipAddress": "{{NE_IP_ADDRESS}}",
        "neType": "{{NE_TYPE}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Perform static MPLS commissioning

Commissioning supports the configuration of basic MPLS based settings so that a node is ready for actual MPLS tunnel creation.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Perform AIS global config

  • Perform AIS profile config

  • Perform AIS profile show

  • Perform BFD H/W acceleration and global config

  • Perform BFD profile config

  • Perform IP-BFD/BFD session config

  • Perform IP-interface/loopback interface config

  • Perform MPLS label ranges

To perform static MPLS commissioning, use the Network element configuration (configmgmt) API.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Perform AIS global config

The aisGlobalConfig Config Manager script allows a user to apply ais-global config commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 PF device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

The aisGlobalConfig script allows the user to execute update ais-global config attributes. The schema provides the user with an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with option: "update".

  • The "update" action allows the user to update the ais-global config attribute.

A use case example is provided below.

The "scriptName" attribute must contain the value "aisGlobalconfig" to execute the ais-global-configuration script.
"id" (contained twice in the example below) is the network construct ID given by Navigator MC for the NE, and "ipAddress" is the IP of the NE.
AIS global config update

Sample request:

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2020-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "aisGlobalConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "update",
                    "globalConfig": "enable"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a",
        "neName": "87c_0009",
        "ipAddress": "10.182.130.100",
        "neType": "8700"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Sample response:

{
  "jobId": "6f057d9f-c912-435b-8f0b-47cab0f540b2",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
   "input": {
    "data": {
      "type": "jobs"
    }
   },
  "output": {
    "data": {
      "type": "jobResults",
      "attributes": {
        "scriptResults": [
          {
            "scriptName": "aisGlobalConfig",
            "status": "COMPLETED",
            "commandResults": [
              {
                "command": "set-ais-global-configuration.json",
                "result": {
                  "result": {
                    "data": "",
                    "result": "success"
                  }
                }
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
Perform AIS profile config

AIS profiles on SAOS based nodes support the node’s use by an MPLS tunnel BFD session or IP interface BFD session. The AIS profile will specify the RDI state, the refresh timer, and tlv-mode.

The "aisProfileConfig" Configuration Manager script allows you to apply an AIS profile commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 Packet Fabric device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

User need to use one of the following AIS profiles:

  • ais profile create profile MCP_AIS_s01 refresh-timer 1

  • ais profile create profile MCP_AIS_s05 refresh-timer 5

  • ais profile create profile MCP_AIS_s10 refresh-timer 10

  • ais profile create profile MCP_AIS_s15 refresh-timer 15

  • ais profile create profile MCP_AIS_s20 refresh-timer 20

The aisProfileConfig script allows you to execute the following with a single script:

  • create and delete an AIS profile

  • set and reset AIS profile attributes

  • set AIS global configuration

The scrip’s schema provides an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with the options "create", "delete", "update", and "unset".

  • The "create" action allows you to create an AIS profile with attributes and set the "ais-global config" attribute.

  • The "delete" action allows you to remove AIS profile.

  • The "set" action allows you to set "ais-profile" attributes and set "ais-global config" attribute.

  • The "unset" action allows you to reset ais-profile attributes.

Examples are provided below.

Perform BFD H/W acceleration and global config

The "bfdHwAccelerationGlobalConfig" Configuration Manager script allows you to apply a bfd-h/w acceleration and bfd global config commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 Packet Fabric device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

The bfdHwAccelerationGlobalConfig script allows you to execute "update", set and unset bfd-h/w acceleration and bfd global config attributes. The schema provides the user with an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with options: "update", "set", "unset".

  • The "update" action allows you to update BFD global config attribute.

  • The "set" action allows you to set BFD global hardware acceleration attribute.

  • The "unset" action allows the user to reset BFD global hardware acceleration attribute.

Examples are provided below.

The "scriptName" attribute must contain the value "bfdHwAccelerationGlobalConfig" to execute the bfd-global-configuration script.
"id" (contained twice in the examples below) is the network construct ID given by Navigator MC for the NE, and "ipAddress" is the IP address of the NE.
BFD global config update

Sample request:

      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2020-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "bfdHwAccelerationGlobalConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "update",
                    "globalConfig": "enable"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {

        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "f0a27af2-40a7-4618-bb9e-35084a87577a",
        "neName": "87c_0009",
        "ipAddress": "10.182.130.100",
        "neType": "8700"

Perform BFD profile config

The "bfdProfileConfig" Configuration Manager script allows you to apply a bfd-profile commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 Packet Fabric device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

The bfdProfileConfig script allows you to execute, create, and delete a profile, and set and reset profile attributes. The schema provides an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with options: "create", "delete", "update", "unset".

  • The "create" action allows you to create bfd-profile with attributes.

  • The "delete" action allows you to remove bfd-profile.

  • The "set" action allows you to set bfd-profile attributes.

  • The "unset" action allows you to reset bfd-profile attributes.

Examples are provided below.

The "scriptName" attribute must contain the value "bfdProfileConfig" to execute the bfd-profile configuration script.

Perform IP-interface/loopback interface configuration

The "ipInterfacesConfig" Configuration Manager script allows you to apply an ip-interface commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 Packet Fabric device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

The ipInterfacesConfig script allows you to:

  • execute create, delete, set, and unset an interface.

  • add and remove ip.

The schema provides the user with an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with options: "create", "delete", "update", "unset", "add", "remove".

  • The "create" action allows you to create an ip-interface with attributes.

  • The "delete" action allows you to remove an ip-interface.

  • The "update" action allows you to set an ip-interface attributes.

  • The "unset" action allows you to reset an ip-interface attributes.

  • The "add" action allows you to add an ip address.

  • The "remove" action allows you to remove an ip address.

Examples are provided below.

The "scriptName" attribute must contain the value "ipInterfacesShow" to execute the ip-interface configuration script.
"id" (contained twice in each example below) is the network construct ID given by Navigator MC for the NE, and "ipAddress" is the IP address of the NE.

Perform MPLS label ranges

The "mplsLabelRangesConfig" Configuration Manager script allows you to apply an mpls-label-range commissioning configuration to any Ciena CES or 6500 Packet Fabric device that has a session established with Navigator MC. The script will execute the RA command to communicate with the device.

The mplsLabelRangesConfig script allows you to update and unset mpls label ranges. The schema provides an input attribute named "action". This action attribute is enumerable with options: "update", "unset".

  • The "update" action allows you to set mpls-label ranges attributes.

  • The "unset" action allows you to reset mpls-label ranges attributes.

Examples are provided below.

The "scriptName" attribute must contain the value "mplsLabelRangesConfig" to execute the mpls-label-ranges configuration script.
"id" (contained twice in each example below) is the network construct ID given by Navigator MC for the NE, and "ipAddress" is the IP address of the NE.

Create static MPLS-TP tunnel

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID

  • Create an MPLS tunnel facade

  • Retrieve the status of an MPLS tunnel creation

  • LAG support

  • Adding constraints

Retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID

To retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the “ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade”. Use this ID as the “product Id” in Create an MPLS tunnel facade.

Create an MPLS tunnel facade

To create an MPLS tunnel facade, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the productId, which you obtain from the response when you Retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID.

Sample request:

{
  "productId": "58cb1ddd-564e-4c6a-afb4-bd3a70449e13",
  "label": "Tunnel SJ to SF",
  "properties": {
    "name": "Tunnel-P2”,
    "turnUpDateTime": "2020-11-19T11:37:29.739",
    "turnDownDateTime": "2020-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "protectionType": "PROTECTED",
    "bfdInterval": "100msec",
    "aisRefreshTimer": "10sec",
	"autoReversionPossible": true,
	"waitToRevertDelay": 300,
	"reversionTimeUnit": "seconds",
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-200"
      },
      "primary": {
      	"port": "3"
      },
      "backup": {
      	"port": "4"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-201"
      },
      "primary": {
      	"port": "3"
      },
      "backup": {
      	"port": "4"
      }
    }
  }
}

A list of parameters and related descriptions follows.

Table 11. Parameters and description
Parameter Description

productId

The id from the API.

label

The label of the tunnel stored in Navigator MC db only.

name

The name for the tunnel on the NE.

The "name" field is optional; if not provided the tunnel name will be auto-generated.

turnUpDateTime

The time when the tunnel has to be deployed. The values can be empty,“NOW” or any time. If empty, then tunnel is deployed immediately.

turnDownDateTime

The time the tunnel has to be deleted.

protectionType

Can be “PROTECTED or “UNPROTECTED”. Indicates whether both primary and backup tunnel has to be created.

autoReversionPossible

true/false. Indicates whether tunnel reversion should be enabled.

endPointA/Z

The endpoint-related information.

networkElement

The NE name.

primary-port

Optional. The I-NNI port to be used for primary tunnel.

For 8700/6500-Packet Fabric, the port information should also have shelf, slot as in the following example:

"primary": {

“shelf” : "{SHELF_NUM}",

“slot”: “{SLOT_NUM}”,

"port": "{TUNNEL_AEND_PORT}"

}

NOTE: When built on LAG, instead of shelf/slot/port, lagName must be provided. For 6500 Packet Fabric, in addition to shelf, eqptGrp must be provided. See also: LAG show.

backup-port

Optional. The I-NNI port to be used for backup tunnel.

For 8700/6500-PacketFabric, the port information should also have shelf, slot (as in the example for the parameter <primary-port, primary port> in this table.
The other parameter values and roles are the same as in the Navigator MC GUI.

Sample response:

{
  "id": "58cb239a-2770-466e-af62-ce66cb1b7981",
  "label": "Tunnel SJ to SF",
  "resourceTypeId": "ifd.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade",
  "productId": "58cb1ddd-564e-4c6a-afb4-bd3a70449e13",
  "tenantId": "2f0a1fae-05c0-448d-96eb-84b989b2f89a",
  "shared": false,
  "properties": {
    "name": "Tunnel-P2",
    "autoReversionPossible": true,
    "protectionType": "PROTECTED",
    "reversionTimeUnit": "seconds",
    "waitToRevertDelay": 300,
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-200"
      },
      "primary": {
        "port": "3"
      },
      "backup": {
        "port": "4"
      }
    },
    "bfdInterval": "100msec",
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-201"
      },
      "primary": {
        "port": "3"
      },
      "backup": {
        "port": "4"
      }
    },
    "aisRefreshTimer": "10sec"
  },
  "discovered": false,
  "differences": [],
  "desiredOrchState": "active",
  "orchState": "requested",
  "reason": "",
  "tags": {},

Note the “id” in the response (above) is the “id” of the MPLS Tunnel Facade created (using the API in Create an MPLS tunnel facade).

Use this id to:

  • retrieve the status of an MPLS tunnel creation (see Retrieve the status of an MPLS tunnel creation)

  • to delete a tunnel (see Delete a static MPLS-TP LSP tunnel (protected and unprotected) by provisioning intent)

IfdConfig resource has a configurable property ifd.lsp.defaultStaticLabelAssignmentPolicy for static LSP label assignment.
Value Description

UNIQUE

Navigator MC will calculate unique labels across all NEs and if there are no unique labels, an error will be thrown.

HOP_BY_HOP

Navigator MC will calculate labels hop-by-hop for each LSP segment.

BEST_EFFORT

Default. Navigator MC will try to find the unique labels across all NEs and if there are no unique labels found, it will try to calculate the labels hop-by-hop for each segment.

  "createdAt": "2020-03-16T23:45:30.424Z",
  "autoClean": false
}

In the response, check the “orchState” and “reason” attributes for the result of the provisioning. If provisioning failed, these fields contain the details (for example, device errors or smoother error).

LAG support

You can use the API to create a tunnel with LAG endpoints as shown below.

Request: POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
    "bfdInterval": "",
    "aisRefreshTimer": "",
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "3930_0064"
      },
      "primary": {
        "lagName": "AGG-64-22"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "3932_0022"
      },
      "primary": {
        "lagName": "AGG-64-22"
      }
    }
  }
}
Adding constraints

During MPLS tunnel provisioning, you can specify constraints that will apply when calculating valid tunnel paths. These constraints can specify a list of nodes the tunnel should, or should not traverse. The list can be a partial or full list of ordered nodes or ports.

  • You can specify a list of nodes/ports to be included or excluded from the tunnel path.

  • These constraints are in addition to the INNI ports that can be specified at the endpoints.

  • You can specify separate constraints for the primary and backup paths.

  • You can specify diversity constraints for protected tunnels, to limit the nodes or links they share in common.

  • You can LAG and TIDc objects as part of these constraints using their equipment group ID

  • Navigator MC will validate the constraints and return a path if available; otherwise no path will be returned.

The examples below show various constraint configurations which can be included in the provisioning call.

Unprotected tunnel with one constraint

"protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
    {
        "includeRouteObjects": [
            {
                "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
                "value": ["A", "B"]
            },
            {
                "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
                "value": ["C", "D"]
            }
        ]
    }
]

Protected tunnel with one Constraint

Here constraints are provided for only one tunnel in the protected pair.

"protectionType": "PROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
  {
    "includeRouteObjects": [
      {
        "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
        "value": ["A", "B"]
      },
      {
        "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
        "value": ["C", "D"]
      }
    ]
  },
  {}
]

Protected tunnel with two Constraints

Here constraints are provided for both the primary and backup tunnel.

"protectionType": "PROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
      {
        "includeRouteObjects": [
          {
            "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
            "value": ["A", "B"]
          },
          {
            "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
            "value": ["C", "D"]
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "includeRouteObjects": [
          {
            "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
            "value": ["X"]
          }
        ]
      }
]
Port-based constraints

In addition to constraints that specify the inclusion or exclusion of individual nodes, you can configure constraints that require the inclusion or exclusion of specific ports.

You can specify routing constraints that require the inclusion or exclusion of Ethernet links by specifying the Ethernet link’s endpoint ports for inclusion or exlcusion.

Port constraints take the following form:

objectType: END_POINT locations: a list of following location objects. Among locations, they are OR relationship:

  • nodeName

  • Other attributes:

    • port = 4 (6x)

    • slot = 3, port = 4 (8700)

due to the list format limitation, only one set of the port value can be supported. There can currently be no OR relationship to specify multiple ports.

Unprotected tunnel with port-based constraints

Here constraints are configured for the inclusion of specific ports.

"protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
  {
    "includeRouteObjects": [
      {
        "objectType": "END_POINT",
        "locations": [
          {
            "nodeName": "MCP-5142-200",
            "port": "4"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "objectType": "END_POINT",
        "locations": [
          {
            "nodeName": "MCP-8700-206",
            "slot": "3",
            "port": "5"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]

Unprotected tunnel with LAG-based constraints

Similar to a physical port-based constraint, you can specify a LAG port in the constraint. You can configure the inclusion or exclusion of LAG links by specifying the LAG link’s endpoint LAG port.

These constraints take the following form:

objectType: LAG_END_POINT

locations: a list of the following:

  • nodeName

  • lagName = MyAggPort1 (for CES 6x, 8x)

  • lagName = MyAggPort1, eqptGrp = 8 (for 6500 Packet Fabric)

"protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
  {
    "includeRouteObjects": [
      {
        "objectType": "LAG_END_POINT",
        "locations": [
          {
            "nodeName": "MCP-5142-200",
            "lagName": "MyAggName1"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "objectType": "LAG_END_POINT",
        "locations": [
          {
            "nodeName": "6500-200",
            "shelf": "31",
            "eqptGrp": "8",
            "lagName": "MyAggName1"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]

Unprotected tunnel with IP Interface Name and Address constraints

Similarly, routing constraint for tunnels using IP links can be implemented by specifying the IP link’s endpoint IP interface name or IP interface address. These constraints take the following form:

objectType: IP_INTERFACE_NAME and IP_INTERFACE_ADDR locations: a list of the followings:

  • nodeName

  • When objectType is IP_INTERFACE_NAME, interfaceName = ipCtrl_3_6

  • When objectType is IP_INTERFACE_ADDR, interfaceAddress = 9.4.1.1

"protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
"endPointA": {},
"endPointZ": {},
"routingConstraints": [
  {
    "includeRouteObjects": [
      {
        "objectType": "IP_INTERFACE_NAME",
        "locations": [
          {
            "nodeName": "MCP-5142-200",
            "interfaceName": "ipCtrl_3"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
Node and link diversity constraints

Node and link diversity constraints only apply to the primary and backup path of a protected tunnel.

  • Diversity Level: Indicate whether to use link or node diversity using the API enums NODE_DIVERSE or LINK_DEVERSE. If not specified, the default is LINK_DEVERSE.

  • Diversity Selection Criteria: Indicate whether the diversity if mandatory or best effort using the API enums MANDATORY or BEST_EFFORT. If not specified, the default is MANDATORY.

By default, without specifying any diversity constraints, a protected tunnel will be configured with link diversity (LINK_DIVERSE) and mandatory (MANDATORY) enabled.

Diversity constraints can be applied to new tunnel creation, and also when adding a backup path to an existing tunnel.

Sample: node diversity constraints

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "turnUpDateTime": "2117-11-19T11:37:29.739",
    "turnDownDateTime": "2117-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "PROTECTED",
    "bfdInterval": "10msec",
    "aisRefreshTimer": "10sec",
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-200"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-201"
      }
    },
    "globalDiversity": {
      "diversityLevel": "NODE_DIVERSE",
      "selectionCriteria": "BEST_EFFORT"
    }
  }
}

Sample: link diversity constraints

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "turnUpDateTime": "2117-11-19T11:37:29.739",
    "turnDownDateTime": "2117-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "PROTECTED",
    "bfdInterval": "10msec",
    "aisRefreshTimer": "10sec",
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-200"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "MCP-5142-201"
      }
    },
    "globalDiversity": {
      "diversityLevel": "LINK_DIVERSE",
      "selectionCriteria": "BEST_EFFORT"
    }
  }
}

Delete a static MPLS-TP LSP tunnel (protected and unprotected) by provisioning intent

Considerations

  1. Navigator MC will perform a best-effort cleanup of configurations during undeploy/delete. A failure to delete one NE or configuration will not prevent the deletion of configurations on the rest of the NEs.

  2. If a service deployment has failed (it is in an INCOMPLETE_DEPLOYMENT state), trying to delete the service will result in the following:

    • Navigator MC will perform a best-effort cleanup of all devices, including partial configurations on NEs for which deployment failed.

    • All resources (facade, intent, expectations) will be deleted even if there are failures during undeployment.

  3. If a service was deployed properly, attempting delete the service will result in the following:

    • Navigator MC will attempt a best-effort cleanup of all devices.

    • If deletion fails on a device, then the resources (façade, intent, expectations) will not be deleted. You will still see a service in an INCOMPLETE_UNDEPLOYMENT state.

To delete a static MPLS-TP tunnel, use the Market API.

Sample request:

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

Specify the resourceId (which you obtain from the request Create static MPLS-TP tunnel.

The tunnel is deleted from the NEs and Navigator MC.

Retrieve dynamic MPLS-TP tunnels

This topic describes how to use the Navigator MC REST API to retrieve:

  • Retrieving a list of all tunnels

  • Retrieving a single dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

Retrieving a list of all tunnels

To retrieve a list of all tunnels, including dynamic tunnels, use the Services Inventory (FREs) API.

This call will also return any tunnel fragments that cannot be matched to a full, end-to-end tunnel. Such tunnel fragments will start and end on the same endpoint.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres

Adding particular filters after the "?" will restrict the returned list to tunnels, or a subset of tunnels. For example:

  • To view only MPLS tunnels:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?layerRate=MPLS&type=link&include=tpes

  • To view only MPLS protected tunnels:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?layerRate=MPLS_PROTECTION&type=link&include=tpes

  • To view only unidirectional MPLS tunnels (either FRR or FB):

    GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v4/search/fres?serviceClass=Tunnel&directionality=unidirectional

In the returned list of TPEs, any tunnel for which the "signaled" attribute is set to "true" is a dynamic MPLS tunnel. An example is shown below.

Create a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID

  • Create a dynamic MPLS tunnel

  • Create a dynamic MPLS tunnel with optimization enabled

  • Creating a dynamic tunnel with routing constraints

Navigator MC Supports the provisioning of dynamic MPLS tunnels with the following devices acting as Label Edge Routers (LERs) or Label Switched Routers (LSRs):

  • SAOS 6.16.1+ nodes, including:

    • 3938

    • 3942

    • 5142

    • 5150

    • 5160

    • 5170 when MPLS capable

  • SAOS 8.6+ nodes, including:

    • 8700

    • 8700 HD

  • 6500 13.0+ nodes with Packet Fabric cards:

    • 6500-T release 13.0 both in TIDC and non-TIDc configurations

    • 6500 PTS release 13.0 in non-TIDc configuration

For information about Navigator MC’s support for LAG endpoints and configuring constraints, see <<create-static-mpls-tp-tunnel, Create static MPLS-TP tunnel>.

Retrieve an MPLS tunnel facade product ID

Begin by retrieving an MPLS tunnel facade product ID, using the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the “ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade”. Use this ID as the “product Id” in Create an MPLS tunnel facade.

Create a dynamic MPLS tunnel

To create an MPLS tunnel facade, use the Market API.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the "productId", which you obtain from the response when you retrieved the MPLS tunnel facade product ID.

The request is similar to that used to create a static tunnel, but supports a different set of parameters. Note the following parameters used in the sample request below:

Table 12. Parameters used in the following example API call
Parameter Assigned value (or supported values) Description

signaledTunnel

true

Indicates that this is a dynamic tunnel; if these parameters is false or omitted then the request is for a static tunnel.

protectionType

UNPROTECTED

This indicates that this will be an unprotected tunnel.

Bandwidth parameters

The following bandwidth parameters are used in the "bandwidth" section.

When you create a dynamic tunnel, you do not configure a single, specific bandwidth. Instead, the NE creates the tunnel with the minimum bandwidth value and will increment that bandwidth as required by the services that are placed on it, up to the maximum bandwidth value. The parameters described below configure this dynamic bandwidth.

dynamicTunnelMinBandwidth

2

The minimum bandwidth for the tunnel.

dynamicTunnelMinBandwidthUnit

mbps

The units for minimum bandwidth: kbps, mbps, or gbps.

assignedBandwidth

11

The maximum bandwidth for the tunnel.

assignedBandwidthUnit

mbps

The units for maximum bandwidth: kbps, mbps, or gbps.

dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements

15

The increment by which the bandwidth can be adjusted.

dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements

kbps

the units for bandwidth increment: kbps, mbps, or gbps.

dynamicTunnelBwAutoSize

enable/disable

Allow tunnel bw automatically resized.

Auto-sizing bandwidth parameters

If dynamicTunnelBwAutoSize is enabled, then the following parameters can be also be configured:

dynamicTunnelBandwidthMode

cac/utilization

the bandwidth auto-resize mode

dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeInterval

5-60

the tunnel bandwidth auto-resize interval

dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeIntervalUnits

minutes

The tunnel bandwidth auto-resize interval units; currently only minutes is supported

dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeFailureAction: alarm/MBB (make before break)

alarm or MBB (make before break)

whether to generate an alarm or perform "make before break" if the auto-size attempt fails

Optimization parameters

For details and example of usage, see Create a dynamic MPLS tunnel with optimization enabled.

dynamicTunnelReOptimization

DISABLE, MANUAL, PERIODIC

DISABLE: do not allow manual optimization or automatic optimization by NE Control Plane

MANUAL: allow only manual optimization (on demand by user) through Immediate LSP Optimization on co-routed Dynamic Tunnels. Automatic optimization by NE Control plane will be disabled, In this case, dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval is set to 0.

PERIODIC: Allow manual (on-demand by user) and automatic optimization by the NE Control Plane. The "dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval" parameter sets how often the tunnel has to be optimized by the NE Control Plane.

dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval

0 (if optimization is disabled), or 5 to 60

Applicable when the "dynamicTunnelReOptimization" parameter is set to "PERIODIC".

If optimization is disabled, the only valid value is 0. When optimization is enabled, possible values are 5 to 60.

NOTE: The units these values refer to are set by the "dynamicTunnelReOptimizationIntervalUnit" property, which currently supports only a value of "minutes".

dynamicTunnelReOptimizationIntervalUnit

minutes

The time unit for dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval. The only valid value is "minutes".

Routing constraint parameters

For information about these parameters and an example of usage, see Creating a dynamic tunnel with routing constraints.
The above parameters which have the prefix "dynamic" are supported only for dynamic tunnels.
Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) must be enabled for all dynamic tunnels managed by Navigator MC. An attempt to create a tunnel with BFD disabled will be rejected.

POST : {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample request:

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "turnDownDateTime": "2117-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
    "signaledTunnel": true,
    "bfdInterval": "100msec",
    "bandwidth": {
	    "assignedBandwidth": 11,
	    "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
	    "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidth": 2,
	    "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
	    "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements": 15,
	    "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrementUnit": "kbps",
	    "dynamicTunnelBandwidthMode" : "cac",
	    "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSize" : "enable",
	    "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeInterval" : 5,
	    "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeIntervalUnits": "minutes",
	    "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeFailureAction": "alarm"
	},
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "3930_SJ_20"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "3930_SJ_21"
      }
    }
  }
}

Sample response:

Creating a dynamic tunnel with optimization enabled

Dynamic tunnel paths can be optimized after the tunnel has been created to make use of a new or modified topology (whether new links, new NEs, or increased capacity). Tunnel re-optimization can be triggered either manually, or automatically by the NE control plane.

To enable optimization for a tunnel, configure the following parameters during tunnel provisioning.

Parameter Description

dynamicTunnelReOptimization

DISABLE: do not allow manual optimization or automatic optimization by NE Control Plane

MANUAL: allow only manual optimization (on demand by user) through Immediate LSP Optimization on co-routed Dynamic Tunnels. Automatic optimization by NE Control plane will be disabled, In this case, dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval is set to 0.

PERIODIC: Allow manual (on-demand by user) and automatic optimization by the NE Control Plane. The "dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval" parameter sets how often the tunnel has to be optimized by the NE Control Plane.

dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval

Applicable when the "dynamicTunnelReOptimization" parameter is set to "PERIODIC".

If optimization is disabled, the only valid value is 0.

When optimization is enabled, possible values are 5 to 60.

NOTE: The units these values refer to are set by the "dynamicTunnelReOptimizationIntervalUnit" property, which currently supports only a value of "minutes".

dynamicTunnelReOptimizationIntervalUnit

The time unit for dynamicTunnelReOptimizationInterval. The only valid value is "minutes".

The API call for provisioning a tunnel is described above. An example of an API call that includes the optimization parameters is shown below.

{
    "aliasNames": [

Creating a dynamic tunnel with routing constraints

The Navigator MC REST API supports several types of constraints that can shape the set of valid paths the control plane can consider for the tunnel. These constraints can be defined when provisioning the tunnel.

Explicit routing constraints

You can specify a set of rsvp-te paths (as IP interfaces) that must be included in any tunnel path. This constraint can be qualified as either mandatory or best-effort.

These paths can be a partial set of IPs or a full set of IPs and can be pre-created on the NE as part of commissioning.

  • This constraint can be specified for only the primary tunnels.

  • The hop-type can be either MANDATORY (strict) or BEST_EFFORT (loose).

    • If hop-type is MANDATORY then the IP has to be a Interface IP.

    • If hop-type is BEST_EFFORT then the IP can be a loopback IP or Interface IP.

Traffic Engineering constraints You can also specify Traffic Engineering parameters to shape valid tunnel paths, in the form of an affinity (color-group) constraint. Tunnel paths must then include, or exclude, links that support certain color groups. These color groups must be predefined on all nodes within the path.

When creating a dynamic tunnel, following types of Traffic Engineering constraint can be specified:

  • "include-all": constrains the path to links that contain all colors specified in the color group

  • "exclude-any": constrains the path to links that do not contain the colors specified in color group

  • "include-any": constrains the path to links that contains at a minimum one of color specified in color group

  • Include All Backup: constrain the path to links that contain all colors specified in the color group of backup tunnel

  • Include Any Backup: constrain the path to links that do not continue the colors specified in color group of backup tunnel

  • Exclude Any Backup: constrain the path to links that contains at a minimum one of color specified in color group of backup tunnel

All three of these constraints can be included for a single tunnel.

Constraint Details:

  • The constraints can be specified for primary tunnel only, for backup tunnel "Diversity" options can be used.

  • The affinity (colors and color-groups) must be pre-created and applied to the IP links (IP interface level) as part of commissioning. The color-groups and colors have to be created uniformly across all NEs. It is not sufficient to simply use the same group names; the color group’s bitmask and each color’s bit id must also match.

  • During the tunnel creation, you must specify these color groups by their correct names.

The sample below shows part of an API request that includes both explicit IP routing and affinity constraints.

Sample request:

{
    "aliasNames": [
    {
        "aliasType": "MANAGEMENT_NAME",
        "name": "MyDynTn08"
        }
    ],
    "label": "myDynTn08",
    "turnUpDateTime": "2117-11-19T11:37:29.739",
    "layerRate": "MPLS_PROTECTION",
    "protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
    "signaledTunnel": "true",
    "bfdInterval": "100msec",
    "bandwidth": {
        "bookingFactor": 1,
        "bandwidthLockout": false,
        "assignedBandwidth": 10,
        "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
        "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidth": 1,
        "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
        "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements": 10,
        "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrementUnit": "kbps",
        "dynamicTunnelBandwidthMode" : "cac",
        "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSize" : "enable",
        "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeInterval" : 5,
        "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeIntervalUnits": "minutes",
        "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeFailureAction": "alarm"
        },
    "dynamicTunnelPathConstraints":{
        "explicitTunnelPath": [
        {
            "hopAddress": "7.6.1.2",
            "hopType": "MANDATORY"
            },
            {
                "hopAddress": "7.7.2.1",
                "hopType": "BEST_EFFORT"
                }
            ],
        "includeAllResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpGreen",
        "includeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpRed",
        "excludeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpY",
        "includeAllBackupResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpGreen",
        "includeAnyBackupResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpRed",
        "excludeAnyBackupResourcesColorGroup": "colorGrpY"
        },
    "endPoints": [
    {

Modify a dynamic MPLS co-routed tunnel

Delete a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel

Considerations

  1. Navigator MC will perform a best-effort cleanup of the tunnel configuration during undeploy/delete. A failure to delete the tunnel configuration on one NE will not prevent deletion of the same tunnel configuration on the rest of the NEs.

  2. If a tunnel deployment has failed (it is in an INCOMPLETE_DEPLOYMENT state), then trying delete the tunnel will do the following:

    • Navigator MC will attempt a best-effort cleanup of all devices, including partial configurations on NEs for which deployment failed.

    • All resources (facade, intent, expectations) will be deleted even if there are failures during undeployment.

  3. If the tunnel was deployed properly, attempting to delete the tunnel will do the following:

    • Navigator MC will attempt a best-effort cleanup of all devices.

    • If the deletion fails on a device then the resources (façade, intent, expectations) will not be deleted. You will still see a tunnel in an “INCOMPLETE_UNDEPLOYMENT state.

To delete a dynamic MPLS-TP tunnel, begin by obtaining a Managed Container resource:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.ManagedServicesContainer

Sample response:

        {

Multiple instances of the ManagedServicesContainer resources will be returned. For the Delete operation, select one resource instance; for example, the first one, as the RID for the next step: 5b4e39e2-f5b8-4ba9-b16e-e9ea1ce122b2

Next, delete the tunnel using an FRE ID:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Sample body:

{
  "interface": "manageService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "managedOperation": "Delete",
      "freId": "-4964036073725228033"
    }
  }
}

Retain the operation ID, since the custom operation is an ASYNC operation. In the example above, the operation ID (OID) is: 589928bc-180a-45a9-aa57-58d9e5ea317a.

To check whether the operation was successful, use the OID to retrieve the operation result with a call resembling the following:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

The response will indicate whether the Delete operation was successful, or failed.

When successful, the tunnel is deleted from the supporting NEs and from the Navigator MC database.

Unidirectional tunnels

The Navigator MC REST API supports the discovery, inventory, provisioning, and management of dynamic unidirectional MPLS TE tunnels.

Much like the dynamic co-routed tunnels that are also supported by Navigator MC, dynamic TE tunnels are directly provisioned only on the two tunnel endpoints. The tunnel routing between those endpoints is then configured by the node-driven Control Plane and updates dynamically over time; this route is maintained as a list of IP links that constitute the current tunnel path. The sizing and bandwidth properties and routing constraints that are already used with dynamic co-routed tunnels also apply to unidirectional tunnels.

Protection for unidirectional tunnels is provided by Fast Rerouting (FRR) to a Facility Bypass (FB) tunnel, which provides an alternative path to replace a single failed link. Each unidirectional tunnel should have access to an FRR profile, a list that is maintained on participating nodes of the protecting FB tunnels that can be used in the place of failed links along the tunnel path.

FB tunnels are provisioned individually, and function themselves much like the unidirectional tunnels they support; however they are not intended to carry services normally. They serve exclusively as protective entities for the unidirectional tunnels they support. However, an FB tunnel is clearly identified during provisioning as a protecting entity, and unlike conventional unidirectional tunnels they do not support bandwidth properties or auto-sizing. FB tunnels are not themselves protected.

  • FB tunnels can also be automatically provisioned by nodes when required by unidirectional tunnels that encounter a link failure.

  • A new GCS property ‘fbTunnelEroEventKey’ is introduced to control the sync behaviour of the auto-created facility bypass (FB) tunnels. The default value is ‘true’, it means auto-created FB tunnel would be automatically synced on receival of ‘cienaCesMplsTunnelOperStateChgTrap’, ‘cienaCesMplsEncapTunnelMbbResultTrap’ or ‘cienaCesMplsEncapTunnelResizeResultTrap’ snmp traps. The sync of the FB tunnel could in-turn trigger the full NE sync depending on the change in actual route. This property could be turned to ‘false’ to disable the sync of auto-created FB tunnels.

Retrieve an inventory of unidirectional TE tunnels

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to retrieve a list of all unidirectional TE tunnels in the managed network.

Use the NSI API to retrieve the tunnel inventory. In the API call, include the following filters:

  • "serviceClass" = Tunnel

  • "directionality" = unidirectional

This results in an API call formatted like the following:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api//v4/fres?serviceClass=Tunnel&directionality=unidirectional

The response to this call will include all unidirectional TE and Faciilty Bypass (FB) tunnels.

You can also use the REST API to retrieve the list of FRR tunnels that are being protected by a given FB tunnel.

Use the Market API for this call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

With this call you can provide the FRE ID of an FB tunnel, and the call will return a list of FRR tunnels supported by that FB tunnel. This requires two steps:

  1. Create an asynchronous task (AsyncTask) that will retrieve the list

  2. Retrieve the result of the AsyncTask.

Sample call body to create task

{
  "productId": "{{PID}}",
  "label": "getFbProtectedTunnels956",
  "properties": {
    "operationName": "getFbProtectedTunnels",
    "objectId": "4.4.4.4_6.6.6.6_Auto_facility-2-2001_TE",
    "input": {
    }
   }
}

Similarly, you can use the API to retrieve the set of protecting FB tunnels associated with an FRR tunnel.

By providing the top FRR ID of a unidirectional protected tunnel, you can retrieve:

  • data

    • id: MPLS top FREAP ID

    • type: frrProtections

    • attributes:

      • frrProtection:

        • primaryPath: IP link FREAPs of the primary path

        • activePath: FREAPs of IP links and FB tunnels

        • protections: a list of nodal protection

          • NetworkContruct

          • ip

          • protectionAvailable: true/false

          • protectionType: link-protect, node-protect, none

          • protectionInUse: true/false

          • protectionFbName: FB tunnel name

          • protectionFb

  • included:

    • A list of referred IP link FREAPs, FB Tunnel FREAPs and NetworkConstructs

First, obtain an AsynTask’s product ID:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample body

{
  "productId": "{{PID}}",
  "label": "getUnidirTunnelProtectionInfo1109",
  "properties": {
    "operationName": "getUnidirTunnelProtectionInfo",
    "objectId": "1.1.1.1_6.6.6.6_anUni5to6_TE",
    "input": {
    }
   }
}

Sample output

Retrieve the AsyncTask execution result using a call resembling the following:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5b1028cf-b3c7-4d6e-a4dd-de9199bfb0d9

Incomplete tunnels in the inventory

An incomplete tunnel is a set of tunnel segments that do not yet constitute a full, end-to-end path because either the head endpoint, tail endpoint, or both are not yet defined or discovered.

When you retrieve the data for a complete tunnel, there are two indications that the tunnel is complete:

  • the "topologySources": "discovered", "stitched"

  • the FRE’s endpoint with role z has a populated relationship; the tailEnd exists and so the tailEnd reference link is a hard link that points to the tailEnd TPE.

When you retrieve a partial tunnel’s data using the API, there are two indications in the response that indicate that the tunnel is incomplete:

  • "topologySources": "discovered"

  • The FRE’s endpoint with role z has empty relationships; the tailEnd does not exist, and so the tailEnd reference link is a soft link.
