Create a unidirectional FRR tunnel

Navigator MC supports the provisioning of MPLS-TE unidirectional tunnels with Fast Reroute (FRR) protection with endpoints on 6500 13.0 Packet Fabric cards.

Navigator MC supports the provisioning of dynamic MPLS unidirectional tunnels using the following devices as LER or LSRs:

  • 6500-T release 13.0 both in TIDc and non-TIDc configurations

  • 6500 PTS release 13.0 in non-TIDc configuration

  • 5170, when MPLS capable

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Obtaining a tunnel product ID

  • Provisioning a unidirectional FRR tunnel

  • Optional parameters during tunnel provisioning

  • Provisioning a unidirectional FB tunnel

  • Editing tunnel properties

Restrictions

The auto-fb-profile for auto generated Fast Bypass (FB) tunnels, and FRR profiles (tunnel-frr-profile), must already have been created on the participating nodes. This is usually done as part of commissioning the node.

Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) must be enabled for all dynamic tunnels manage by Navigator MC. An attempt to create a tunnel with BFD disabled will be rejected.

Unidirectional FRR tunnels do not support LSP-BFD; they support only IP-BFD. An IP-BFD profile should be set up on the endpoint nodes (usually as part of commissioning).

The primary tunnel name cannot end with "_facility" or start with "Auto_facility", as these are reserved for Facility Bypass (FB) tunnels

Prerequisites

  • Loopback IPs, all required Interface IPs should be configured.

  • Configure and enable protocols - rsvp-te, LDP, ISIS or OSPF and IP-interfaces.

  • Set dynamic MPLS tunnel label ranges uniformly:

    • > mpls dynamic-label-range set …​

  • Create IP-BFD for the Ip-interfaces needed:

    • > bfd session create session bfd_ip_56 neighbor 56.56.56.1 profile MCP_BFD_Active_ms100

  • Enable PLR:

    • > mpls frr set plr-support enable

  • To auto-generate facility bypass (FB) tunnels use the following CLI commands:

    • > mpls frr set facility-bypass-autogeneration enable

    • > mpls frr set auto-fb-cleanup-hold-time <NUMBER: 0..3600>

  • If needed, create an auto-fb profile:

    • > mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile create …​

    • > mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile show

  • If needed, create an FRR profile:

    • > mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile create

    • > mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile show

Provisioning the unidirectional tunnel has two steps:

  1. Obtain a tunnel Product ID.

  2. Use this ID to create the tunnel.

Obtaining a tunnel product ID

Use the Market API to obtain a tunnel product ID:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "5b4e39d3-5dd3-4a1b-95e0-d6144d7c8408",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade",
      "title": "product for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade",
      "active": true,
      "domainId": "built-in",
      "constraints": {},
      "providerData": {
        "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.MplsTunnelIntentFacade"
      }
    }
  ],
  "total": 126,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 1000
}

Extract the Product ID by matching the resourceTypeId to "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade"

Provisioning a unidirectional FRR tunnel

Once you have the tunnel Product ID, use the following API all to create the unidirectional FRR protected tunnel:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample body

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "turnDownDateTime": "2117-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
    "signaledTunnel": true,
    "directionality": "unidirectional",
    "dynamicMplsTunnelFrr": {
      "frrProtected": true,
      "frrProfile": "DefaultFrrProfile"
    },
    "dynamicMplsTunnelAdditionalProperties": {
      "setupPriority" : 3,
      "holdPriority" : 4,
      "softPreemption" : "enable"
    },
    "dynamicTunnelPathConstraints":{
      "explicitTunnelPath": [
        {
          "hopAddress": "14.101.3.2",
          "hopType": "BEST_EFFORT"
        },
        {
          "hopAddress": "46.101.11.2",
          "hopType": "BEST_EFFORT"
        }
      ]
    },
    "bandwidth": {
      "bookingFactor": 1,
      "bandwidthLockout": false,
      "assignedBandwidth": 11,
      "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
      "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidth": 2,
      "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
      "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements": 15,
      "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrementUnit": "kbps",
      "dynamicTunnelBandwidthMode" : "cac",
      "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSize" : "enable",
      "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeInterval" : 5,
      "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeIntervalUnits": "minutes",
      "dynamicTunnelBwAutoSizeFailureAction": "alarm"
    },
    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "SIM1"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "SIM6"
      }
    }
  }
}
Optional parameters during tunnel provisioning

You can include soft or hard pre-emption parameters in the call, resembling the following:

"dynamicMplsTunnelAdditionalProperties": {
  "setupPriority" : 3,
  "holdPriority" : 4,
  "softPreemption" : "enable"
},

Affinity constraints resemble the following:

"dynamicTunnelPathConstraints": {
  "includeAllResourcesColorGroup": "cg-indigo",
  "includeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "cg-indigo",
  "excludeAnyResourcesColorGroup": "cg-red"
},

Explicit path constraints resemble the following:

"dynamicTunnelPathConstraints":{
  "explicitTunnelPath": [
    {
      "hopAddress": "14.101.3.2",
      "hopType": "BEST_EFFORT"
    },
    {
      "hopAddress": "46.101.11.2",
      "hopType": "BEST_EFFORT"
    }
  ]
},
Provisioning a unidirectional FB tunnel

The API call used to provision an FB tunnel resembles that used to provision a conventional unidirectional tunnel, but uses the following attribute values to distinguish the FB tunnel as a purely protective entity:

  • "facilityBypassTunnel" is set to true.

  • "dynamicMplsTunnelFb" is used to specify the FB tunnel related configuration.

Sample body

{
  "productId": "{{TUNNEL_FACADE_PID}}",
  "label": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
  "properties": {
    "turnDownDateTime": "2117-12-19T11:37:29.739",
    "name": "{{TUNNEL_NAME}}",
    "protectionType": "UNPROTECTED",
    "signaledTunnel": true,
    "directionality": "unidirectional",
    "facilityBypassTunnel": true,
    "dynamicMplsTunnelFb": {
      "protectedInterface": "IP-PORT106",
      "excludeIp": "12.101.5.2"
    },
    "dynamicMplsTunnelAdditionalProperties": {
      "setupPriority" : 3,
      "holdPriority" : 4,
      "softPreemption" : "enable"
    },
  "bandwidth": {
      "bookingFactor": 1,
      "bandwidthLockout": false,
      "assignedBandwidth": 11,
      "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
      "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidth": 2,
      "dynamicTunnelMinBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
      "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrements": 15,
      "dynamicTunnelBandwidthIncrementUnit": "kbps"
  },

    "endPointA": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "SIM1"
      }
    },
    "endPointZ": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "SIM2"
      }
    }
  }
}

Note the following parameters that can be used within the API call to configure additional unidirectional tunnel properties:

Configure a setup priority value for a unidirectional Fast Reroute (FRR) tunnel:

"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFrrTunnelSetupPriority":{
    "default": "5",
    "supportedValues": "0-7",
    "description": "The setup priority value to be used for creating Dynamic Unidirectional FRR Tunnel"
},

Configure a hold priority value for a unidirectional Fast Reroute (FRR) tunnel:

"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFrrTunnelHoldPriority":{
    "default": "5",
    "supportedValues": "0-7",
    "description": "The hold priority value to be used for creating Dynamic Unidirectional FRR Tunnel"
},

Enable or disable soft pre-emption for a unidirectional Fast Reroute (FRR) tunnel:

"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFrrTunnelEnableSoftPreemption":{
    "default": "true",
    "supportedValues": "true, false",
    "description": "Enabled/Disable soft-preemption during creation of Dynamic Unidirectional FRR Tunnel"
},

Configure a setup priority value for a Facility Bypass (FB) tunnel:

"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFbTunnelSetupPriority":{
    "default": "7",
    "supportedValues": "0-7",
    "description": "The setup priority value to be used for creating Dynamic Unidirectional FB Tunnel"
},

Configure a hold priority value for a Facility Bypass (FB) tunnel:

"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFbTunnelHoldPriority":{
    "default": "2",
    "supportedValues": "0-7",
    "description": "The hold priority value to be used for creating Dynamic Unidirectional FB Tunnel"
},
"ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFbTunnelEnableSoftPreemption":{
    "default": "true",
    "supportedValues": "true, false",
    "description": "Enabled/Disable soft-preemption during creation of Dynamic Unidirectional FB Tunnel"
}
Editing tunnel properties

To edit any of the tunnel’s properties, use the following GET and PATCH calls.

First issue a GET call to retrieve the necessary ID:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig

Note the "ID" value in the response to the above call, and use it in a PATCH request to edit the configuration property as shown below.

PATCH BP_SERVER/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/RESOURCE_ID_V5_IFD_CONFIG

{
   "properties": {
       "configurationProperties": {
           "ifd.lsp.dynamicUniFrrTunnelSetupPriority":{ "value": "3" }

       }
   }
}

Manage a unidirectional tunnel

You can use the Navigator MC API to perform the following management operations on a unidirectional tunnel.

Refresh states

You can use the REST API to refresh tunnel state data in Navigator MC. The method is the same for unidirectional tunnels as for other dynamic tunnels.

For the procedure to refresh state and other data for an MPLS tunnel, see Refreshing properties for links and tunnels.

Immediately optimize the tunnel

You can use the REST API to immediately optimize a dynamic FRR or FB tunnel so that it makes the best use of current network resources.

For the procedure to immediately optimize an MPLS tunnel, see Manually invoke an immediate optimization for a unidirectional tunnel

Retrieve the path of a tunnel

You can use the REST API to retrieve the latest information about FRR and FB tunnels. For an FRR tunnel, this includes the set of FB tunnels that are supporting it. For an FB tunnel, this includes the list of FRR tunnels that it supports.

For the procedure to retrieve the latest path data for a tunnel, see Manually invoke an immediate optimization for a unidirectional tunnel

Resize the LSP

You can use the REST API to resize an LSP, including a unidirectional FRR or FB tunnel. "Re-sizing" a dynamic tunnel increases or decreases the associated LSP bandwidth to reflect the committed service load. Although a tunnel configured to auto-resize will perform this operation automatically given time, you can use this procedure to trigger the resize operation immediately.

The steps to resize a unidirectional tunnel using the API follows the same sequence as for any dynamic MPLS tunnel. For the procedure to resize an LSP, see Perform LSP resize for a dynamic MPLS tunnel.

Edit link bandwidth properties

To edit link bandwidth properties, use the Services inventory (FREs) API.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/v4/fres/<freID>/bookingData/<bookingDataKey>

Specify the new attribute value, as applicable. The attributes that can be modified are as follows:

  • "assignedBandwidth"

  • "assignedBandwidthUnit"

  • "bandwidthLockout" (for example, true or false)

  • "bookingFactor"

The <bookingDataKey> in the PUT URL relates to the attributes listed above.

Sample response:

There is no response beyond the HTTP status code.

Modify static MPLS-TP co-routed LSP tunnels

To modify the attributes of a static & MPLS-TP co-routed tunnel, use the Market API.

To modify the tunnel, use following POST API call:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}/operations

You can use this call to make the following modifications to an existing tunnel (identified by {TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}):

  • modify AIS timer

  • modify BFD interval

  • disable AIS

  • disable BFD

  • modify reversion properties

  • modify protection path

  • add a backup tunnel path (optionally with a constraint or with explicit routing)

You can also modify bandwidth and Call Admission Control (CAC) properties (including assigned bandwidth, booking factor, and bandwidth lockout); these are described separately in Modify MPLS-TP LSP tunnel bandwidth call admission control (CAC).

Requirements You must know the following values before issuing this call:

  • TUNNEL_FACADE_ID: the tunnel’s facade ID

  • OID (where indicated): the operation ID from a previous POST operation.

Viewing results of modification Due to the asynchronous nature of custom operations, you should use a GET call to retrieve the result of the operation.

The original operation to modify the tunnel will return the tunnel OID. Use that value to retrieve details for the modified tunnel:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}/operations/{OID}

Sample requests

Sample request: update AIS timer and BFD interval

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/aisRefreshTimer",
        "value": "20sec"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bfdInterval",
        "value": "1sec"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: disable AIS timer and BFD interval

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/aisRefreshTimer",
        "value": ""
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bfdInterval",
        "value": ""
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: update tunnel reversion

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/autoReversionPossible",
        "value": true
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/waitToRevertDelay",
        "value": 180
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/reversionTimeUnit",
        "value": "seconds"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: add a backup tunnel path

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: add a backup tunnel path with constraint

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/routingConstraints/1",
        "value": {
          "includeRouteObjects": [
            {
              "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
              "value": ["MCP-8700-206"]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Add or remove a backup tunnel to/from an MPLS-TP co-routed tunnel

To modify the attributes of a static MPLS-TP co-routed tunnel, use the Market API.

To modify the tunnel, use following POST API call:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}/operations

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Adding a backup tunnel

  • Removing a backup tunnel

Adding a backup tunnel

You can use this call to add a backup tunnel to an existing, unprotected tunnel. You identify the unprotected tunnel within the call by its {TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}.

This topic shows example requests to add a backup tunnel:

  • without specifying ports

  • with explicit ports

  • without routing constraints

  • with routing constraints

  • with explicit routing constraints

  • specifying a backup tunnel name

  • with backup affnity constraints

Requirements You must know the following values before issuing this call:

  • TUNNEL_FACADE_ID: the tunnel’s facade ID

Viewing results of modification Due to the asynchronous nature of custom operations, you should use a GET call to retrieve the result of the operation.

The original operation to modify the tunnel will return the tunnel OID. Use that value to retrieve details for the modified tunnel:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}/operations/{OID}

Sample requests

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel without explicit ports

{  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel with explicit ports

{  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endPointA/backup",
        "value": {
          "port": "8"
        }
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/endPointZ/backup",
        "value": {
          "port": "9"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel with routing constraints

In this example, the original, unprotected tunnel was created without routing constraints.

{  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/routingConstraints",
        "value": [
          {},
          {
            "includeRouteObjects": [
              {
                "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
                "value": [
                  "A",
                  "B"
                ]
              },
              {
                "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
                "value": [
                  "C",
                  "D"
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

In this example, the original, unprotected tunnel was created with routing constraints.

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/routingConstraints/1",
        "value": {
          "includeRouteObjects": [
            {
              "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
              "value": ["MCP-8700-206"]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel with explicit constraints

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/routingConstraints/1",
        "value": {
          "excludeRouteObjects": [
            {
              "objectType": "NODE_NAME",
              "value": ["MCP-8700-206"]
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel and specifying a tunnel name

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/backupPathName",
        "value": "Backup-sankar-9"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: adding a backup tunnel with backup affnity constraints

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "PROTECTED"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/dynamicTunnelPathConstraints",
        "value": {
          "includeAllBackupResourcesColorGroup": "group-YELLOW",
          "includeAnyBackupResourcesColorGroup": "group-YELLOW",
          "excludeAnyBackupResourcesColorGroup": "group-GREEN"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
Removing a backup tunnel

You can similarly use this call to remove a backup tunnel from an existing, static protected tunnel. In this case you set the protectionType to "UNPROTECTED", which removes the protecting backup tunnel from the current configuration.

Only static tunnels can currently be modified in this way.

You identify the protected tunnel you are altering by its {TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}.

{
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "path": "/properties/protectionType",
        "value": "UNPROTECTED",
        "op": "replace"
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

Modify MPLS-TP LSP tunnel bandwidth call admission control (CAC)

To modify bandwidth CAC properties for an MPLS-TP tunnel, use the Market API.

PATCH {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{config_resource_id}

When the tunnel bandwidth CAC is off, no bandwidth CAC will be performed during tunnel creation or tunnel bandwidth modification.

When the tunnel bandwidth CAC is on, bandwidth CAC will be applied to tunnel creation and tunnel bandwidth modification.

When bandwidth CAC is on, the tunnel creation with bandwidth will be validated by PCE pathfinding. The PCE path will be selected only if (assignedBW x bookingFactor) is less than or equal to the minimal link available bandwidth along the path.

When you edit a tunnel’s assigned bandwidth you can modify the booking factor and lockout, subject to the following restrictions:

  • When decreasing bandwidth, if (new assignedBW x bookingFactor) is greather than or equal to the current usedBW, then the decrease is allowed; otherwise, it is disallowed.

  • When increasing bandwidth, if the increased bandwidth amount is less than or equal to the minimal link available bandwidth along the path, the increase is allowed.

  • When increasing bandwidth, if the increased bandwidth amount is greater than the minimal link available bandwidth along the path, but (new assignedBW x bookingFactor) is less than or equal to the current usedBW, then the increase is allowed; otherwise, it is disallowed.

Retrieving an IfdConfig ID and modifying tunnel CAC configuration

To modify a tunnel, first use the GET API call described below to obtain the ifdConfig resource ID for the service you plan to alter. The following GET call should retrieve one IfdConfig resource:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig

Extract the resource ID from the result and use the resource ID for the subsequent PATCH request. In the sample response below, the IfdConfig resource ID is 592e633d-1d00-481e-a019-3b2d9d83d4de

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "592e633d-1d00-481e-a019-3b2d9d83d4de",
      "label": "Resource for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig",
      "productId": "592e6328-1451-4ea4-995b-63f4e31309ba",
      "tenantId": "697827c1-cdf6-4433-9d0f-2c565ba05be8",
      "shared": false,
      "properties": {
        "configurationProperties": {
          "ifd.l2.autoReversionPossible": {
            "default": "true",
            "supportedValues": "true, false",
            "description": "Whether Auto Reversion is Possible for Protected Pseudowire.",
            "value": "true"
          },
          "ifd.l2.cac": {
            "default": "on",
            "supportedValues": "on, off",
            "description": "Flag to turn on L2 service bandwidth CAC.",
            "value": "on"
          },
          "ifd.lsp.cac": {
            "default": "on",
            "supportedValues": "on, off",
            "description": "Flag to turn on MPLS tunnel bandwidth CAC.",
            "value": "on"
          },
          "ifd.l2.protectionScheme": {
            "default": "ONE_PLUS_ONE",
            "supportedValues": "ONE_FOR_ONE, ONE_PLUS_ONE",
            "description": "Protection scheme for Protected Pseudowire.",
            "value": "ONE_PLUS_ONE"
          }
        }
      },
      "discovered": false,
      "differences": [],
      "desiredOrchState": "active",
      "orchState": "active",
      "reason": "",
      "tags": {},
      "providerData": {},
      "updatedAt": "2020-05-31T06:31:29.658Z",
      "createdAt": "2020-05-31T06:31:25.704Z",
      "autoClean": false
    }
  ],
  "total": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 1000
}

Then issue the following PATCH call to modify the CAC settings for the tunnel.

PATCH {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{config_resource_id}

For example, the following call will disable CAC for the tunnel:

Sample request: disable CAC

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.lsp.cac": {
        "value": "off"
      }
    }
  }
}

Viewing results of modification Due to the asynchronous nature of custom operations, you should use a GET call to retrieve the operation result.

The original operation to modify the tunnel will return the tunnel OID. Use that value to retrieve details for the modified tunnel:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{TUNNEL_FACADE_ID}/operations/{OID}

Adding and modifying tunnel bandwidth properties

Sample request: add bandwidth properties Use this call to add bandwidth properties to a tunnel for which they are not currently defined. These properties include:

  • assigned bandwidth

  • assigned bandwidth unit

  • booking factor

  • bandwidth lockout

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bandwidth",
        "value": {
          "assignedBandwidth": 300,
          "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
          "bookingFactor": 1,
          "bandwidthLockout": true
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample request: modify tunnel bandwidth Provided bandwidth properties are already defined for a tunnel, you can use a call like the one shown below to modify these properties.

If the bandwidth properties are not yet defined, use the Add Tunnel Bandwidth call described above to define them first.

{
  "interface": "modify",
  "inputs": {
    "differences": [
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bandwidth/assignedBandwidth",
        "value": 399
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bandwidth/assignedBandwidthUnit",
        "value": "mbps"
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bandwidth/bookingFactor",
        "value": 3.99
      },
      {
        "op": "add",
        "path": "/properties/bandwidth/bandwidthLockout",
        "value": true
      }
    ]
  }

Promote discovered LSP tunnels/ G.8032 Rings/ EVCs to modify or delete - Manual

Discovered Navigator MC services are not manageable by Navigator MC and cannot be modified.

Service promotion makes discovered services manageable by Navigator MC. After the promotion, these services will behave just like services created using Navigator MC.

You can use the Navigator MC API to modify and delete discovered LSP tunnels, G.8032 Rings and EVCs (i.e. discovered services with no intent), so you can properly manage your L2 network. This includes:

  • manually promoting a discovered LSP tunnel which does not have an intent and have intent generated for the LSP tunnel.

  • manually promoting a discovered G.8032 Ring which does not have an intent and have intent generated for the G.8032 Ring.

  • manually promoting a discovered EVC service which does not have an intent and have intent generated for the EVC.

You can modify or delete promoted tunnels, G.8032 Rings and EVCs in the same way as tunnels, G.8032 Rings and EVCs created using Navigator MC itself.

Service is a general term used here that represents MPLS tunnels, G.8032 Rings (transport services) and L2/L0 services.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Promote an MPLS tunnel/LSP

  • Promote a G.8032 Ring

  • Promote a L2 service

Promote an MPLS tunnel/LSP

To promote an MPLS tunnel/LSP, use the Market API.

Request = POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

The following apply:

  • FRE ID provided must be an MPLS Tunnel top FRE AP ID.

  • The "settings" section, which contains bandwidth information, is optional.

  • Tunnel bandwidth information can be always updated later.

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "5713422440907523218"
    },
    "settings": {
      "lsp": {
        "bandwidth": {
          "assignedBandwidth": 180,
          "assignedBandwidthUnit": "mbps",
          "bookingFactor": 1.8,
          "bandwidthLockout": false
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Promotion is an asynchronous operation. The immediate return of a promotion is as follows:

  • "id" is the operation ID and needs to be extracted for later result query as OID.

  • "state" will report one of the following values:

    • executing

    • pending

    • requested

Sample immediate promote tunnel response

{
  "id": "58ffb8bc-777f-462c-8858-3d536cf82ed1",
  "resourceId": "58fd866d-5436-4dd1-b6e2-edfb19b592b6",
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {...},
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "requested",
  "reason": "",
  "createdAt": "2020-04-25T20:59:40.773Z",
  "updatedAt": "2020-04-25T20:59:40.773Z",
  "resourceStateConstraints": {}
}

To retrieve the final promotion result, use the following GET:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

The value of "state" should be one of the following:

  • successful (for success case)

  • failed (for failed case)

Sample final promote tunnel response

{
    "inputs": {
        "service": {
            "serviceType": "LSP",
            "deploymentState": "discovered",
            "managementName": "Bo_202-203_UP_11-50",
            "userLabel": "",

            "details": {}
        }
    },
    "resourceId": "58fd866c-a124-4dde-95c1-7275281ef9ec",
    "updatedAt": "2020-04-24T07:15:23.728Z",
    "reason": "",
    "resourceStateConstraints": {},
    "state": "successful",
    "outputs": {
        "result": {
            "status": "succeeded",

            "managementName": "Bo_202-203_UP_11-50",
            "userLabel": "",
            "intentFacadeId": "58fda5fb-3dca-43fe-8147-98ad1b1bbb56",

            "details": {},

                "58fda5fe-f9e3-4d33-b778-65474ef09b60"

Promote a G.8032 Ring

To promote a G.8032 Ring, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

The following apply:

  • The FRE ID provided must be a G.8032 Ring’s top FRE ID.

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}"
    }
  }
}

Sample request with customer-name and note:

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}",
      "details": {
        "userData": {
          "note": {
            "noteMsg": "{{NOTE}}",
            "lastUpdatedBy": "{{USER}}",
            "lastUpdatedTime": "<Mon Jan 13 08:17:53 GMT 2020>"
          },
          "customerName": "{{CUST_NAME}}"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
Promotion for single node Major-Incomplete and Sub-Incomplete is not supported.

The remaining steps are the same as for tunnel promotion: getting the immediate response and getting the final promotion result.

Promote an L2 service

To promote an L2 service, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

The following apply:

  • The FRE ID provided must be an L2 service’s top FRE ID.

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}"
    }
  }
}

Sample request with user-label, customer-name and note:

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}",
      "details": {
        "userData": {
          "userLabel": "{{LABEL}}",
          "note": {
            "noteMsg": "{{NOTE}}",
            "lastUpdatedBy": "{{USER}}",
            "lastUpdatedTime": "<Mon Jan 13 08:17:53 GMT 2020>"
          },
          "customerName": "{{CUST_NAME}}"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

TDM service promotion doesn’t support “userLabel” update.

E-Tree services with misconfigured PFG (not supported by Navigator NCS, e.g. root node has all endpoints with PFG role as leaf, etc.) will be discovered and promoted in Navigator NCS. Further operation on these services like adding endpoint/modification of PFG will fail and the user will be given an error message to correct the PFG.

Two-endpoint point-to-point service with no “freType” in Navigator MC can be promoted as an ELAN or Drop and Continue instead of default promotion as an E-Line. Additionally, promoteL2ServiceType as TWO_EP_ELAN or TWO_EP_DNC must be provided as input for this.

In case of promotion as Drop and Continue service, it is also required to provide Source NE as input.

For example, a two-endpoint point-to-point discovered service provisioned outside of Navigator MC has no “freType”.

Sample request:

To promote as ELAN

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}",
      "promoteL2ServiceType": "TWO_EP_ELAN"
    }
  }
}

To promote as Drop and Continue

{
  "interface": "promoteService",
  "inputs": {
    "service": {
      "freId": "{{FRE_ID}}",
      "promoteL2ServiceType": "TWO_EP_DNC",
      "source": {
            "name": "{{Source NE}}"
      }
    }
  }
}

The remaining steps are the same as for tunnel promotion: getting the immediate response and getting the final promotion result.

Perform tunnel group protection switch

You can use the Navigator MC API to move traffic away from the currently active LSP. This could be useful in order to allow the performance of disruptive maintenance on the path currently carrying traffic.

This operation is supported on both static and dynamic tunnels.

As part of this switch operation:

  • You can switch traffic without specifying the desired outcome, in which case Navigator MC will switch traffic away from the currently active LSP.

  • You can specify the desire to switch and the newly designated active tunnel, in which case Navigator MC will ensure that the switch operation is performed if required.

Using the API, it is possible to specify whether the primary or backup should be active as part of the switch operation.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve the MplsOperationContainer resource ID

  • Execute the tunnel group protection switch

  • Retrieve the status of the tunnel group protection switch

Retrieve the MplsOperationContainer resource ID

To retrieve the MplsOperationContainer resource ID, use the Market API.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

Execute the tunnel group protection switch

To execute the tunnel group protection switch, use the Market API.

Request = POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

{

  "inputs": {
    "freId": "-3770626729195966017",
    "switchToTunnelRole" : "primary"

interface

protectionSwitch as the default value for this operation.

inputs

switchToTunnelRole

Possible values:

Perform LSP protection switch on link

When performing an LSP protection switch with the API, you can define whether this operation is the best-effort or not.

  • In the case of a best-effort operation, the LSP switch will still proceed even if some LSPs cannot be switched. The response will include a list of tunnels that could not be switched.

  • If the operation is not best-effort, the operation will fail if some LSPs cannot be switched away.

  • Any backup LSP configured over this link may be left alone.

Perform LSP correction on node insertion

Use this procedure to correct a static MPLS co-routed bidirectional LSP tunnel group when adding a new node to its path.

A tunnel group can be protected or unprotected:

  • An unprotected tunnel group consists of a single LSP between two LER nodes with or without intermediate transit nodes (LSRs).

  • A protected tunnel group consists of two such LSPs, one being the primary and the other being the backup. Only one LSP (primary or backup) is active at a given time.

Requirements

Perform the following:

  1. Physically disconnect the nodes and insert the new node.

    The link added between A-X and X-B should be on the same ports where the old link between A-B used to be. As an example if the original link was between Port 1 of Node A and Port 2 of Node B and a Node X was inserted between A and B, then the link to X from A should start from Port 1 and the link to X from B should start from Port 2.

  2. Pre-provision the following on the devices:

    • loopback IP and interface IP addresses (for IP links)

    • AIS profiles

    • BFD profiles

  3. Pre-assign a loopback IP address to each node in the tunnel path (including LER and LSR nodes)

  4. Provision interface IP addresses and VLANs for every port on CES devices over which a tunnel could be routed.

MTU size on the newly configured IP interfaces should match the MTU size on the original IP interfaces of nodes A and B respectively.

  1. Rediscover the affected nodes.

As part of commissioning the new IP interfaces, do not change or delete the existing interface.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve the NodeInsertionWorkflow product ID

  • Create the NodeInsertionWorkflow resource

  • Execute the LSP correction

  • Get the status of LSP correction operation

  • Retrieve the workflow resource

Retrieve the NodeInsertionWorkflow product ID

      "active": true,
      "domainId": "built-in",
      "constraints": {},
      "providerData": {
        "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.NodeInsertionWorkflow"
      }

    {
      "id": "5953f3f3-e8c1-4e12-a950-b7e76bead5f3",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.NodeDeletionWorkflow",
      "title": "product for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.NodeDeletionWorkflow",
      "active": true,
      "domainId": "built-in",
      "constraints": {},
      "providerData": {
        "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.NodeDeletionWorkflow"
      }

  "limit": 1000
}

In the response, note the “ifd.v6.resourceTypes.NodeInsertionWorkflow”. Use this ID as the “product Id” in Create the NodeInsertionWorkflow resource.

Create the NodeInsertionWorkflow resource
Use the original link that was removed and provide that as part of endpoints while creating the NodeInsertionWorkflow resource.

Assumption: If X is the new node that is inserted between A-B, use the port from A (connected to X) and port from B (connected to X) to create the workflow resource.

The link added between A-X and X-B should be on the same ports where the old link between A-B used to be. As an example, if the original link was between Port 1 of Node A and Port 2 of Node B and a Node X was inserted between A and B, then the link to X from A should start from Port 1 of Node A and the link to X from B should start from Port 2 of Node B.

In the case of LAGs, the LAG link between A-X and X-B should be on the existing LAG created on nodes A & B.

As an example, if the original LAG created on nodes A and B were LAG_A and LAG_B respectively, it will be discovered as LAG_A, LAG_B in the Navigator MC. Now, Node X is inserted between A and B, the link to X from A should start from LAG_A of Node A and the link to X from B should start from LAG_B of Node B.

To perform the LSP correction procedure now, the user will need to create 2 LAGs on node X,

  • LAG_X1 which will be stitched with LAG_A of Node A, discovered as LAG_A, LAG_X1 between Node A and Node X.

  • LAG_X2 which will be stitched with LAG_B of Node B, discovered as LAG_B, LAG_X2 between Node B and Node X.

Perform LSP correction on node deletion

You can use the Navigator MC API to correct a static MPLS co-routed bidirectional LSP tunnel group following the deletion of a node in its path.

A tunnel group can be protected or unprotected.

Assumptions:

  • The initial connection is A-X-B.

  • Node X is physically disconnected from A and B.

  • A and B are directly connected.

LSP correction on node deletion will correct the LSPs terminating on A or B, and LSPs transiting through nodes A or B.

Requirements

Perform the following:

  1. Physically disconnect the nodes and connect the two nodes A and B.

  2. Pre-provision the following on the devices:

    • loopback IP

    • interface IP addresses (for IP links)

  3. Pre-assign a loopback IP address to each node in the tunnel path (including LER and LSR nodes).

  4. Provision interface IP addresses and VLANs for every port on CES devices over which a tunnel could be routed.

  5. Rediscover the two affected nodes.

As part of commissioning the new IP interfaces, do not change or delete the existing interface.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve the NodeDeletionWorkflow product ID

  • Create the NodeDeletionWorkflow resource

  • Execute the LSP correction

  • Retrieve the status of the LSP correction operation

  • Retrieve the workflow resource

Create the NodeInsertionWorkflow resource
Use the original link that was removed and provide that as part of endpoints while creating the NodeDeletionWorkflow resource.

Assumption: If X is the new node that is deleted between A-B, use the port from A (connected to B) and port from B (connected to A) to create the node deletion workflow resource.

The link added between A-B should be on the same ports where the old links between A-X and X-B used to be.

As an example if the original link was between

  • Port 1 of Node A and Port 1 of Node X

  • Port 2 of Node B and Port 2 of Node X

Now, Node X is removed between A and B, and then the link between A and B should start from Port 1 (of Node A) and end to Port 2 (of Node B).

Similarly, in the case of underlying LAG, the LAG link between A-B should be on the existing LAGs created on nodes A & B.

Consider a scenario, where

  • LAG_A and LAG_X1 created on nodes A and X respectively, discovered as LAG_A, LAG_X1

  • LAG_X2 and LAG_B created on nodes X and B respectively, discovered as LAG_X2, LAG_B

Now, Node X is deleted between A and B, the link from A should start from Port 1 (underlying port in LAG_A) of Node A and end at Port 2 (underlying port in LAG_B) of Node B. Finally, there will be a single LAG link discovered in the Navigator MC, LAG_A, LAG_B between nodes A and B.

Perform LSP resize for a dynamic MPLS tunnel

Use this procedure to manually trigger the immediate re-sizing of a dynamic tunnel for which auto-resizing has been enabled.

"Re-sizing" a dynamic tunnel increases or decreases the associated LSP bandwidth to reflect the committed service load. Although a tunnel configured to auto-resize will perform this operation automatically given time, you can use this procedure to trigger the resize operation immediately.

When you trigger the re-size operation, Navigator MC will send the auto-resize trigger command to the supporting device. This operation will only trigger the auto-resize instruction to the NE; whether the tunnel is actually auto-resized or not is controlled by NE.

Resizing a tunnel, and verifying success, involves the following steps:

  1. Retrieve a MplsOperationContainer resource ID

  2. Execute the tunnel group resize (using the resource ID you obtained in step 1)

  3. Get the status of resize operation (using the operation ID you obtained in step 2)

After a resize operation, Navigator MC may not immediately update the values for "Last resize start time", "Last resize end time" and "Resize reason". To ensure that you have the latest values for these attributes, first manually resynchronize the tunnel.

The response includes the list of MplsOperationContainer resources; and every resource in the response will have an attribute named "id".

Select one resource from the returned list of resources, and use the value of id property to execute the tunnel group Resize.

Executing tunnel group resize

Use the Market API POST operation to resize the tunnel group.

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Request data :

Parameter Description

interface

Resize as the default value for this operation

inputs

input data for the resize operation

field

tunnel group FRE ID

 
{
  "interface": "resize",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "6515318274086203180"
  }
}

Sample response:

{
  "id": "5956d1d6-d0e1-45d7-a636-587815eb9736",
  "resourceId": "5955a92d-1f6a-4b41-aa36-8019be2dfd84",
  "interface": "resize",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "6515318274086203180"
  },
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "requested",
  "reason": "",
  "createdAt": "2020-01-30T22:33:58.889Z",
  "updatedAt": "2020-01-30T22:33:58.889Z",
  "resourceStateConstraints": {}
}
The “id” in the response (above) is the unique id number that assigned to the resize operation.

You can use this id to:

  • Retrieve the status of the tunnel group resize operation.

  • Retrieve the status of tunnel group resize operation.

NOTE:

  • RID is the MplsOperationContainer resource ID used as part of executing the resize operation.

  • OID is the operation ID generated as part of tunnel group resize operation (Step 3)

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

Retrieving the status of the resize operation

Using the resize operation ID, you can obtain the status of the operation to verify its successful execution.

Use the Market API GET operation to obtain this status.

Sample request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

Sample response:

Parameter Description

id

The resize operation ID

state

The state of the resize operation.

Possible values are:

  • successful

  • failed

  • aborted

 
{
  "id": "5956d1d6-d0e1-45d7-a636-587815eb9736",
  "resourceId": "5955a92d-1f6a-4b41-aa36-8019be2dfd84",
  "interface": "resize",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "-3770626729195966017"
  },
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "successful",
  "reason": "",
  "createdAt": "2020-01-30T22:33:58.889Z",
  "updatedAt": "2020-01-30T22:34:04.846Z",
  "resourceStateConstraints": {}
}

Retrieve the latest information about an MPLS tunnel

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve the latest information about an MPLS tunnel. You do this by resynchronizing the tunnel, which will cause Navigator MC to load the latest information about that tunnel from the supporting node.

The tunnel resynchronization process is an asynchronous process, and the latest tunnel information is available only after the resynchronization is completed.

The steps to retrieve the latest tunnel information are:

  1. Resync the tunnel

  2. Wait for the resync completion

  3. Get the latest information

Navigator MC now uses an easy-to-use REST API call, the AsyncTask, to wrap all three steps together.

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Retrieving an AsyncTask product ID

  • Retrieving information for a unidirectional FRR tunnel

  • Retrieving information for a unidirectional FB tunnel

Retrieving an AsyncTask product ID

To create an AsyncTask, we first need to get its product ID. This is a common step that is frequently used to begin a chain of related API calls.

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

An example of the output in response to this call:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "5b0efc15-a4f4-4df3-a2d8-078f80e2433e",
      "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask",
      "title": "product for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask",
      "active": true,
      "domainId": "built-in",
      "constraints": {},
      "providerData": {
        "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.AsyncTask"
      }
    }
  ],
  "total": 125,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 1000
}

From this response, parse the product ID of AsyncTask. In the above example, this is:

5b0efc15-a4f4-4df3-a2d8-078f80e2433e

Retrieving information for a unidirectional FRR tunnel

For a unidirectional Fast Reroute (FRR) protected tunnel, you retrieve the set of protecting FB tunnels and the tunnel’s current active path.

Input for this call consists of:

  • the unidirectional FRR protected tunnel’s top FRE ID

Output returned by this call will include:

  • data

    • id: MPLS top FREAP ID

    • type: frrProtections

    • attributes:

    • frrProtection:

    • primaryPath: IP link FREAPs of the primary path

    • activePath: FREAPs of IP links and FB tunnels

    • protections: a list of nodal protection

      • NetworkContruct

      • ip

      • protectionAvailable: true/false

      • protectionType: link-protect, node-protect, none

      • protectionInUse: true/false

      • protectionFbName: FB tunnel name

      • protectionFb

  • included

    • a list of referred IP link FREAPs, FB Tunnel FREAPs and NetworkConstructs

First, retrieve an AsyncTask product ID as described at the beginning of this topic.

Then, create an AsyncTask:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Sample request body

{
  "productId": "{PID}",
  "label": "getUnidirTunnelProtectionInfo1109",
  "properties": {
    "operationName": "getUnidirTunnelProtectionInfo",
    "objectId": "1.1.1.1_6.6.6.6_anUni5to6_TE",
    "input": {
    }
   }
}

Sample response:

Retrieving information for a unidirectional FB tunnel

Similarly, you can use an AsyncTask to retrieve the set of FRR tunnels that are being protected by a given FB tunnel.

Input:

  • the FB tunnel’s top FRE ID

Output:

  • data

    • A list of protected unidirectional FRR tunnel FREs

First, retrieve an AsyncTask product ID as described at the beginning of this topic.

Then, create an AsyncTask:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

sample body

{ "productId": "{PID}", "label": "getFbProtectedTunnels956", "properties": { "operationName": "getFbProtectedTunnels", "objectId": "4.4.4.4_6.6.6.6_Auto_facility-2-2001_TE", "input": { } } }

Sample response:

{
    "id": "5b10356b-9110-45a9-89d0-77febabad4ec",
    "label": "getFbProtectedTunnels956",
    "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.AsyncTask",
    "productId": "5b0efc15-a4f4-4df3-a2d8-078f80e2433e",
    "tenantId": "ec5d7efe-9e19-4503-8402-b0fc8b78ba8c",
    "shared": false,
    "properties": {
        "objectId": "4.4.4.4_6.6.6.6_Auto_facility-2-2001_TE",
        "operationName": "getFbProtectedTunnels",
        "input": {}
    },
    "discovered": false,
    "differences": [],
    "desiredOrchState": "active",
    "orchState": "requested",
    "reason": "",
    "tags": {},
    "providerData": {},
    "updatedAt": "2020-05-31T17:48:27.618Z",

Manually invoke an immediate optimization for a unidirectional tunnel

If you see that an MPLS LSP (either unidirectional or co-routed/bidirectional) could be more efficiently routed, you can use the REST API to have Navigator MC immediately move the LSP to a more optimal route based on the current topology so that it uses a minimum of resources.

This operation will fail if executed on an LSP that has been configured as "Never optimize".

Performing an immediate optimization consists of three steps:

  1. Retrieve the MplsOperationContainer resource ID.

  2. Execute the tunnel group reoptimization.

  3. Verify the status of reoptimize operation.

Retrieve the resource ID

Retrieve the MplsOperationContainer resource ID using the following API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

Managing Fast Rerouting (FRR) profiles

An MPLS Fast Reroute (FRR) profile supports the local repair of a dynamic, unidirectional LSP following a failure in the LSP’s active path. Fast Reroute mechanisms enable the rapid re-direction of traffic from the failed active path onto a backup path.

Navigator MC supports the creation, editing, and deletion of FRR profiles on SAOS 6.x and 8700 devices using the REST API.

This topic describes using the REST API to:

  • create an FRR profile

  • edit an FRR profile

  • delete an FRR profile

Creating an FRR profile

To create an FRR profile, use the Configuration Management (configmgmt) API. As part of the API call to create the profile, provide the values described in the table below.

Attribute Data type Supported values

frrProfileName

string

The FRR Profile name can consist of 1 to 31 characters, excluding the following: !%,?*

setupPriority

integer

A value from 0 to 7

holdPriority

integer

A value from 0 to 7

hopLimit

integer

A value from 0 to 255

bandwidth

integer

A value from 1000 to 1000000

bwProtection

string

"yes" or "no"

nodeProtection

string

"yes" or "no"

protectionMethod

string

"detour" or "facility"

colourGroupIncludeAny

integer

A value from 0 to 31

colourGroupIncludeAll

integer

A value from 0 to 31

colourGroupExcludeAny

integer

A value from 0 to 31

Sample request:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2020-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "frrProfileConfig",
          "inputs": [
           {
             "data": [
               {
                 "attributes": {
                   "action": "create",
                   "frrProfileName": "fr_test1",
                   "setupPriority": 3,
                    "holdPriority": 4,
                    "hopLimit": 100,
                    "bandwidth": 1000,
                    "bwProtection": "yes",
                    "nodeProtection": "yes",
                    "protectionMethod": "detour",
                    "colourGroupIncludeAny": 10,
                    "colourGroupIncludeAll": 11,
                    "colourGroupExcludeAny": 12
                 }
               }
             ]
           }
         ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}",
        "ipAddress": "{{NE_IP_ADDRESS}}",
        "neType": "{{NE_TYPE}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}
Editing an FRR profile

Edit an FRR profile using the Configuration Management (configmgmt) API.

The action in this case is "update", and you must provide the values to configure the FRR profile including the new values you are setting.

                   "setupPriority": 3,
                    "holdPriority": 4,
                    "hopLimit": 100,
                    "bandwidth": 1000,

                    "protectionMethod": "detour",
                    "colourGroupIncludeAny": 10,

          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",

Status notifications for tunnel creation, modification, and deletion using the API

Navigator MC generates status messages regarding its progress when creating, deleting, or modifying MPLS tunnels. If you subscribe to these Navigator MC messages using a web socket connection (Kafka Comet), you will receive status messages and can check that list to see the latest status of your request.

Below you can see the status messages that Navigator MC generates during service provisioning, creation, or deletion, and elements of those messages that indicate the operation’s success failure.

Note: Navigator MC supports E-Line service provisioning using the API that includes an instruction to automatically create any dynamic MPLS tunnels the service requires. This status notification capabiity does not yet support such automatic tunnel creation, so it is not yet possible to check the status of automatically created tunnels.

This topic describes Navigator MC’s status messages in the following cases:

  • Tunnel provisioning

  • Tunnel modification

  • Tunnel Deletion

Tunnel provisioning

When provisioning a new MPLS tunnel, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to the market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" using Kafka Comet.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Facade Creation Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade"

  • Resource id is MplsTunnelIntentFacade Id

  • Resource Orch State is "failed "

Facade Creation Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntentFacade"

  • Resource id is MplsTunnelIntentFacade Id

  • Resource Orch State is "active"

Relationship Creation Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is RelationShipCreated

  • relationshipTypeId is "ifd.v6.relationshipTypes.FcHasFacade"

  • relationship.sourceId is "MplsTunnelIntentFacade Id"

  • Resource Orch State is "failed "

Relationship Creation Success

  • The Kafka message event type is RelationShipCreated

  • relationshipTypeId is "ifd.v6.relationshipTypes.FcHasFacade"

  • relationship.sourceId is "MplsTunnelIntentFacade Id"

  • Resource Orch State is "active"

Tunnel Provisioning Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntent"

  • Resource id is MplsTunnelIntent Id

  • lastOperationStatus is "failed "

Tunnel Provisioning Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceUpdated"

  • Resource Type Id is "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.MplsTunnelIntent"

  • Resource id is MplsTunnelIntent Id

  • Deployment State is "COMPLETE_FULLY_READY"

  • LifeCyclePhase is "ASSURING"
Tunnel modification

When modifying an existing MPLS tunnel, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" using Kafka Comet.

When you issue the API call for the tunnel edit operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "TunnelEditOperation Id". Use that ID to identify a particular edit operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Tunnel Edit Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is " TunnelEditOperation Id"

  • Interface is "Modify"

  • Operation State is "failed"

Tunnel Edit Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is " TunnelEditOperation Id"

  • Interface is "Modify"

  • Operation State is "successful"
Tunnel deletion

When deleting an MPLS tunnel, Navigator MC issues status messages as described below.

To receive these messages, subscribe to market topic "com.cyaninc.bp.market" via kafka comet.

When you issue the API call for the tunnel deletion operation, Navigator MC will return a unique "TunnelDeleteOperation Id". Use that ID to identify a particular deletion operation.

This case is associated with these messages and statuses

Tunnel Deletion Failure

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is " TunnelDeleteOperation Id"

  • Interface is "manageService"

  • Operation State is "failed "

Tunnel Deletion Success

  • The Kafka message event type is "com.cyaninc.bp.market.ResourceOperationUpdated"

  • Operation Id is " TunnelDeleteOperation Id"

  • Interface is "manageService"

  • Operation State is "successful"

Enable or disable automatic synchronization after tunnel events

Navigator MC’s Global Configuration Service (GCS) allows you to configure certain properties that will modify Navigator MC’s behavior. You can configure these properties using a GCS API call:

PUT {BP-SERVER}/gcs/api/v1/config

One such property, called "tunnelResyncEventKey", controls whether Navigator MC will resynchronize an MPLS tunnel in response to an event on that tunnel.

By default, this property is disabled (its value is set to "false"). You can enable this property by settings its value to "true" using the GCS configuration API call shown above.

When the tunnelResyncEventKey property is enabled, any tunnel state change event will trigger a tunnel resynchronization so that Navigator MC adopts the associated topology change.

The tunnelResyncEventKey property has the following attributes:

 {
    "application": "l2",
    "instance": "-",
    "name": "tunnelResyncEventKey",
    "title": "L2 Tunnel Resync Events",
    "description": "Generate Tunnel Resync events on Tunnel State Change.",
    "value": "true",
    "default": "false",
    "key": "l2/-/tunnelResyncEventKey"
  }
Considerations when configuring the tunnelResyncEventKey property

When a network condition causes a tunnel’s state to fluctuate rapidly, enabling this property can flood Navigator MC with state message and trigger resynch events more rapidly than the system can respond.

If a tunnel is unstable for any reason, you should disable the tunnelResyncEventKey property until the condition is resolved.

You can use the REST API to update Navigator MC with the latest data about a G.8032 Ring from the network.

Create a G.8032 Ring

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve G.8032 Ring facade product ID

  • Create a G.8032 Ring facade

  • Retrieve the status of G.8032 Ring creation

Retrieve G.8032 Ring facade product ID

To retrieve G.8032 Ring facade product ID, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products

Sample response:

For a sample response, see Retrieve L2 service intent facade product ID.

In the response, note the ifd.v6.resourceTypes.G8032RingFacade. Use this ID as the “product Id” in Create a G.8032 Ring facade.

Create a G.8032 Ring facade

To create a G.8032 Ring facade, use the Market API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

Specify the productId, which is obtained from the response of Retrieve G.8032 Ring facade product ID.

Sample facade request:

{
  "productId": "5f7caf15-262a-4049-aac4-228a3e992a47",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "endNE": {
        "name": "3938_0054",
        "westPort": {
          "location": {
            "port": "19"
          }
        }
      },
      "intermediateNEs": [
        {
          "eastPort": {
            "location": {
              "port": "18"
            }
          },
          "name": "3938_0056",
          "westPort": {
            "location": {
              "port": "20"
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "eastPort": {
            "location": {
              "port": "19"
            }
          },
          "name": "3938_0055",
          "westPort": {
            "location": {
              "port": "18"
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      "startNE": {
        "name": "3938_0054",
        "eastPort": {
          "location": {
            "port": "20"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "interactive_mode": "false",
    "ringAttributes": {
      "rapsVid": "11",
      "revertive": true,
      "partial": false,
      "ringId": "11",
      "rplOwner": [
        {
          "name": "3938_0054",
          "port": {
            "location": {
              "port": "19"
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      "virtualRingName": "K-LR1-VR1",
      "holdOffTime": "0",
      "guardTime": "500",
      "logicalRingName": "K-LR1",
      "ringType": "majorRing",
      "waitToRestore": "5",
      "reuseLR": false
    }
  },
  "discovered": false
}

A list of parameters and related descriptions.

Table 26. Parameters and description
Parameter Description

productId

The G.8032 facade ID from the API. (Retrieved in Retrieve G8032 Ring facade product ID)

ringId

This is a numeric identifier for the logical ring.

logicalRingName

The Logical Ring name of the provisioned G.8032 Ring.

  • The LR name cannot include any spaces.

  • The following special characters are not allowed:

    • ,

    • !

    • %

    • ?

    • *

    • \

    • ”

ringType

majorRing/subRing. This defines whether the ring is Major or Sub.

partial

true/false. This defines whether the ring is Complete or Partial. A partial ring can carry traffic, but does not yet offer the protection afforded by a complete ring.

virtualRingName

The Virtual Ring name of the provisioned G.8032 Ring.

  • The VR name cannot include any spaces.

  • The following special characters are not allowed:

    • ,

    • !

    • %

    • ?

    • *

    • \

    • ”

rapsVid

The ID of the VLAN that is used for Ring Automatic Protection Switching (R-APS) messaging for this ring. This is configured on a Virtual Ring.

  • Virtual rings can be created on logical rings that share the same ring-id if the raps-vid for the virtual rings are different.

  • Virtual rings with the same raps-vid can be created on different logical rings as long as the logical rings do not have the same ring-id.

rplOwner

RPL owner information.

Network Element name and location object to be provided. For reference, see above sample facade request.

  • The RPL Network Element should be one among which are selected in G.8032 Ring Path.

  • The RPL port should only among the ports which are selected for the above selected RPL Network Element in the G.8032 Ring Path.

  • Shared ports for Sub-ring should not be selected in the RPL port.

revertive

true/false. Indicates whether the ring will automatically revert to its original configuration once the issue that triggered a protection switch has been resolved. This is configured on a VR.

  • true: After a failure condition is cleared, the traffic channel unblocks the ports for the failed link and reverts to the configured RPL.

  • false: After a failure condition is cleared, the traffic channel continues to use the previously-failed node as the channel block, and traffic continues over the configured RPL. If a second failure occurs, the recovered link will unblock its ports.

guardTime

The period that the node will wait before acting on R-APS State and Status request messages, in order to prevent the creation of closed loops.

  • This should be configured in 10ms steps.

holdOffTime

When an interruption occurs, this is the period (if any) that must elapse before service is switched to the protection route over the ring.

  • This should be configured in 100ms steps.

waitToRestore

Once an interruption has been resolved, this is the period (if any) that must elapse before traffic is restored to the original path over the ring.

reuseLR

true/false. True if virtual ring is created over existing logical ring. The path needs to be of the existing LR according to provided ringType and partial attribute.

It will be the responsibility of the user integrating through REST to provide a valid and correct input as done by Navigator MC UI. The BPO-IFD wouldn’t validate or do any sanity checks for this case. If the provided input is invalid, then the desired outcome is undefined.

startNE

Starting Network Element details like Network Element name and location

Location for different config are as below:

  • Major Complete requires: eastPort

  • Major Incomplete requires: disconnectedPort and connectedPort

  • Sub Complete requires: sharedPort and terminatingPort

  • Sub Incomplete requires: sharedPort and terminatingPort

intermediateNEs

List of intermediate Network Elements. Each entry should have Network Element name and location

Requires: westPort and eastPort

endNE

Ending Network Element details like Network Element name and location

Location for different config are as below:

  • Major Complete requires: westPort

  • Major Incomplete requires: connectedPort and disconnectedPort

  • Sub Complete requires: terminatingPort and sharedPort

  • Sub Incomplete requires: connectedPort and disconnectedPort
For 8700/8180/6500-Packet Fabric, the location should contain shelf, slot, eqptGrp as applicable on different devices. Consider the following example for 6500 Packet-Fabric, 6500 EMOTR:
"location": {

"eqptGrp": "{EQPT_GRP}",
“shelf” : "{SHELF}",
“slot”: “{SLOT}”,
"port": "{PORT}"
}

When built on LAG, lagName should also be provided.

Considerations & Limitations

  • Enabling/Disabling of RSTP/MSTP protocols on ring ports is via Config-Mgmt scripts.

  • G.8032 OAM provisioning is not supported. It is only available via Config-Mgmt scripts.

  • G.8032 Ring provisioning between the shelves of a TIDc node is not supported.

  • G.8032 Ring provisioning using semi-explicit path is not supported.

  • CRUD operations on G.8032 Ring are best effort. No rollback support is provided.

  • Provisioning of single node Major-Incomplete and Sub-Incomplete is not supported. Promotion of such rings is also not supported.

  • 8180 and SAOS 10x devices doesn’t support sub-rings.

Modify a G.8032 Ring

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to modify the following attributes of a G.8032 Ring:

  • revertive

In the sample API calls below:

  • BP_SERVER is the Navigator MC server host name or IP address

  • FACADE_ID is the G.8032 Ring facade ID

Edit revertive

Use the Market API to edit a G.8032 ring’s revertive attribute.

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{FACADE_ID}/operations

Sample POST body

{
  "inputs": {
    "resource_properties_jsonpatch": [
      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/ringAttributes/revertive",
        "value": false
      }
    ]
  },
  "interface": "modify"
}

Parse the Operation OID, and use that value to retrieve the operation result. In the above sample, the OID is: 5f7db77c-1bf3-4884-844e-54652df0f4a1.

Sample POST result

{
  "id": "5f7db77c-1bf3-4884-844e-54652df0f4a1",

      {
        "op": "replace",
        "path": "/properties/ringAttributes/revertive",
        "value": false
      }
    ]
  },

To see whether the operation has succeeded or failed, use the OID to retrieve the operation result:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{FACADE_ID}/operations/{OID}

Editing of LR attributes is not supported.
Browser refresh will be required to see the updated data.

Delete a G.8032 Ring

Considerations

  1. Navigator MC will perform a best-effort cleanup of the G.8032 Ring configuration during undeploy/delete. A failure to delete the ring configuration on one NE will not prevent deletion of the same ring configuration on the rest of the NEs.

  2. If a G.8032 Ring deployment has failed (it is in an INCOMPLETE_DEPLOYMENT state), then trying delete the ring will do the following:

    • Navigator MC will attempt a best-effort cleanup of all devices, including partial configurations on NEs for which deployment failed.

    • All resources (facade, intent, expectations) will be deleted even if there are failures during undeployment.

  3. If the G.8032 Ring was deployed properly, attempting to delete the ring will do the following:

    • Navigator MC will attempt a best-effort cleanup of all devices.

    • If deletion fails on a device, then the resources (facade, intent, expectations) will not be deleted. You will still see the ring in an INCOMPLETE_UNDEPLOYMENT state.

To delete a G.8032 Ring, begin by obtaining a Managed Container resource:

Retrieve an inventory of G.8032 Rings in the network

Navigator MC can discover G.8032 rings in the managed network and add them to its network inventory. Navigator MC can discover rings that use the following NE types:

  • Devices using SAOS 6.15+:

    • 3903/4, 3905, 3906mvi

    • 3911, 3916

    • 3920, 3926, 3928

    • 3930/1, 3932, 3938

    • 3940, 3942

    • 3960

    • 5142, 5150, 5160

  • Devices using SAOS 8.4+:

    • 5170

    • 8700

  • Devices using SAOS 10.4+:

    • 8180

  • Devices using SAOS 10.7.1+:

    • 3924, 3926, 3928

    • 3948

    • 5144, 5162, 5170, 5171

    • 5130, 5131, 5132, 5164, 5166, 5168

    • 8110, 8112, 8114

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve a list of G.8032 rings from the inventory.

      }

You can further narrow the set of returned rings based on completeness (specifying either complete or partial rings, respectively) by using one of the following calls:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?ringType=major&ringCompleteness=complete

or

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?ringType=major&ringCompleteness=partial

Similarly, you can retrieve a list of subrings from the network using the following API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?ringType=subring

Perform G.8032 Ring operations

User can perform different Ring operations like:

  • Force switch/clear

  • Set/Unset RPL

  • Add/Delete Node

As part of the switch/clear operation:

  • User can switch traffic without specifying the desired outcome, in which case Navigator MC will switch traffic away from the currently active ring link.

  • User can specify the desire to switch, and the designated ring link, in which case Navigator MC will ensure that the switch operation is performed if required.

As part of the set/unset RPL operation:

  • User can designate the configured channel block to prevent traffic loop.

  • User can also unset the configured channel block and set a different channel block.

As part of the add/delete node operation:

  • User can add a ring node to an existing G.8032 ring.

  • User can delete the ring node from an existing G.8032 ring.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve the G8032OperationContainer resource ID

  • Execute the G.8032 Ring operation

  • Execute the G.8032 Service correct operation on G.8032

  • Execute Add/Delete node operation on G.8032 ring

  • Retrieve the status of the G.8032 Ring operation

Retrieve the G8032OperationContainer resource ID

To retrieve the G8032OperationContainer resource ID, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.G8032OperationContainer

Sample response:

In the response, you can find the list of G8032OperationContainer resources with size=1.

Execute the G.8032 Ring operation

To execute the G.8032 Ring operation, use the Market API.

Request = POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "switch",
  "inputs": {
    "freId": "1343372878405190553",
    "tpeId":"32dae257-5e17-3051-b278-0374db9f6386::TPE_18_CTPServerToClient_G8032_lr100"
  }
}

A list of parameters and related descriptions follows.

Table 27. Parameters and description
Parameter Description

interface

switch, clear, setRPL and unsetRPL are the valid values for this operation.

inputs

Input data for the G.8032 Ring operation.

freId

G.8032 Ring fre ID.

tpeId

Nodal Ring link tpe ID.

Sample response:

{
  "id": "5956d1d6-d0e1-45d7-a636-587815eb9736",

  },
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "requested",
  "reason": "",
  "createdAt": "2020-09-30T22:33:58.889Z",

  "resourceStateConstraints": {}
}
The id in the response (above) is the G.8032 Ring operation id.

Use this id to retrieve the status of the G.8032 Ring operation.

Retrieve the status of the G.8032 Ring operation

As part of this call:

  • RID is the G8032OperationContainer resource ID used as part of executing the G.8032 Ring operation.

  • OID is the operation ID generated as part of G.8032 Ring operation.

To retrieve the status of the G.8032 Ring operation, use the Market API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

Sample response:

{
  "id": "5956d1d6-d0e1-45d7-a636-587815eb9736",
  "resourceId": "5955a92d-1f6a-4b41-aa36-8019be2dfd84",

    "freId": "1343372878405190553",
    "tpeId":"32dae257-5e17-3051-b278-0374db9f6386::TPE_18_CTPServerToClient_G8032_lr100"
  },
  "outputs": {},
  "state": "successful",
  "reason": "",
  "createdAt": "2020-09-30T22:33:58.889Z",
  "updatedAt": "2020-09-30T22:34:04.846Z",
  "resourceStateConstraints": {}
}

A list of parameters and related descriptions follows.

Table 30. Parameters and description
Parameter Description

id

Operation ID.

state

Values can be:

  • successful

  • failed

  • aborted
Browser refresh will be required to see the updated data.
Considerations when configuring the tunnelResyncEventKey property

When a network condition causes a tunnel’s state to fluctuate rapidly, enabling this property can flood Navigator MC with state message and trigger resynch events more rapidly than the system can respond. If a tunnel is unstable for any reason, you should disable the tunnelResyncEventKey property until the condition is resolved.

Retrieve an inventory of FlexE groups in the network

Navigator MC can discover FlexE groups in the managed network. Navigator MC can discover FlexE groups that use the following NE types:

  • Devices using SAOS 10.5.1 or above:

    • 5164

    • 5166

    • 5130

    • 5168

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve a list of FlexE groups from the inventory.

Retrieving FlexE groups from the network

Use the following API request (in this case, to return a list of all FlexE groups):

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/search/fres?serviceClass=FlexeGroup

Sample response:

Filtered FlexE groups could be retrieved on the basis of

  • completeness

  • misconfigured

using below REST APIs

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?serviceClass=FlexeGroup&completeness=partial

or

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?serviceClass=FlexeGroup&completeness=complete

or

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?serviceClass=FlexeGroup&misconfigured=true

or

GET {BP_SERVER}/nsi/api/v2/search/fres?serviceClass=FlexeGroup&misconfigured=false

Configure Stats Collection and Y.1731 on an IP Links

You can use the REST API to configure Stats Collection and Y.1731 on an IP Link.

There are three steps to this process:

  1. Retrieving the container resource ID

  2. Execute request for configuration

  3. Retrieve the result to confirm the operation

Retrieving the container’s resource ID

Retrieve the container resource and select one of the resource IDs. For example, in the case below, the resource ID, RID is 60c72633-47b9-4887-b529-40aaff48a7f0.

Use the Market API to retrieve resource IDs.

Sample call:

{BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IPLinkOperationContainer

Sample response:

{
    "items": [{
            "id": "60c72633-47b9-4887-b529-40aaff48a7f0",
            "label": "Resource for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IPLinkOperationContainer",
            "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IPLinkOperationContainer",
            "productId": "60c725dd-4557-4d0d-8fa7-616133da647e",
            "domainId": "built-in",
            "tenantId": "70ecf7f7-ade1-4759-8b52-4ff4a042c6ba",
            "shared": false,
            "subDomainId": "7fd5144c-552f-39a3-9464-08d3b9cfb251",
            "properties": {},
            "discovered": false,
            "differences": [],
            "desiredOrchState": "active",
            "orchState": "active",
            "reason": "",
            "tags": {},
            "providerData": {
                "templateResources": {}
            },

            "createdAt": "2021-06-14T09:49:39.523Z",
            "revision": 13194139536214,
